Capítulo 1: Una nueva alumna

En el primer día de clases de la Academia Seiran, una nueva alumna llegó a la escuela. Se llamaba Rin, y tenía el cabello largo y negro, junto con ojos oscuros que parecían no tener emoción alguna. Desde el momento en que se matriculó, todos los chicos de la escuela se peleaban por ser amigos de ella o tener algo más. Entre ellos, estaban Yuuto y Shin, quienes también se interesaron en ella desde el primer momento.

Yuuto, el chico más popular de la escuela, era el primero en hacerle frente a Rin. Él quería ser su amigo, pero ella era muy distante y fría con él. A pesar de esto, Yuuto no se rindió y siguió tratando de acercarse a ella, aunque cada vez se tornaba más difícil.

Por otro lado, Shin conocía a Rin antes de la escuela de preparatoria. Él sabe que ella no es una persona fácil de tratar, pero no puede evitar sentirse atraído por ella. Al principio, Shin intentó hacer que Yuuto se alejara de ella, pero al ver que no tuvo éxito, decidió acercarse a Rin directamente.

Capítulo 2: Amor no correspondido

Con el tiempo, Rin comenzó a sentirse un poco más cómoda con Yuuto y Shin, aunque se mantuvo fría con ellos. Uno de los días, Yuuto invita a Rin a salir y ella acepta. Durante la cita, Yuuto intenta hacer que Rin se sienta cómoda y feliz, pero sus intentos sólo la hacen sentir incómoda y más distante.

Por su parte, Shin comenzó a experimentar nuevos sentimientos hacia Rin, aunque sabía que ella no sentía lo mismo por él. Sin embargo, él sigue tratando de acercarse a ella mientras que Yuuto sigue luchando para ganarse su corazón.

Capítulo 3: Infiel

Un día, Rin decidió aceptar la propuesta de Yuuto para salir, aunque ella ya había aceptado salir con Shin ese mismo día. En el parque, Rin se encuentra con Yuuto, quien le da de regalo un hermoso collar. Ella se siente confusa y sin saber qué hacer, decide aceptarlo. Pero al mismo tiempo, Shin estaba esperando en otro lugar para encontrarse con ella, presenciando todo lo ocurrido.

Cuando Shin se entera de que ella salió con Yuuto, se siente engañado y traicionado. Él confronta a Rin y le pregunta por qué lo hizo, a lo que ella simplemente responde que no quería lastimarlo. Después de esto, Shin se siente herido y se distancia de ella.

Capítulo 4: El triángulo amoroso se complica

Con el tiempo, Rin se siente cada vez más confundida con sus sentimientos hacia Yuuto y Shin. Ella se da cuenta que empieza a sentir algo por Shin, pero sabe que ya lo ha lastimado. En este punto, tanto Yuuto como Shin empiezan a competir por el amor de Rin. Yuuto le da regalos y la invita a salir constantemente, mientras que Shin la evita y se aleja de ella.

Un día, Rin decide tomar un descanso de la presión de tener que decidir entre los dos chicos y sale con sus amigas. En la salida, se encuentra con un chico llamado Kenta, quien le muestra interés y le dice que está enamorado de ella. Aunque Rin no estaba interesada en Kenta, su presencia hace que Yuuto y Shin se pongan celosos.

Capítulo 5: La confesión

Yuuto se da cuenta que tiene sentimientos muy fuertes por Rin, y decide confesárselos. Cuando él le dice que la ama, Rin le responde que sólo lo ve como un amigo. Aunque él se siente triste, acepta su respuesta y decide alejarse de ella, pensando que tal vez así podrá superarla.

Por otro lado, Shin encuentra a Rin llorando en el jardín de la escuela, y se da cuenta que todavía tiene sentimientos por él. Él la abraza y le dice que siempre estará ahí para ella. Es entonces cuando Rin se da cuenta de que quiere estar con Shin, pero sabe que tendrá que enfrentarse a Yuuto.

Capítulo 6: La tragedia

Rin decide hablar con Yuuto y decirle que ella está enamorada de Shin. Esto provoca la ira de Yuuto, quien no puede aceptar la idea de que ella está enamorada de otra persona. En un momento de locura, él decide ir a buscar a Shin para confrontarlo.

Cuando Yuuto encuentra a Shin, se enoja y empiezan a discutir. Sin embargo, la discusión se vuelve violenta y los dos empiezan a pelear. En medio de la pelea, Yuuto saca un cuchillo y apuñala a Shin, matándolo al instante.

Rin llega al lugar justo a tiempo para ver a Shin morir en sus brazos, mientras que Yuuto huye. Rin queda desolada, sin saber qué hacer ni a quién acudir. Ella, quien pensaba que había encontrado el amor, ahora se siente sola e incapaz de superar la muerte de Shin.

Epílogo: Los recuerdos

Años después del trágico evento, Rin sigue atormentada por los recuerdos de aquel día. Aunque ella ha intentado seguir adelante con su vida, no puede olvidar a Shin ni a lo que le sucedió. Cada vez que ve algún objeto que le recuerda a él, se siente abrumada por el peso de su tristeza.

Yuuto, el causante de la tragedia, nunca fue encontrado y se presume que sigue huyendo. Rin, por otro lado, sigue asistiendo a la academia Seiran, pero ya no muestra interés en tener una relación o en interesarse por alguien más. Su corazón está vacío, lleno de dolor y pesar por la pérdida de Shin.

Biggest challenges

Most urgent communications needs

Brand imperatives

Tools to use for situation analysis

Text:
Some boys taught me to play football. This was fine sport. You thought up a new strategy for every play and whispered it to the others. You went out for a pass, fooling everyone. Best, you got to throw yourself mightily at someone's running legs. Either you brought him down or you hit the ground flat out on your chin, with your arms empty before you. It was all or nothing. If you hesitated in fear, you would miss and get hurt: you would take a hard fall while the kid got away, or you would get kicked in the face while the kid got away. But if you flung yourself wholeheartedly at the back of his knees - if you gathered and joined body and soul and pointed them diving fearlessly -- then you likely wouldn't get hurt, and you'd stop the ball. Your fate, and your team's score, depended on your concentration and courage. Nothing girls did could compare with it.
Boys welcomed me at baseball, too, for I had, through enthusi- 2
astic practice, what was weirdly known as a boy's arm. In winter, in the snow, there was neither baseball nor football, so the boys and I threw snowballs at passing cars. I got in trouble throwing snowballs, and have seldom been happier since.
On one weekday morning after Christmas, six inches of new snow had just fallen. We were standing up to our boot tops in snow on a front yard on trafficked Reynolds Street, waiting forcars. The cars traveled Reynolds Street slowly and evenly; they were targets all but wrapped in red ribbons, cream puffs. We couldn't miss.
I was seven; the boys were eight, nine, and ten. The oldest two Fahey boys were there - Mikey and Peter - polite blond boys who
lived near me on Lloyd Street, and who already had four brothers and sisters. My parents approved Mikey and Peter Fahey. Chickie McBride was there, a tough kid, and Billy Paul and Mackie Kean
too, from across Reynolds, where the boys grew up dark and furi- ous, grew up skinny, knowing, and skilled.We had all drifted from our houses that morning looking for action, and had found it here on Reynolds Street.
It was cloudy but cold. The cars' tires laid behind them on the snowy street a complex trail of beige chunks like crenellated castle walls. I had stepped on some earlier; they squeaked. We could have wished for more traffic. When a car came, we all popped it one. In
the intervals between cars we reverted to the natural solitude of children.
I started making an iceball - a perfect iceball, from perfectly 6 white snow, perfectly spherical, and squeezed perfectly translucent
os no snow remained all the way through. (The Fahey boys and I considered it unfair actually to throw an iceball at somebody, but it had been known to happen.)
I had just embarked on the iceball project when we heard tire
chains come clanking from afar. A black Buick was moving toward us down the street. We all spread out, banged together some regu- lar snowballs, tookaim, and, when the Buickdrew nigh, fired.
A soft snowball hit the driver's windshield right before the
driver's face. It made a smashed star with a hump in the middle.
Often, of course, we hit our target, but this time, t h eonly time in
all of life, the car pulled overand stopped. Its wide black door opened;
a man got out of it, running. He didn't even close thecardoor.
He ran after us, and we ran away from him, up the snowy 01 Reynolds sidewalk. At the corner, I looked back; incredibly, he was
still after us. He was in city clothes: a suit and tie, street shoes.
Any normal adult would have quit, having sprung us into flight and made his point. This man was gaining on us. He was a thin man,
all action. Al of asudden, we were running for our lives.
Wordless, we split up. We were on our turf; we could lose our- 1 selves in the neighborhood backyards, everyone for himself. I paused and considered. Everyone had vanished except Mikey Fahey, who was just rounding the corner of a yellow brick house. Poor Mikey, I trailed him. 'The driver of the Buick sensibly picked the two of us to follow. The man apparently had all day.
He chased Mikey and me around the yellow house and up a 21 backyard path we knew by heart: under a low tree, up a bank, through a hedge, down some snowy steps, and across the grocery store's delivery driveway. We smashed through a gap in another hedge, entered a scruffy backyard and ran around its back porch
and tight between houses to Edgerton Avenue; we ran across Edgerton to an alley and up our own sliding woodpile to the Halls' front yard; he kept coming. We ran up Lloyd Street and wound through mazy backyards toward the steep hilltop at Willard and
Lang.
He chased us silently, block after block. He chased us silently
13 over picket fences, through thorny hedges, between houses, around garbage cans, and across streets. Every time I glanced back, chok-
ing for breath, I expected he would have quit. He must have been
as breathless as we were. His jacket strained over his body. It was
an immense discovery, pounding into my hot head with every slid-
ing, joyous step, that this ordinary adult evidently knew what I
thought only children who trained at football knew: that you have
to fling yourself at what you're doing, you have to point yourself, forget yourself, aim, dive.
Mikey and I had nowhere to go, in our own neighborhood or out
41
of it, but away from this man who was chasing us. He impelled us forward; we compelled him to follow our route. The air was cold; every breath tore my throat. We kept running, block after block; we kept improvising, backyard after backyard, running a frantic course and choosing ti simultaneously, failing always to find small places or hard places to slow him down, and discovering always, ex- hilarated, dismayed, that only bare speed could save us - for he would never give up, this man- and we were losing speed.
He chased us through the backyard labyrinths of ten blocks be- fore he caught us by our jackets. He caught us and we all stopped.
We three stood staggering, half blinded, coughing, in an ob-
16 scure hilltop backyard: a man in his twenties, a boy, a girl. He had released our jackets, our pursuer, our captor, our hero: he knew we weren't going anywhere. We all played by the rules. Mikey and I
unzipped our jackets. I pulled off my sopping mittens. Our tracks multiplied in the backyard's new snow. We had been breaking new snow all morning. We didn't look at each other. I was cherishing my excitement. The man's lower pants legs were wet; his cuffs were full of snow, and there was a prow of snow beneath them on his shoes and socks. Some trees bordered the little flat backyard, some messy winter trees. There was no one around: a clearing in a grove, and we the only players.
It was a long time before he could speak. I had some difficulty 71 at first recalling why we were there. My lips felt swollen; Icouldn't
see out of the sides of my eyes; I kept coughing.
"You stupid kids," he began perfunctorily. 18 We listened perfunctorily indeed, if we listened at all, for the 19 chewing out was redundant, a mere formality, and beside the point.
The point was that he had chased us passionately without giving
up, and so he had caught us. Now he came down to earth. I wanted
the glory to last forever.
But how could the glory have lasted forever? We could have run 20 through every backyard in North America until we got to Panama.
But when he trapped us at the lip ofthe Panama Canal, what pre- cisely could he have done to prolong the drama ofthe chase and cap
its glory? I brooded about this for the next few years. He could only have friedMikey Fahey and me in boilingoil, say, or dismembered us piecemeal, or staked us to anthills. None of which I really wanted, and none ofwhich any adult was likely to do, even in the spirit of fun. He could only chew us out there in the Panamanian jungle, after
months or years of exalting pursuit. He could only begin, "You stupid kids," and continue in his ordinary Pittsburgh accent with his normal righteous anger and the usual common sense.
Ifin that snowy backyard the driver of the black Buick had cut 12 off our heads, Mikey's and mine, I would have died happy, for noth-
ing has required so much ofme since as being chased all over Pitts- burghin the middle of winter- running terrified, exhausted- by
this sainted, skinny, furious red-headed man who wished to have a word with us. I don't know how he found his way back to his car.

import os
import logging
from langchain.document_loaders import TextLoader
from langchain.text_splitter import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
from langchain.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain.embeddings import LlamaCppEmbeddings
import sys


def create_vector_store(input_file, model_path, persist_directory, chunk_size, chunk_overlap):
    # Load document and split into chunks
    try:
        loader = TextLoader(input_file, encoding="utf8")
        documents = loader.load()
        text_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(chunk_size=chunk_size, chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap)
        texts = text_splitter.split_documents(documents)
    except Exception as e:
        logging.error(f"Error loading and splitting documents: {str(e)}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Create embeddings
    try:
        llama = LlamaCppEmbeddings(model_path=model_path)
    except Exception as e:
        logging.error(f"Error loading LlamaCppEmbeddings model: {str(e)}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Create and persist vector store
    try:
        db = Chroma.from_documents(texts, llama, persist_directory=persist_directory)
        db.persist()
        db = None
        logging.info("Vector store created and persisted successfully.")
    except Exception as e:
        logging.error(f"Error creating and persisting vector store: {str(e)}")
        sys.exit(1)

def main():
    # Set up logging
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s")

    # Configuration
    current_directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    input_file = os.path.join(current_directory, "source_documents", "Decantment2.txt")
    model_path = os.path.join(current_directory, "Models", "ggml-model-q4_0.bin")
    persist_directory = os.path.join(current_directory, "db")

    # Prompt user for chunk_size and chunk_overlap
    chunk_size = int(input("Enter the chunk size: "))
    chunk_overlap = int(input("Enter the chunk overlap: "))

    create_vector_store(input_file, model_path, persist_directory, chunk_size, chunk_overlap)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Перефразируй «Глава 2. Этапы процесса внедрения SMM маркетинга в социальных сетях Приход в социальные сети должен быть осмысленным, спланированным, с четко поставленными задачами. Только в этом случае кампания даст ощутимый эффект. Интуитивный подход в SMM не работает и, как правило, приводит к разочаровывающим результатам. Именно поэтому необходимо заранее проанализировать все предпосылки кампании, сформировать стратегию продвижения в социальных сетях и в дальнейшем работать по четкому плану, привязанному к определенным срокам. Весь процесс можно разбить на несколько этапов: 2.1. Определение целевой аудитории Одним из важнейших этапов в разработке стратегии является определение портрета целевой аудитории. Для этого необходимо ответить на ряд вопросов: География. Где живут ваши потенциальные клиенты? Социально-демографические характеристики. Каковы пол, возраст, семейное положение, должность, образование, уровень доходов целевой аудитории? Интересы, увлечения. Что может привлечь аудиторию, на что она обращает внимание, какие другие товары и услуги аудитории нужны? 2.2. Определение ключевых задач кампании Уже говорилось о том, для чего в основном используется SMM. Надо понять, какая задача либо несколько задач наиболее актуальны именно для вашего бизнеса. От этого будут зависеть все дальнейшие действия в рамках кампании. Очень распространена ошибка, когда компания идет в социальные сети «для галочки» либо потому, что там проявляют активность конкуренты. Результатом этого оказываются пустые бессмысленные сообщества, мертвые блоги, равнодушная аудитория и, конечно же, нулевая эффективность. Любое маркетинговое действие должно быть нацеленным на определенный результат. Важно проследить, чтобы задачи, которые вы ставите перед SMM-кампанией, в итоге работали на ваши глобальные бизнес-цели. Sarah is a 12-year-old girl who has been living with Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (JIA) for two years, experiencing pain, stiffness, and swelling in both her knees (more severe in the right one) and her right ankle which affect her mobility. JIA is a long-lasting autoimmune inflammatory condition that affects the joints of children under 16 years old and is characterized by persistent inflammation lasting six weeks or more (Petty et al., 2004). Beside the physical issues, this burdensome condition also leads to psychological issues, such as depression and anxiety, compared to healthy children (Fair et al., 2019). The fear avoidance model suggests that individuals who overestimate the danger of their pain may develop “protective fear responses” (Vlaeyen et al., 2016). Unfortunately, Sarah’s physical and mental well-being caused her to avoid physical activities due to her concern that it could cause more harm to her joints. Her parents’ perception of pain also contributes to this behavior. Research indicates that only 40% of children with JIA engage in the recommended daily 60-minute of physical activity( PA)  (Niewerth et al., 2014, Bohr et al., 2015). This avoidance, in turn, leads to further physical decline, disability, and a decreased quality of life. Low bone mineral density is one of the potential side effects in this cases. All these factors: anxiety, fear of movement, pain contributed to her low physical activity. The SWASY was designed to address these aspects according to the current research on behavior changes, especially in adolescent.  

Exercise therapy considers as an important component of her management (Cavallo et al., 2017),  improving pain, mobility, and quality of life. In a across sectional study conducted on adult with JIA, they found that patient with JIA who were physical active had better health-related quality of life (HQoL) (de Oliveira et al., 2023). The adolescent period is crucial as habits developed during this time tend to persist, making it a key phase for establishing longlasting routines (McGorry et al., 2011). It is important Sarah to establish a heathy level of PA to improve quality of life and prevent further disease and health complications. In order to promote physical activity (PA) and therefore improve adherence to exercise therapy, barrier to PA need to be considered and tackled. Factors that were found to improve and encourage participation to exercise therapy amongst adolescent with JIA were knowledge of its potential benefits and parental support (Sims-Gould et al., 2018). In addition, lack of information about how to manage the disease was one of the challenging of child and their parents (Min et al., 2022).  Education was considered in the SWAY by providing information about the condition in order to change perceived beliefs and threats and the benefits of exercise.  Also, advice and skills training on how to control flare-up was included. That was one arm of the way to behavior change which difficult and complex specially with adolescents (Strömmer et al., 2020).  Parental support plays an important role toward improving physical activity for their children. That was emphasized in the SWAY in a way that Sarah’s parent can encourage her to be active and support her through rebuilding confidence and increasing self-efficacy. Therapist support 

Fear-avoidance model is described how a person responds to their pain (Asmundson et al., 2012). Sarah developed a maladaptive response to her pain- which spirals into a cycle of dependence on others and further increase disability and depression.  A robust cochrane reviews on psychological therapies for chronic pain in children and adolescents of 37 RCTs (n= 2111) shows that   cognitive behavioural treatments are effective in reducing pain intensity and disability. However, none of the included studies evaluated the effectiveness of psychological therapies for children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, which limits our ability to generalize the results. 
 Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) is based on acceptance of pain and enables a transition in life's focus from suffering to items of greater value(Bailey et al., 2010, Delprato, 2001). A randomized control trial conducted on 32 children with chronic pain due to certain pathology including arthritis, to compare the effectiveness of ACT and exposure strategies to a multidisciplinary treatment approach involving amitriptyline (Wicksell et al., 2009). The ACT group experienced significant and long-lasting improvements in various areas such as perceived functional ability, pain-related discomfort, kinesiophobia and quality of life. This concept was adopted in the SWAY for improving Sarah psychological flexibility and helping her engage in satisfying activities- which is physical activity and exercise despite her pain. However, to make this approach more age-appropriate, therefore, she can understand the concept easily, cartoons in a lay language were utilized. Another approach that was incorporated with ACT is gradual exposure therapy. It is a widely utilized behavioral approach to re-engage patient to perform feared activities. Sarah was afraid of return to dancing and stairs climbing. Sarah was introduced to these activities slowly -more details in the SWAY. In addition, these avoided activities had great value for Sarah which could improve adherence toward the therapy. Relaxation techniques was taught to Sarah to cope with the anxiety that comes up with the therapy.

Motivational interviewing (MI) is a client-centered, collaborative approach to behavior change through communication with emphases on change that elicits and reinforces by the clients (Miller and Rollnick, 2012). MI interventions will be utilize  when therapist notice a desire of change using Transtheoretical Model of Change. Given that Sarah is an adolescent who likes to have control over her life, encouraging her towards self-initiated changes would be more appealing for her (Naar and Suarez, 2021) rather than imposing external goals or pressures. Suarez and Mullins (2008)  reviewed several studies and meta-analyses to determine the efficacy of MI in improving pediatric health behaviors. The paper suggests that MI can be effective in improving pediatric health behaviors and outcomes  as a single intervention by itself, or it can be included as a supplementary component in more complex interventions (Suarez and Mullins, 2008). However, JIA was not included in any of these studies, which limits the generalizability. A meta-analysis of MI for paediatric and adolescent  by Gayes and steele (2014) suggests MI appears to be most successful when both the child and the parent participate in the MI sessions and when the practitioner shares a similar cultural background with the family (Gayes and Steele, 2014). These factors will be taken into consideration when applying MI. 
The SWAY represents Collaborative goals that are meaningful and motivating to Sarah. Exercise program was designed to work on these goals and rationales of these exercises were clear and linkage to the goals(Pritchard-Wiart et al., 2019) .  The International Classification of Functioning was utilize as a model to facilitate discussion of the linkage of the prescribed exercise with Sarah and her parent (McDougall and Wright, 2009). Exercise prescription in the SWAY were based on FITT principles, considering frequency, intensity, time and type of exercise. A systematic review and meta-analysis of 114 articles reported physical activity interventions has a small but significant improvement on psychological wellbeing in children and adolescents ( efect size 0.173, 95% confdence interval 0.106–0.239, p <0.001) (Rodriguez-Ayllon et al., 2019). The authors concluded that meeting the recommendation of physical activity (60 mins or more) was associated with significant improvement in compared to those who engaged less than 60 min. Therefore, lifestyle change is important for Sarah to promote psychological well-being which is her barrier. Monitor Sarah progress regularly was considered by using “ moving diary” which is a way to provide visual aids that help with adherence and make physical activity part of her routine. The plan of the exercise was a small steps until meeting the recommendation and achieving her goals. The SWAY included only the exercise program for the first 4 weeks.  Many Factor the affect her bone density which are low physical activity and poor diet- Low BMI of Sarah indicates poor nutrition. Wight bearing exercise is effective in increase bone density in children (Nikander et al., 2010). 

Physical therapist support and feedback is important throughout the therapy. Weekly video meetings with Sarah were arranged out to provide encouragement and provide feedback (Pritchard-Wiart et al., 2019). Diefendorf „The Religious Wars in France“ ir Stuart Carroll „Blood and Violence in Early Modern France“.
Šių knygų autoriai remiasi archyvų bei istorinių dokumentų tyrimais ir kitais pirminiais šaltiniais, siekdami atskleisti religinių karų Prancūzijoje vystymąsi, jų vidaus ir išorinius konfliktus, ir jų poveikį visuomenei, politikai ir kultūrai. Taigi, šio darbo tikslas - išanalizuoti religinių karų Prancūzijoje XVI a. antroje pusėje priežastis, eigą, ir pasekmes, naudojant svarbiausias šaltinius bei mokslinius tyrimus. import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 加载并分离数据集
(train_images, train_labels), (test_images, test_labels) = keras.datasets.mnist.load_data()

# 数据集归一化处理
train_images = train_images / 255.0
test_images = test_images / 255.0

# 模型架构
model = keras.Sequential(name="CNN_Model")
model.add(keras.layers.Reshape((28, 28, 1), input_shape=(28, 28)))
model.add(keras.layers.Conv2D(filters=32, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation="relu"))
model.add(keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))
model.add(keras.layers.Conv2D(filters=64, kernel_size=(3, 3), activation="relu"))
model.add(keras.layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)))
model.add(keras.layers.Flatten())
model.add(keras.layers.Dense(64, activation="relu"))
model.add(keras.layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax"))

# 模型编译
model.compile(optimizer="adam", loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy", metrics=["accuracy"])

# 训练模型
history = model.fit(train_images, train_labels, epochs=5, validation_data=(test_images, test_labels))

# 可视化训练过程
plt.plot(history.history["accuracy"], label="accuracy")
plt.plot(history.history["val_accuracy"], label="val_accuracy")
plt.xlabel("Epoch")
plt.ylabel("Accuracy")
plt.legend()
plt.show()

The doctor arrived to tend to our wounds, and Mark looked a little apprehensive. Sensing his fear, I reached out and held his small hand tightly, offering him comfort. Once the doctor was done, and gone, Mark eagerly took my hand and led me to his room. "Let's watch a superhero movie together, Rose!" he exclaimed, his eyes shining with excitement. I couldn't resist his enthusiasm, so I agreed, settling down beside him on his cozy bed.
As the movie played, Mark couldn't contain his excitement, pointing at the screen and exclaiming, “Did you see that, Rose? The superhero just saved the day! Like you saved the day. I can be in your team, we can fight off bad people together. We're like a team, right?”
I nodded, munching on the popcorn. “Absolutely, Mark! We make a great team. And you know what? You're my favorite superhero.”
Mark beamed with pride, his cheeks flushed with excitement. “You're my favorite too, Rose!”
The room echoed with laughter and exclamations as we cheered on the hero's adventures. We shared funny comments and silly impressions, fully immersing ourselves in the fictional world of superheroes.
But as the movie drew to a close, Mark's eyelids grew heavy, and he nestled against me, his breathing steady and peaceful. I couldn't help but smile at his serene face, feeling a sense of joy and contentment wash over me.
It was in that moment, amidst the sound of Mark's soft snores, that I realized how lucky I was to have found this unexpected bond. A bond forged through laughter, popcorn, and shared moments of bravery.
And so, as I snuggled closer to Mark and closed my eyes, I couldn't help but whisper, “Thank you, Mark, for being my superhero too.”
I don’t know for how long I was gone, but I woke up with a jolt, someone is screaming and it’s not in my dream.
I stood up, I recognize this voice, it’s Linda. Linda's angry voice reverberated through the hallway, crashed on me like a lightening bolt. Confusion and unease washed over me. How did she even know I was here? I hesitantly made my way downstairs, my heart pounding with a mix of apprehension and sadness.
Linda stood there, her arms crossed and an accusatory glare fixed upon me. “Well, well, if it isn't the leech herself,” she sneered. “Taking advantage of Joseph's kindness, are we?”
I tried to find the right words to defend myself, but Linda's relentless taunts cut me off at every turn. It felt as though she was purposefully twisting the knife, exacerbating my already raw emotions.
Mark, who had been ascending the same set of stairs, sensed the tension in the air. He approached me, his eyes filled with concern. “Rose, why is Linda being mean to you? She doesn't know what she's talking about, right?”
I knelt down to his level, brushing away a tear that had escaped my eye. “Sometimes, people say hurtful things without knowing the whole story, Mark,” I explained, my voice quivering with emotion. “But it's okay. We just need to be strong and walk away from negativity.”
Mark nodded, his small hand reaching out to grasp mine. “We're superheroes, remember? We can handle anything together.”
 
A small smile tugged at the corners of my lips, grateful for Mark's unwavering support. “That's right, Mark. We're superheroes, and superheroes don't let mean words bring them down.” I said as much, but deep down, Linda's hurtful accusations and my own insecurities were gnawing at my spirit. I excused myself from Mark's presence, needing a moment to gather my thoughts and emotions.
With tears streaming down my face, I quietly slipped out of the house, the weight of Linda's words heavy on my shoulders. The cool breeze provided a welcome respite as I found solace in the embrace of the night.
Sobs racked my body as I walked aimlessly, the turmoil within me threatening to consume my every thought. I couldn't bear the thought of causing any further disruption to Joseph's life, even if it meant sacrificing my own happiness.
As I wandered through the quiet streets, a voice inside me whispered, “Rose, don't let the darkness overshadow the light that you've found in Mark and Joseph. They care about you.”
 
Taking a deep breath, I wiped away my tears and made a decision.
I cab stopped past me that took me towards my home. As the cab pulled up, a sense of trepidation washed over me when I spotted Richard standing outside, like a specter from a nightmare I couldn't shake.
My breath caught in my throat as our eyes met, and I could feel his gaze piercing through me. His smug smile sent shivers down my spine as he began to speak, his words dripping with arrogance and a twisted sense of nostalgia.
“Well, well, if it isn't Rose,” he taunted, his voice oozing with false sweetness. He followed me as I tried to get inside. “Doesn't this place bring back memories? The passion we shared, the secrets whispered within these walls.”
My stomach churned with a mix of anger and disgust, but I refused to show him any sign of weakness. I steadied myself, determined not to let his presence unravel me.
“This place is just a structure of bricks and plaster, nothing more. I've moved on from those memories, Richard,” I replied, my voice steady but laced with a hint of bitterness. “They are nothing more than ghosts of a toxic past. I suggest you leave before I take further action. I have some quiet great ideas.”
Richard's smirk wavered for a moment, his eyes narrowing in frustration. But he quickly regained his composure, attempting to regain control over the situation.
“Rose, we need to talk.”
“So, talk.” I said folding my hands.
He readjusted his posture. “Rose, we need to talk about the company, our shares, our future,” he insisted, his voice filled with a false sense of urgency. “I think we still have a conversation undue.”
I couldn't help but roll my eyes, seeing through his manipulative tactics. I refused to be ensnared by his words again.
“All the conversations I would ever had interest in sharing with you ended when your vows to share a lifetime with her began. I have no interest in your empty promises,” I retorted, my voice laced with defiance.
“I was serious when I said you'll get the company back. I meant it and my offer still stands. I won't move from here until you hear me out.”
I scoffed, this is the hardest he’s ever tried to make a conversation with me. “If you're so keen on discussing it, meet me at the café down the street, two blocks away. That's the only way I'll even consider entertaining this conversation.”
Richard's frustration was palpable, his façade slipping as he grudgingly agreed to meet at the designated location. I knew deep down that I had rattled him, that his power over me was slipping away.
Walking to the café, my mind raced with a mix of caution and determination. I couldn't help but feel a surge of gratitude for Joseph and Mark, whose unwavering support had emboldened me to confront the demons of my past. Their belief in me bolstered my strength, reminding me that I was not alone in this battle.
As I sat across from Richard in the bustling café, my gaze locked with his, my eyes mirrored the fire within my soul. I could see the flicker of uncertainty in his eyes as he realized that the person before him was no longer the one he once controlled.
“Speak your piece, Richard,” I said, my voice steady but filled with a newfound assertiveness. “But know this: I am not the same person you once manipulated. Your attempts to regain power over me will be in vain. So, if you have some real business to talk, then talk.”
Richard's mask cracked, his realization of my transformation evident in his eyes. The tables had turned, and he struggled to regain his composure. He understood, perhaps for the first time, that his toxic influence would no longer hold sway over me.
The aroma of freshly brewed coffee and the sight of donuts reminiscent of our shared after-school treats wafted through the air, a wave of bittersweet nostalgia washed over me. But any semblance of sentimentality quickly dissipated as Richard dared to bring up those precious memories.
“I'm planning on selling out the company I brought from you. It’s been a thorn on my profits for quite some time now.”
I chuckled at his shamelessness. “It wasn't yours, Richard,” I snapped, my voice trembling with anger and indignation. “The company belonged to my father, not to you. And let's set the record straight – you didn't 'buy' it from me. You manipulated and deceived your way into acquiring it. don’t be mistaken to think I don’t remember all I've suffered because of you.”
Richard's lips curled into a smug smile. “Well, it's mine now any way, Rose,” he retorted, his tone dripping with arrogance. “You shouldn't have trusted me with your shares. Now, it's time for you to face the consequences. Well, you’ve faced it for some years already.”
I clenched my fists, my nails digging into my palms. “Consequences? Selling my father's legacy for your selfish gain? You're nothing but a snake in the grass, Richard.”
“A snake you loved.”
“Shut up!!”
He leaned back, crossing his arms, and continued to mock me. “Oh, Rose, always the fiery one. But let's be practical here. The company isn't making any profit, and I'm considering selling it. You can buy it back from me for three million dollars. it’s your family’s legacy and you can keep it.”
“Three million dollars?” I scoffed, my voice laced with disbelief. “Do you think I have that kind of money lying around? do you think my family is just as vile and soulless as you to con other people out of their fortunes? You've always underestimated me, Richard, but this time, you've truly outdone yourself.”
 
A glint of mischief danced in his eyes as he leaned in, his voice dropping to a sickeningly seductive whisper. “I know you won't have that kind of money, you're too innocent. just don’t understand this cruel world. Perhaps, Rose, we can strike a different kind of deal. Three million dollars on loan from me to you, in exchange for your companionship and lively pleasures. Think about it.”
I felt a wave of revulsion surge through me, my face contorting into a mix of anger and disgust. “You're repulsive, Richard. How dare you reduce me to a mere object? I'd rather live in poverty than sell my dignity to the likes of you.”
His laughter filled the air, echoing through the café, further fueling my fury. “Take your time to think, Rose. But remember, the offer won't stand for long. Anyone would be glad to grasp onto such an offer. And who knows, we could have some unforgettably steamy experiences together. You, me and Isa.”
That was the breaking point. Rage consumed me like a wildfire, blazing through every fibre of my being. Without a second thought, my hand propelled the cup of coffee towards him, the hot liquid splattering across his face and staining his suit. The café fell silent as everyone turned their attention to the spectacle unfolding before them.
Wiping the coffee from his face, Richard's expression twisted into a mix of amusement and annoyance. “You always were a wild one, Rose. But mark my words, you won't find a better offer anywhere else. The clock is ticking.”
I rose from my seat, my voice quivering with a mix of fury and determination. “I won't waste another second of my life with you, Richard. Consider our association severed, once and for all.”

Introduction to Cloud Firestore
• The course project will rely, for its backend on the Cloud
Firestore database, part of Google Firebase platform

NoSQL
• Broad term that refers to any DBMS that does not rely on the
SQL language for querying data
o NoSQL DBMSs typically provide support for many other ways to store data,
not necessarily tables made of simple tuples
• Designed for spreading over several server machines
o In order to scale both in terms of number of records and in terms of
number of concurrent users
• Scalability comes at a price: consistency is eventual
o Data is not immediately updated
o Consequence of the C,A,P theorem©G. Malnati, J. Xhembulla 2016-23 4
Types of NoSQL DBMS
• Key/Value stores
o Big distributed hash-table
o Each data item has a unique key
o Actual data is not understood by the server
o Examples: Redis, Riak
• Document stores
o Similarly to Key/Value, each data
item has a unique key
o Data is a structured document,
often represented in JSON format
o Examples: MongoDB, CouchDB©G. Malnati, J. Xhembulla 2016-23 5
Types of NoSQL DBMS
• Column data stores
o Single records represent data columns,
not data rows as in relational DBs
o This approach simplifies data aggregation
o Examples: Cassandra, Hbase
• Graph stores
o Data is organized in graphs, using
nodes and links
o Examples: Neo4J, HyperGraphDB,
JanusGraph©G. Malnati, J. Xhembulla 2016-23 6
Cloud Firestore architecture
• Schema-less document store
o Data is organized in collections and documents
• Every collection has a name
o A collection may contain zero or more documents
• A document consists of a JSON data structure
o Having textual keys and boolean, numerical, textual, temporal, geographical
values
o Values can also consist of list of values, sub-objects (maps), or references to
other objects (caution!)
o Documents can contain sub-collection, too
o A document is limited to 1MB in size, whatever its internal structure
• Every document has a ID
o Assigned by the system or by the programmer
o ID is unique within the collection where the document is stored, and is part of
its path©G. Malnati, J. Xhembulla 2016-23 7
Expressive querying
• Firestore allows to retrieve individual documents inside a
collection
o Provided their id is known
• …or to retrieve all documents of the collection that match a set
of constraints
o Queries can contain multiple filters and sorting criteria
o Thanks to indexing, query performance depends on the result set size
and not on the data set size

• Nested data in documents

Referencing data
• A document reference is a kind of URL
o As such, it can be stored in the source document in order to allow the
retrieval of the target document
• A new collection must be created to implement many-to-many
relationships
o Its documents contain references to two related parties
• Not having columns, Firestore does not support column joins

De-normalising data
• As an alternative, a data duplication may be introduced
o Products, components and suppliers can be stored in separate collections
o Each supplier can have an array field listing the set of components it

o Each component has two array fields: one listing the set of possible

• De-normalization introduces redundancy and possible conflicts
o What happens if only one side of the relationship is updated?

Отформатируй Свойства внимания: Направленность - внимание всегда направлено на что-то. Объем внимания - это число простых, не связанных друг с другом впечатлений или идей, сознаваемых ясно и отчетливо в данный момент времени. Только несколько последовательных впечатлений могут осознаваться ясно и отчетливо. Ясность — собственное свойство каждого отдельного впечатления, тогда как отчетливость — степень отличия впечатлений друг от друга. Интенсивность - насколько сильно человек сконцентрирован в данный момент времени. Распределяемость - распределять свое внимание между разными видами деятельности (решать задачи и петь, слушать лекцию и записывать) Переключаемость - это “переключение” своего внимания. Насколько быстро можно переключиться с одного объекта на другой. Устойчивость - возможность удерживать определенную степень внимания по отношению к воздействию на протяжении времени. Посмотреть ролик Фаликман: Виды и свойства внимания — Мария Фаликман Ошибки и нарушения внимания: 1. Истинное невнимание = рассеянность. Характеризуется отсутствием ясных мыслей, расплывчатостью ощущений, упадком сил и оттого — минимальным субъективным напряжением, отсутствием концентрации на чем бы то ни было и интереса к происходящему вокруг. Причинами истинного невнимания могут быть и усталость, и бессонница, и монотонная работа, и просто скука. “Дорожный гипноз” - случай истинного невнимания. Характеризуется провалом во времени. Человек не управляет ходом собственных мыслей, а в его памяти не остается ничего из происходившего в момент рассеяния внимания. Но не всегда связан с дорогой, может просто на лекции… Симптом: пустой взор (он просто сопровождать может!) 2. Мнимая рассеянность. Шахматный рейтинг ELO и корреляция IQ
Юрий Маркушин
Юрий Маркушин
30.06.2012
34,0 тыс.
31
Рубрика: Здоровье/Психология
Теги: шахматы Эло , шахматный iq , корреляция шахматного iq , интеллект iq шахматы , баллы iq и шахматы
Многих интересует, есть ли связь между шахматным рейтингом и показателем IQ. Я провел небольшое исследование информации, собрал факты и данные и решил, что сейчас самое время написать статью о корреляции показателя IQ и рейтинга ELO .

Если существует корреляция между IQ и ELO, было бы также интересно узнать, насколько она сильна. Правда ли, что сильными шахматистами могут быть только люди с высоким IQ? Все ли сильные шахматисты имеют высокий IQ? На эти и другие вопросы мы постараемся ответить в этой статье.


Прежде всего, нам нужно выяснить, что такое IQ. Это аббревиатура для коэффициента интеллекта, который представляет собой числовую оценку, полученную в результате одного или нескольких стандартизированных тестов. IQ большинства среднестатистических людей равен 100, в то время как 95% населения имеют IQ от 70 до 130. Но что на самом деле измеряют эти тесты или, по крайней мере, пытаются измерить? Это что-то называется интеллектом. Как ни странно, для этого слова нет хорошего формального определения. Многие понимают, что это значит, но лишь немногие могут дать определение.

 

 

Согласно Википедии , интеллект включает в себя способности, но не ограничивается ими:

1 . абстрактное мышление

2. понимание

3. самосознание

4. общение

5. рассуждение

6. обучение

7 . обладающий эмоциональными знаниями

8. сохранение

9. планирование

10. решение проблем

Опять же, это не полный список, а лишь некоторые характеристики классической модели интеллекта. Какие из этих 10 способностей необходимы для успеха в игре в шахматы?

Абстрактное мышление определенно необходимо для игры в шахматы, шахматные фигуры можно визуализировать с точки зрения их относительной ценности пешки и стрелок, представляющих способность двигаться.

Понимание определяется как знание объекта и умение с ним обращаться. Это также определенно необходимо в игре в шахматы. Например, все шахматисты знают, что шахматный конь (объект) может двигаться L-образно и перепрыгивать фигуры (поведение), единственный способ остановить угрозу фигурой коня - это взять коня (решение проблемы).

Самосознание — это способность различать себя и других: «Я мыслю, следовательно, я существую как вещь, которая думает». Он не имеет прямого отношения к процессу мышления в шахматах, но присущ всем людям и даже некоторым животным, таким как обезьяны и слоны. Я не уверен, какими могут быть показатели IQ или рейтинги ELO слонов, но, согласно этому списку, они определенно обладают некоторым интеллектом.

Общение технически не нужно, чтобы хорошо играть в шахматы. Однако очень трудно или почти невозможно стать хорошим шахматистом, не общаясь с другими, кто играет в шахматы. Поскольку чтение шахматной книги, получение знаний из шахматной базы данных или изучение эндшпиля на TheChessWorld.com — это форма визуального общения, это абсолютно необходимо для успеха в шахматах. Позвольте мне взять это обратно, способность к общению необходима, чтобы быть сильным шахматистом.

Рассуждение — это способность человека придавать смысл вещам, устанавливать и проверять факты. Это, безусловно, одна из очень важных способностей для шахматистов, поскольку они используют ее для самых разных целей, сидя за шахматной доской. Анализ шахматных позиций — один из примеров, когда в шахматах решающую роль играет рассуждение.

Обучение – это приобретение новых или модификация существующих знаний или навыков. В шахматах и ​​то, и другое. Учиться играть дебюты — значит приобретать новые знания. Оттачивание тактики путем решения шахматных задач — это модификация имеющегося мастерства. Умение учиться абсолютно необходимо для шахматиста.

Наличие эмоциональных знаний также играет определенную роль в шахматах. Например, если человек ненавидит проигрывать в шахматы, мы используем этот негативный стимул и предварительное эмоциональное знание, чтобы избежать этого в будущем. Он может либо учиться и лучше играть в шахматы, либо перестать играть в шахматы, чтобы избежать проигрышей.

Удержание абсолютно важно для шахмат. Хорошая память может дать шахматисту огромное преимущество перед другим игроком. Способность запоминать шахматные партии, позиции, классические эндшпили и дебюты необходима для игры в шахматы высокого уровня.

Планирование — ключ к любой шахматной игре. В шахматах главное планирование и стратегия. Чтобы переиграть соперника, нужно придумать план, подходящий для конкретной позиции, а также хорошо его реализовать. Википедия определяет стратегию как план, направленный на получение (или подготовку к получению) преимущества над противниками или наилучшее использование возникающих возможностей. Это прекрасно применимо к шахматам, поскольку мы хотим использовать все доступные ресурсы на шахматной доске, чтобы действительно выиграть игру.

Решение задач – это то, что шахматист делает буквально во время каждого хода во время игры в шахматы. Ему предстоит принимать множество решений на протяжении всей игры и придумывать способы защиты и атаки, развивать фигуры и управлять временем. Тактика также на 100% решает проблемы.

Как видно из списка выше, 9 из 10 характеристик интеллекта также очень важны для игры в шахматы. Отсюда можно сделать вывод, что для того, чтобы быть сильным шахматистом, нужно обладать уровнем интеллекта выше среднего. Но значит ли это, что хороший шахматист должен иметь высокий показатель IQ? Все зависит от того, насколько точно и надежно IQ-тест может измерить интеллектуальные способности человека. Многие ученые спорят о том, является ли IQ-тест достаточно точным показателем интеллекта, поскольку он оценивает IQ на основе множества ложных предположений. Некоторые ученые полностью оспаривают идею IQ, поскольку считают, что невозможно оценить свой интеллект, основываясь исключительно на стандартных тестах.

На мой взгляд, я считаю, что тест IQ не является точным показателем интеллекта, это всего лишь мера того, насколько хорошо человек может пройти конкретный тест (навык, которому можно научиться). Поэтому утверждение о том, что человек с высоким IQ обязательно будет сильным шахматистом или что человек с высоким ELO будет иметь высокий показатель IQ, некорректно.

Вот таблица IQ из книги Левитта «Гений в шахматах »:

IQ 185 Высокий естественный нейрокинестетический контроль; высокая любознательность; анти мелочи; в спешке, спешу

IQ 180 Новое творение

IQ 175 Знает умного (и правильного!)

IQ 165 Формализация; зачатки уверенности в себе; меньше скрывать

IQ 160 Интерес к логике; паранойя; второстепенное творение; признает хорошую работу; искусство; музыка

IQ 150 Тривиальная формализация

IQ 145. Ниже этого уровня, а часто и выше, везде обнаруживается рабство условностей.

Левитт утверждает, что распределение IQ населения выглядит следующим образом (100 - это средний IQ):

16% свыше 115
2,3% свыше 130
0,13% свыше 145
0,003% свыше 160

Левитт выводит уравнение, связывающее показатель ELO и IQ:

ЭЛО ~ (10 х IQ) + 1000

Символ «~» означает, что «учитывая многолетние усилия, они будут приблизительно равны».

Если мы подставим 100 IQ (средний показатель IQ) в уравнение, мы получим 2000 ELO, а это означает, что среднестатистический человек должен иметь рейтинг 2000. Однако некоторые шахматисты (фактически большинство шахматистов) играют всю свою жизнь и никогда не достигают даже 1700, благодаря чему отметка 2000 года попадает в число 4-5% лучших шахматистов планеты. Так что, возможно, этот член в уравнении «1000» нужно несколько уменьшить.

Вот (оценочный) список показателей IQ известных шахматистов:

Гарри Каспаров Шахматист Россия 190
Бобби Фишер Шахматист США 187
Дональд Бирн Шахматист Ирландия 170
Джудит Полгар Шахматист Венгрия 170
Роберт Бирн Шахматист Ирландия 170

Международная команда психологов попыталась измерить показатель IQ Гарри Каспарова и после многих утомительных тестов пришла к выводу, что IQ Каспарова составляет 135 баллов, что относит его к категории «умеренно одаренных». По уравнению Левитта ЭЛО Каспарова должно быть 2350, а не 2850, как это есть на самом деле.

Выводы:

1. Существует прямая зависимость между уровнем интеллекта и шахматными способностями.

2. Тесты IQ не являются точным показателем уровня интеллекта и поэтому не могут точно сравниваться с ELO.

3. Формула Левитта, связывающая IQ с ELO, неточна, и коэффициент «1000» следует несколько уменьшить.

Augmenter et enrichir d'arguments significatifs le texte suivant sur une page : Les logiciels de Microsoft seraient des logiciels malveillants, d'après la Free Software Foundation.
D'après la Free Software Foundation, les logiciels non libres (propriétaires) seraient très souvent des logiciels malveillants (conçus pour nuire à l'utilisateur). Les logiciels non libres sont contrôlés par leurs développeurs, ce qui les place en position de force par rapport aux utilisateurs, c'est là l'injustice fondamentale d'après la FSF. La FSF affirme que les développeurs et les fabricants exercent souvent ce pouvoir au détriment des utilisateurs qu'ils devraient servir, et que cela prend généralement la forme de fonctionnalités malveillantes. Voici l'analyse intégrale de la FSF :

Vulnérabilité induite par l'UEFI

L'UEFI rend les ordinateurs vulnérables aux menaces persistantes avancées qui sont presque impossibles à détecter une fois installées. Voici les détails techniques.

Kaspersky a découvert cet exemple par hasard, mais n'est pas en mesure de vérifier de manière générale la présence de tels rootkits dans les ordinateurs.

Les logiciels non libres ne sécurisent pas votre ordinateur, mais font le contraire : ils vous empêchent d'essayer de le sécuriser. L'UEFI est un programme non libre nécessaire au démarrage et impossible à remplacer ; il s'agit en fait d'un rootkit de bas niveau. Tout ce qu'Intel a fait pour sécuriser son pouvoir sur vous protège également les rootkits de niveau UEFI contre vous.

group <- dat[, .(n = .N, mean_PCA = mean(PCA_), sd_PCA = sd(PCA_)), by = .(age, sex)]

ages <- c()
p_values <- c()
t_values <- c()
n_female <- c()
n_male <- c()

for (age in unique(group$age)) {
  cat("age:", age, "\n")
  data_male <- c()
  data_female <- c()
  for (gender in unique(group$sex)) {
    dat <- data %>%
      filter(age == age, sex == gender) %>%
      select(PCA_) %>%
      unlist()
    cat("sex:", gender, "\n")
    cat("N:", length(dat), "\n")
    cat("Mean:", mean(dat), "\n")
    cat("Std:", sd(dat), "\n")
    if (gender == 1) {data_male <- dat} 
    else if (gender == 0) {data_female <- dat}
  }
  result <- t.test(data_male, data_female)
  t_stat <- result$statistic
  p_value <- result$p.value
  
  # Print t-test results
  cat("t:", t_stat, "\n")
  cat("p:", p_value, "\n")
  
  # Add results to respective vectors
  ages <- c(ages, age)
  t_values <- c(t_values, t_stat)
  p_values <- c(p_values, p_value)
  n_female <- c(n_female, length(data_female))
  n_male <- c(n_male, length(data_male))
}

summarize: Once you have ruled out (or addressed) serious problems like sleep apnea,
there are concrete steps that you can take to improve your sleep, or at least
improve your chances of getting good sleep.
Most important, you must create an environment for yourself that is
conducive to sleeping well. The first requirement for good sleep is darkness.
Light is the enemy of sleep, full stop. Thus, you want to make your bedroom
itself as dark as possible—installing room-darkening curtains if you live
somewhere with a lot of outdoor evening light, and removing all light sources
in the bedroom, even down to electronic equipment like TVs and cable boxes
and such. Their little pinpoint LEDs are more than bright enough to keep you
from sleeping well. Digital clocks are especially deadly, not only because of
their bright numerals but also because if you wake up and see that it’s
3:31 a.m., you might start worrying about your 7 a.m. flight and never fall
back asleep.
This is easier said than done, because it essentially amounts to evicting the
twenty-first century from your bedroom. Modern life almost systematically
destroys our ability to sleep properly, beginning with the ubiquity of electric
light. Not only does non-natural lighting interfere with our natural circadian
rhythm, but it also blocks the release of melatonin, the darkness-activated
hormone that tells our brain that it is time to fall asleep. It’s similar to the way
that the SAD interferes with satiety hormones that normally tell us that we
are full and we can stop eating.
Even worse is the relatively recent advent of LED household lighting,
which is predominantly on the blue end of the spectrum, meaning it more
resembles daylight. When our brain detects that blue light, it thinks it is
daytime and that we should be awake, so it tries to block us from falling
asleep. Therefore, you should also reduce the amount of bright, LED light
that you’re exposed to in the evening. A couple of hours before you go to bed,
begin turning off unnecessary lights in your house, gradually reducing your
light exposure from there. Also, try to swap out blue-intensive LED bulbs for
those on the warmer end of the spectrum.
The devices we stare at before bed—phones, laptops, video games—are
even worse for our sleep. Not only do they bombard us with more blue light,
but they also activate our minds in ways that impede our ability to sleep. One
large-scale survey found that the more interactive devices subjects used
during the hour before bedtime, the more difficulties they had falling asleep
and staying asleep—whereas passive devices such as TV, electronic music
players, and, best of all, books were less likely to be associated with poor
sleep. This may partially explain why watching TV before bed does not seem
to affect sleep quite as negatively as playing video games or scrolling social
media does, according to research by Michael Gradisar, a sleep researcher
and professor of psychology at Flinders University in Australia.
I am increasingly persuaded that our 24-7 addiction to screens and social
media is perhaps our most destructive habit, not only to our ability to sleep
but to our mental health in general. So I banish those from my evenings (or at
least, I try to). Turn off the computer and put away your phone at least an
hour before bedtime. Do NOT bring your laptop or phone into bed with you.
Another very important environmental factor is temperature. Many
people associate sleep with warmth, but in fact the opposite is true: One of
the signal events as we are falling asleep is that our body temperature drops
by about one degree Celsius. To help that happen, try to keep your bedroom
cool—around sixty-five degrees Fahrenheit seems to be optimal. A warm
bath before bed may actually help with this process, not only because the bath
itself is relaxing but also because when we get out of the bath and climb into
our cool bed, our core temperature drops, which signals to our brain that it is
time to fall asleep. (There are also a variety of cooling mattresses and
mattress toppers out there that could help people who like to sleep cool.)
Our internal “environment” is just as important to good sleep. The first
thing I tell my patients who are having difficulty sleeping is to cut back on
alcohol—or better yet, give it up entirely. It’s counterintuitive, because
alcohol initially acts as a sedative, so it can help us fall asleep more quickly.
But as the night wears on, alcohol turns from friend of sleep to foe, as it is
metabolized into chemicals that impair our ability to sleep. Depending on
how much we’ve had to drink, during the second half of the night we may
have a harder time entering REM sleep and be more prone to waking up and
lingering in unproductive light sleep.
The effects of alcohol on memory and cognition are apparent even in
moderate drinkers. Studies have found that young people who drink heavily
are more likely to forget even basic tasks like locking the door or mailing a
letter. Students who averaged nine drinks per week (not much, by collegiate
standards) performed worse on a word-based memory test. And, in a finding
that will surprise no one, students who drank more slept later and felt sleepier
in the daytime, as well as performing worse on tests. More alarming is the
finding that students who drank heavily two days after a bout of learning or
study forgot or failed to retain most of what they had learned.
Note that these are all findings in young people, students who are
presumably at their cognitive peak. If you extrapolate to those of us in middle
and older age, who may have a lower tolerance for alcohol and a greater
propensity to forget things, the implications are worrisome. I find that my
own threshold is two drinks in an evening: any more than that, my sleep goes
sideways, and my work performance suffers the next day, no matter how
much coffee I drink.
Coffee is not a solution to the problem of poor sleep, especially if
consumed to excess or (especially) at the wrong time. Most people think of
caffeine as a stimulant that somehow gives us energy, but actually it functions
more as a sleep blocker. It works by inhibiting the receptor for a chemical
called adenosine, which normally helps us go to sleep every night. Over the
course of the day, adenosine builds up in our brain, creating what scientists
call “sleep pressure,” or the drive to sleep. We may be tired and needing
sleep, but if we ingest caffeine it effectively takes the phone off the hook, so
our brain never gets the message.
This is obviously helpful in the morning, particularly if our “chronotype”
is telling us we should still be asleep at 6 a.m. But the half-life of caffeine in
the body is up to six hours, so if we drink a cup of coffee at noon, we will still
have half a cup’s worth of caffeine in our system at 6 p.m. Now multiply this
by the number of cups of coffee you drink in a day and work forward from
the time of your last cup. If you down one last double espresso at 3 p.m., you
will still have a full shot’s worth of caffeine in your system at 9. What you
won’t have, most likely, is much of an urge to fall asleep anytime soon.
Everyone differs in their caffeine tolerance, based on genes and other
factors (23andMe tests for one common caffeine-related gene). I’m a very fast
metabolizer, so I can handle that afternoon espresso without it affecting my
sleep too much; I can even drink coffee after dinner, and it seems to have no
impact (unlike alcohol). Someone who metabolizes caffeine slowly should
probably stop at one or two cups, before noon.
This concept of sleep pressure, our need or desire for sleep, is key to many
of our sleep tactics. We want to cultivate sleep pressure, but in the right
amounts, at the right times—not too much, not too little, and not too soon.
This is why one of the primary techniques that doctors use to treat patients
with insomnia is actually sleep restriction, limiting the hours when they are
“allowed” to sleep to six, or less. This basically makes them tired enough that
they fall asleep more easily at the end of the day, and (hopefully) their normal
sleep cycle is restored. Their sleep pressure builds up to the point where it
overwhelms whatever is causing their insomnia. But this also helps explain
why napping can be counterproductive. Taking a nap during the day, while
sometimes tempting, can also relieve too much of that sleep pressure, making
it harder to fall back asleep at night.
Another way to help cultivate sleep pressure is via exercise, particularly
sustained endurance exercise (e.g., zone 2), ideally not within two or three
hours of bedtime. My patients often find that a thirty-minute zone 2 session
can do wonders for their ability to fall asleep. Even better is exercise that
entails some exposure to sunlight (i.e., outdoors). While blue light late in the
evening can interfere with sleep, a half-hour dose of strong daylight, during
the day, helps keep our circadian cycle on track, setting us up for a good night
of sleep.
It is also important to mentally prepare ourselves for sleeping. For me,
this means avoiding anything that might create stress or anxiety, such as
reading work emails or especially checking the news. This activates the
sympathetic nervous system (the fight-or-flight one) at a time when we want
to be destressing and generally winding down. I have to force myself to step
away from the computer in the evening; that queue of emails will still be
there in the morning. If there’s a burning issue that I can’t get off my mind,
I’ll write a few lines about it, creating a plan of action for the next morning.
Another way to turn down the sympathetic nervous system and prepare the
brain for sleep is through meditation. There are several very good apps that
can help with guided meditations, including some that are focused entirely on
sleep.
The overarching point here is that a good night of sleep may depend in
part on a good day of wakefulness: one that includes exercise, some outdoor
time, sensible eating (no late-night snacking), minimal to no alcohol, proper
management of stress, and knowing where to set boundaries around work and
other life stressors.

Write the final part of the following story: I slammed the door of my car in a hurry, late to meet my friends at our favorite café. As I fumbled with my phone, I tripped on the curb and went crashing into a row of designer bikes parked outside the newly opened cafe next door.

The bikes clattered to the ground, a domino effect of destruction. I stared at the damage in horror, knowing I was in trouble. The owner of the café, a tall, handsome man with glasses, came rushing outside to see the cause of the commotion.

He quickly assessed the damage and turned to me with a stern expression. “Do you have any idea how much these bikes are worth?”

“I’m so sorry,” I stammered, “I didn’t mean to —”

“I understand it was an accident,” he interrupted, “but you still need to take responsibility for this.”

I opened my purse, praying I had enough to cover the damage. But there wasn’t even enough for one bike. The owner sighed, as if coming to a decision.

“Alright, here’s an option. I’ll agree not to press charges if you work at my café to make up for the damages.”

I hesitated, thinking of my friends waiting for me, but I knew I couldn’t pass up the opportunity to escape legal trouble.

“Deal,” I agreed quickly.

“Good. Come with me,” he said, leading me inside the strange café.

It was a cozy place, but I immediately noticed something odd. All the waiters were dressed in schoolboy uniforms, and there seemed to be an overwhelming theme of male-on-male affection displayed on the merchandise and décor.

I blinked in confusion, but I knew I couldn’t back out of our agreement.

“I take it you’re familiar with yaoi?” he asked, watching my reaction.

I blushed, “Yeah, I’ve heard of it, but I didn’t know there were cafes like this.”

“Well, you’re about to become a part of it. This is a yaoi-themed café. Are you still in?”

“I don’t have a choice, do I?” I resigned.

He smiled slightly, “Not really. But don’t worry, it’s actually quite fun.”

He led me to a small changing room and handed me a uniform.

“Put this on, and it will do the rest.”

“Do what?” I asked, but he simply left the room, urging me to change.

The moment the pinstripe uniform inched its way onto my body, I could feel a sudden warmth enveloping me. My body began to tingle and shift, and before I knew it, the transformation was complete.

I turned to the mirror and couldn’t believe my eyes. I was no longer a woman but a teenage boy with pale, refined features and an ethereal beauty I never had before.

I stumbled out of the changing room, feeling entirely disoriented.

“What’s going on?!?” I cried.

“How did this happen?”

“It’s just part of the magic of the costume,” the owner explained calmly.

“Now, let’s give you a new name. How about… Kaito?”

I froze, staring back at him with wide eyes.

“Kaito?”

He nodded. “Yes. That way, you can blend in with your coworkers and truly immerse yourself in this yaoi-themed world. Are you ready?”

I hesitated before slowly nodding. This was my life now, at least until I paid off my debt. And as strange as it was, there was an undeniable thrill in becoming an entirely different person.

“Ready,” I agreed, and as Kaito, I stepped into my new role as a waiter in this exciting, enchanting world.

As the weeks went by, I found myself becoming more and more comfortable with my new identity as Kaito. My coworkers, all lovely young men with their own mysterious stories, quickly accepted me as one of their own. The customers, too, found me endearing as a shy, innocent boy new to the world of yaoi.

Working at the café wasn’t so bad – the regulars were kind, the food was delicious, and the tips were generous. I was making a dent in the debt I owed and even started enjoying the secret that only the café owner and I shared.

One day, after a particularly busy shift, I found myself alone in the changing room, staring at my reflection. I had grown attached to the Kaito persona, and I couldn’t deny the feeling of security that came with hiding behind this façade. It was nice to be someone else, someone who didn’t have the same problems and responsibilities as my real self.

As I was in the middle of this thought, the door to the changing room opened, and the owner stepped inside.

“You seem to be adjusting well,” he observed with a small smile.

I nodded hesitantly. “Yeah, I guess I am.”

He became serious and continued, “I’ve noticed that you’re doing a great job here and that you’re making a lot of progress towards paying off your debt.”

“That’s good news, right?” I asked, unsure of whether I should be happy or not. The thought of returning to my real life sparked a feeling of dread within me.

“Yes, it is,” he replied carefully. “But I feel like it’s time for me to tell you something.”

“What’s that?” I asked curiously.

“The magic of the uniform doesn’t last forever. Once your debt is paid, the charm will wear off, and you’ll return to your former self. However,” he paused, peering into my eyes, “if you should find yourself attached to this new life, there is an option for you to remain.”

My heart raced as I considered his words. Kaito’s life was filled with fun, adventure, and an escape from reality – but was it worth giving up my old life entirely?
