How To Be Successful
I’ve observed thousands of founders and thought a lot about what it takes to make a huge amount of money or to create something important. Usually, people start off wanting the former and end up wanting the latter.

Here are 13 thoughts about how to achieve such outlier success. Everything here is easier to do once you’ve already reached a baseline degree of success (through privilege or effort) and want to put in the work to turn that into outlier success. [1] But much of it applies to anyone.

1. Compound yourself

Compounding is magic. Look for it everywhere. Exponential curves are the key to wealth generation.

A medium-sized business that grows 50% in value every year becomes huge in a very short amount of time. Few businesses in the world have true network effects and extreme scalability. But with technology, more and more will.  It’s worth a lot of effort to find them and create them.

You also want to be an exponential curve yourself—you should aim for your life to follow an ever-increasing up-and-to-the-right trajectory. It’s important to move towards a career that has a compounding effect—most careers progress fairly linearly.

You don't want to be in a career where people who have been doing it for two years can be as effective as people who have been doing it for twenty—your rate of learning should always be high. As your career progresses, each unit of work you do should generate more and more results. There are many ways to get this leverage, such as capital, technology, brand, network effects, and managing people.

It’s useful to focus on adding another zero to whatever you define as your success metric—money, status, impact on the world, or whatever. I am willing to take as much time as needed between projects to find my next thing. But I always want it to be a project that, if successful, will make the rest of my career look like a footnote.

Most people get bogged down in linear opportunities. Be willing to let small opportunities go to focus on potential step changes.

I think the biggest competitive advantage in business—either for a company or for an individual’s career—is long-term thinking with a broad view of how different systems in the world are going to come together. One of the notable aspects of compound growth is that the furthest out years are the most important. In a world where almost no one takes a truly long-term view, the market richly rewards those who do.

Trust the exponential, be patient, and be pleasantly surprised.

2. Have almost too much self-belief

Self-belief is immensely powerful. The most successful people I know believe in themselves almost to the point of delusion.

Cultivate this early. As you get more data points that your judgment is good and you can consistently deliver results, trust yourself more.

If you don’t believe in yourself, it’s hard to let yourself have contrarian ideas about the future. But this is where most value gets created.

I remember when Elon Musk took me on a tour of the SpaceX factory many years ago. He talked in detail about manufacturing every part of the rocket, but the thing that sticks in memory was the look of absolute certainty on his face when he talked about sending large rockets to Mars. I left thinking “huh, so that’s the benchmark for what conviction looks like.”

Managing your own morale—and your team’s morale—is one of the greatest challenges of most endeavors. It’s almost impossible without a lot of self-belief. And unfortunately, the more ambitious you are, the more the world will try to tear you down.  

Most highly successful people have been really right about the future at least once at a time when people thought they were wrong. If not, they would have faced much more competition.

Self-belief must be balanced with self-awareness. I used to hate criticism of any sort and actively avoided it. Now I try to always listen to it with the assumption that it’s true, and then decide if I want to act on it or not. Truth-seeking is hard and often painful, but it is what separates self-belief from self-delusion.

This balance also helps you avoid coming across as entitled and out of touch.

3. Learn to think independently

Entrepreneurship is very difficult to teach because original thinking is very difficult to teach. School is not set up to teach this—in fact, it generally rewards the opposite. So you have to cultivate it on your own.

Thinking from first principles and trying to generate new ideas is fun, and finding people to exchange them with is a great way to get better at this. The next step is to find easy, fast ways to test these ideas in the real world.

“I will fail many times, and I will be really right once” is the entrepreneurs’ way. You have to give yourself a lot of chances to get lucky.

One of the most powerful lessons to learn is that you can figure out what to do in situations that seem to have no solution. The more times you do this, the more you will believe it. Grit comes from learning you can get back up after you get knocked down.

4. Get good at “sales”

Self-belief alone is not sufficient—you also have to be able to convince other people of what you believe.

All great careers, to some degree, become sales jobs. You have to evangelize your plans to customers, prospective employees, the press, investors, etc. This requires an inspiring vision, strong communication skills, some degree of charisma, and evidence of execution ability.

Getting good at communication—particularly written communication—is an investment worth making. My best advice for communicating clearly is to first make sure your thinking is clear and then use plain, concise language.

The best way to be good at sales is to genuinely believe in what you’re selling. Selling what you truly believe in feels great, and trying to sell snake oil feels awful.

Getting good at sales is like improving at any other skill—anyone can get better at it with deliberate practice. But for some reason, perhaps because it feels distasteful, many people treat it as something unlearnable.

My other big sales tip is to show up in person whenever it’s important. When I was first starting out, I was always willing to get on a plane. It was frequently unnecessary, but three times it led to career-making turning points for me that otherwise would have gone the other way.

5. Make it easy to take risks

Most people overestimate risk and underestimate reward. Taking risks is important because it’s impossible to be right all the time—you have to try many things and adapt quickly as you learn more.

It’s often easier to take risks early in your career; you don’t have much to lose, and you potentially have a lot to gain. Once you’ve gotten yourself to a point where you have your basic obligations covered you should try to make it easy to take risks. Look for small bets you can make where you lose 1x if you’re wrong but make 100x if it works. Then make a bigger bet in that direction.

Don’t save up for too long, though. At YC, we’ve often noticed a problem with founders that have spent a lot of time working at Google or Facebook. When people get used to a comfortable life, a predictable job, and a reputation of succeeding at whatever they do, it gets very hard to leave that behind (and people have an incredible ability to always match their lifestyle to next year’s salary). Even if they do leave, the temptation to return is great. It’s easy—and human nature—to prioritize short-term gain and convenience over long-term fulfillment.  

But when you aren’t on the treadmill, you can follow your hunches and spend time on things that might turn out to be really interesting. Keeping your life cheap and flexible for as long as you can is a powerful way to do this, but obviously comes with tradeoffs.

6. Focus

Focus is a force multiplier on work.

Almost everyone I’ve ever met would be well-served by spending more time thinking about what to focus on. It is much more important to work on the right thing than it is to work many hours. Most people waste most of their time on stuff that doesn’t matter.

Once you have figured out what to do, be unstoppable about getting your small handful of priorities accomplished quickly. I have yet to meet a slow-moving person who is very successful.

7. Work hard

You can get to about the 90th percentile in your field by working either smart or hard, which is still a great accomplishment. But getting to the 99th percentile requires both—you will be competing with other very talented people who will have great ideas and be willing to work a lot.

Extreme people get extreme results. Working a lot comes with huge life trade-offs, and it’s perfectly rational to decide not to do it. But it has a lot of advantages. As in most cases, momentum compounds, and success begets success.

And it’s often really fun. One of the great joys in life is finding your purpose, excelling at it, and discovering that your impact matters to something larger than yourself. A YC founder recently expressed great surprise about how much happier and more fulfilled he was after leaving his job at a big company and working towards his maximum possible impact. Working hard at that should be celebrated.  

It’s not entirely clear to me why working hard has become a Bad Thing in certain parts of the US, but this is certainly not the case in other parts of the world—the amount of energy and drive exhibited by entrepreneurs outside of the US is quickly becoming the new benchmark.

You have to figure out how to work hard without burning out. People find their own strategies for this, but one that almost always works is to find work you like doing with people you enjoy spending a lot of time with.

I think people who pretend you can be super successful professionally without working most of the time (for some period of your life) are doing a disservice. In fact, work stamina seems to be one of the biggest predictors of long-term success.

One more thought about working hard: do it at the beginning of your career. Hard work compounds like interest, and the earlier you do it, the more time you have for the benefits to pay off. It’s also easier to work hard when you have fewer other responsibilities, which is frequently but not always the case when you’re young.

8. Be bold

I believe that it’s easier to do a hard startup than an easy startup. People want to be part of something exciting and feel that their work matters.

If you are making progress on an important problem, you will have a constant tailwind of people wanting to help you. Let yourself grow more ambitious, and don’t be afraid to work on what you really want to work on.

If everyone else is starting meme companies, and you want to start a gene-editing company, then do that and don’t second guess it.

Follow your curiosity. Things that seem exciting to you will often seem exciting to other people too.

9. Be willful

A big secret is that you can bend the world to your will a surprising percentage of the time—most people don’t even try, and just accept that things are the way that they are.

People have an enormous capacity to make things happen. A combination of self-doubt, giving up too early, and not pushing hard enough prevents most people from ever reaching anywhere near their potential.

Ask for what you want. You usually won’t get it, and often the rejection will be painful. But when this works, it works surprisingly well.

Almost always, the people who say “I am going to keep going until this works, and no matter what the challenges are I’m going to figure them out”, and mean it, go on to succeed. They are persistent long enough to give themselves a chance for luck to go their way.

Airbnb is my benchmark for this. There are so many stories they tell that I wouldn’t recommend trying to reproduce (keeping maxed-out credit cards in those nine-slot three-ring binder pages kids use for baseball cards, eating dollar store cereal for every meal, battle after battle with powerful entrenched interest, and on and on) but they managed to survive long enough for luck to go their way.

To be willful, you have to be optimistic—hopefully this is a personality trait that can be improved with practice. I have never met a very successful pessimistic person.

10. Be hard to compete with

Most people understand that companies are more valuable if they are difficult to compete with. This is important, and obviously true.

But this holds true for you as an individual as well. If what you do can be done by someone else, it eventually will be, and for less money.

The best way to become difficult to compete with is to build up leverage. For example, you can do it with personal relationships, by building a strong personal brand, or by getting good at the intersection of multiple different fields. There are many other strategies, but you have to figure out some way to do it.

Most people do whatever most people they hang out with do. This mimetic behavior is usually a mistake—if you’re doing the same thing everyone else is doing, you will not be hard to compete with.

11. Build a network

Great work requires teams. Developing a network of talented people to work with—sometimes closely, sometimes loosely—is an essential part of a great career. The size of the network of really talented people you know often becomes the limiter for what you can accomplish.

An effective way to build a network is to help people as much as you can. Doing this, over a long period of time, is what lead to most of my best career opportunities and three of my four best investments. I’m continually surprised how often something good happens to me because of something I did to help a founder ten years ago.

One of the best ways to build a network is to develop a reputation for really taking care of the people who work with you. Be overly generous with sharing the upside; it will come back to you 10x. Also, learn how to evaluate what people are great at, and put them in those roles. (This is the most important thing I have learned about management, and I haven’t read much about it.) You want to have a reputation for pushing people hard enough that they accomplish more than they thought they could, but not so hard they burn out.

Everyone is better at some things than others. Define yourself by your strengths, not your weaknesses. Acknowledge your weaknesses and figure out how to work around them, but don’t let them stop you from doing what you want to do. “I can’t do X because I’m not good at Y” is something I hear from entrepreneurs surprisingly often, and almost always reflects a lack of creativity. The best way to make up for your weaknesses is to hire complementary team members instead of just hiring people who are good at the same things you are.

A particularly valuable part of building a network is to get good at discovering undiscovered talent. Quickly spotting intelligence, drive, and creativity gets much easier with practice. The easiest way to learn is just to meet a lot of people, and keep track of who goes on to impress you and who doesn’t. Remember that you are mostly looking for rate of improvement, and don’t overvalue experience or current accomplishment.

I try to always ask myself when I meet someone new “is this person a force of nature?” It’s a pretty good heuristic for finding people who are likely to accomplish great things.

A special case of developing a network is finding someone eminent to take a bet on you, ideally early in your career. The best way to do this, no surprise, is to go out of your way to be helpful. (And remember that you have to pay this forward at some point later!)

Finally, remember to spend your time with positive people who support your ambitions.

12. You get rich by owning things

The biggest economic misunderstanding of my childhood was that people got rich from high salaries. Though there are some exceptions—entertainers for example —almost no one in the history of the Forbes list has gotten there with a salary.

You get truly rich by owning things that increase rapidly in value.

This can be a piece of a business, real estate, natural resource, intellectual property, or other similar things. But somehow or other, you need to own equity in something, instead of just selling your time. Time only scales linearly.

The best way to make things that increase rapidly in value is by making things people want at scale.

13. Be internally driven

Most people are primarily externally driven; they do what they do because they want to impress other people. This is bad for many reasons, but here are two important ones.

First, you will work on consensus ideas and on consensus career tracks.  You will care a lot—much more than you realize—if other people think you’re doing the right thing. This will probably prevent you from doing truly interesting work, and even if you do, someone else would have done it anyway.

Second, you will usually get risk calculations wrong. You’ll be very focused on keeping up with other people and not falling behind in competitive games, even in the short term.

Smart people seem to be especially at risk of such externally-driven behavior. Being aware of it helps, but only a little—you will likely have to work super-hard to not fall in the mimetic trap.

The most successful people I know are primarily internally driven; they do what they do to impress themselves and because they feel compelled to make something happen in the world. After you’ve made enough money to buy whatever you want and gotten enough social status that it stops being fun to get more, this is the only force I know of that will continue to drive you to higher levels of performance.

This is why the question of a person’s motivation is so important. It’s the first thing I try to understand about someone. The right motivations are hard to define a set of rules for, but you know it when you see it.

Jessica Livingston and Paul Graham are my benchmarks for this. YC was widely mocked for the first few years, and almost no one thought it would be a big success when they first started. But they thought it would be great for the world if it worked, and they love helping people, and they were convinced their new model was better than the existing model.

Eventually, you will define your success by performing excellent work in areas that are important to you. The sooner you can start off in that direction, the further you will be able to go. It is hard to be wildly successful at anything you aren’t obsessed with.

“In this cross-sectional study, 42 CP patients and 59 controls were recruited from either patients attending to the Department of Periodontology, Faculty of Dentistry, or from the personal patient populations of the academic faculty and postgraduate students at the Ondokuz Mayis University between June 2014 and May 2015. Ethics committee approval was received from Ondokuz Mayıs University clinical research ethics committee with decision number 2014/556-630(2013/416-447).
Individuals included in the study were informed about the purpose and content of the study and signed an informed consent form indicating they voluntarily participated in the study.”,
2. Inclusion criteria
“Individuals included were over 18 years old and willing to provide in- formed consent. In addition, they did not have any systemic diseases including cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, chronic renal failure, and hepatitis B and C, and were not using any chronic anti-inflammatory drugs. Moreover, participants who are pregnant or lactating at the time of the study or receive any periodontal treatment within the preceding six months were excluded from the study. All subjects were evaluated clinically and radiographically at the first clinical visit; periapical and panoramic radiographs were obtained from all patients to verify the clinical periodontal diagnosis and the extent of alveolar bone loss. All clinical parameters were evaluated by a single investigator (S.K). The examiner was calibrated against an expert periodontist. Calibration was validated if 90% of the recordings could be reproduced within a 1.0-mm difference (Badersten, Nilvéaus, & Egelberg, 1984). The following clinical parameters were assessed at six sites per tooth: probing pocket depth (PD); clinical attachment loss (CAL); bleeding on probing (BOP) (Ainamo & Bay, 1975); plaque index (PI) (Silness & Löe, 1964); gingi- val index (GI) (Löe & Silness, 1963); and the number of missing teeth, mobility, and furcation involvement. PD was defined as the distance between the coronal-most margin of the free gingiva to the most apical penetration of the Michigan-0 probe. CAL was defined as the distance from the cemento-enamel junction to the most apical penetration of the Michigan-O probe. The presence of supragingival plaque was recorded dichotomously during PD measurements. Bleeding on probing (BOP) within 20s was recorded dichotomously.Clinical and radiographic criteria proposed by the 1999 International World Workshop were used for diagnosis.”,
3. Control group
“Patients had no history of periodontitis, and no furcation involvement and mobility. Their PD was smaller than 3 mm.”,
4. CP group inclusion criteria
“Radiographic evidence of alveolar bone loss and at least ≥4 mm PDD in two interdental areas, not on the same tooth (Eke, Page, Wei, Thornton-Evans, & Genco, 2012).”,
5. Collection and storage of samples
“GCF samples were obtained for analyses (mainly from the maxillary premolar area for standardization). The supragingival plaque was removed without touching the gingival margin. The area was care- fully washed with water to prevent salivary contamination, the tooth was isolated with cotton rolls, and the area was dried with air for 10 s. For sampling, paper strips (Periopaper, ProFlow, Amityville, NY,USA) were carefully placed in the gingival sulcus and held there for 30 s. If the paper strips were contaminated with blood or saliva, they were discarded and replaced. The volume of each paper strip was determined with Periotron 8,000 (ProFlow, Amityville, NY, USA). The samples were placed with 50 microliters of phosphate-buffered saline (pH 7.0) in an Eppendorf tube. Two milliliters of peripheral venous blood samples were taken from each subject, using a standard venipuncture method. The sam- ples were then transferred to tubes containing 8% liquid EDTA. GCF samples were centrifuged at 1,000 × g for 10 min; blood samples were centrifuged at 3,000 × g for 10 min by a centrifuge device (Shimadzu UV160A, SNo: 28006648, Japan). The supernatants obtained from GCF and serum samples were separated for the study. The samples were mixed thoroughly with a vortex and stored at −80oC until the working day. On the working day, the samples were brought to room temperature.” .1.Determination of hBD-2 concentrations
“Serum and GCF hBD-2 concentrations were studied by the commercially available Human BioD2 ELISA Kit (Sun-Red Bio Company, Cat No. 201-12-1937, Shanghai, China), in the Ondokuz Mayıs University, Faculty of Medicine, by the Medical Biochemistry Research Laboratory. The “double-antibody sandwich” enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) procedure was used for this analysis. All working solutions were freshly prepared and stored at room temperature (25°C) until use.
Five standards were prepared with the serial dilution method using human hBD-2 standard (S1–6.4 ng/ml, S2–3.2 ng/ml, S3–1.6 ng/ml, S4–0.8 ng/ml, and S5–0.4 ng/ml). The wells were identified on the ELISA plate for blank, standards, and samples. Nothing was added to the blank well except Chromogen A, Chromogen B, and a stop solution. The same procedure used with the sample was applied to the standards. Fifty μL of standard (S1–S5) was pipetted into each well, and 40 μl + 10 μl of hBD-2 antibody was pipetted from each sample. Then, 50 μl Streptavidin–Horseradish peroxidase was added to the standards and samples and incubated at 370C for 60 min. After incubation, the plate was washed 5 times with 350 μl washing solution with the help of an automatic washer. 50 μl Chromogen A and 50 μl Chromogen B were added to all wells and incubated at 37°C for 10 min. Then, the reaction was stopped by pipetting 50 μl of stop solution. At the end of the study, absorbance at 450 nm wavelength was read by a microplate reader. Sample hBD-2 concentrations were calculated according to the standard curve generated using standard values, and the concentrations obtained were expressed in ng/ml. Kit sensitivity 0.05 ng/ml and assay range 0.1 ng/ml-10 ng/ml were given. High concentration samples were confirmed by working twice.”,
2. Statistical analysis
"Data analysis was performed using R program version 3.5.1. (R Core Team, 2019). Data are expressed as means and standard deviations (SD) or medians and interquartile ranges (IR) as appropriate. Data were analyzed for normal distribution by the Shapiro–Wilk test. A chi-square test was used for comparison of categorical variables. An independent- sample t test was used to detect the statistical significance between the two groups, based on the clinical variables obtained, such as age, probing depth, clinical attachment loss, and others. Univariable and multivariable logistic regressions were used to assess the association between the outcome (periodontal disease) with serum and GCF hBD-2 levels and other covariates. Correlation between each clinical parameter and serum and GCF hBD-2 levels was analyzed using the Spearman correlation coefficient. A p-value of <.05 was considered statistically significant. The estimated power of the test was 0.80.
3. Clinical findings
“A total of 101 participants, 59 controls and 42 patients with CP, were assessed. Of the volunteers included in the study, only 8 in the control group and only 5 in the CP group were smokers. Thirty- seven (37) females and 22 males (mean age 27.69 ± 7.78) were included in the control group, and 28 females and 14 males (mean age 42.67 ± 10.62) were included in the CP group. There was no statisti- cal difference between the groups in terms of smoking and gender distribution (p > .05). The distribution of demographic data is shown in Table 1.
Age was found to be significantly higher in the CP group (p < .001). The mean age of all participants was 33.93 (±11.68) years; the mean age of the control group was 27.69 (±7.78), and the mean age of the CP group was 42.67 (±10.62) (Table 1).”,
4. Clinical variables
“All recorded clinical parameters (BOP, CAL, PI, GI, and PD) were significantly higher in the CP group than in the control group (p < .001) (Table 2). CP was reclassified according to the modification of the new international classification of periodontitis (Tonetti, Greenwell, & Kornman, 2018). Accordingly, cases were classified as Stage II (n = 3; 7%); Stage III (n = 34; 81%); Stage IV (n = 5; 12%); and Grade B (n = 25; 60%) to C (n = 17; 40%) periodontitis. Of these, 67% of CP patients were generalized CP, and 33% were localized CP.The mean hBD-2 levels of GCF samples in the CP group were 2.77 (±0.74) ng/30 s and 2.51 (±0.54) ng/30 s in the control group. The GCF levels of the mean hBD-2 were significantly higher in the CP group compared with those in healthy controls (p = .047; Figure 1). Adjusting for potential confounders such as smoking, age, and gender did not alter this association (p = .036). Conversely, the mean hBD-2 levels of serum samples in the CP group were lower (2.92 ± 3.07 ng/ ml) compared with those of the control group (7.75 ± 6.37 ng/ml; p < .001; Figure 2). Similarly, adjusting for smoking status, age, and gender did not alter this association (p < .001). Additionally, we tested the difference of hBD-2 level between generalized and localized CP. The difference between the groups both in serum (p = .25) and in GCF hBD-2 levels (p = .51) was not statistically significant.”,
5. Correlations
“The correlation between serum and GCF hBD-2 expression and clinical periodontal measures was analyzed. No correlation was observed between serum and GCF hBD-2 levels (r = .004, n = 99, p = .97). On the other hand, both localized GCF and serum hBD-2 were correlated with BOP within the periodontitis group. However, after adjustment by the Bonferroni method for multiple comparisons, a statistically significant correlation remained only between GCF hBD-2 and BOP (r = .54, p = .0002; Table 3).” .

THE PAST — MAY 29, 2023
Sol Invictus: The pagan Sun god that helped Christianity conquer the Roman Empire
Before Constantine received his history-defining vision, a pagan Sun god paved the way for Jesus Christ’s triumphal entry into the Eternal City.
A close up of a carving on a wall showing Sol Invictus
(Credit: Wikimedia Commons)
KEY TAKEAWAYS
For centuries, the Romans persecuted Christians who refused to worship the emperor. This changed in 312 AD when Constantine had a vision and converted to the Christian faith. As the new state religion, Christianity subsumed the framework of the cult of the sun god Sol Invictus.

Tim Brinkhof
Copy a link to the article entitled
Share Sol Invictus: The pagan Sun god that helped Christianity conquer the Roman Empire on Facebook
Share Sol Invictus: The pagan Sun god that helped Christianity conquer the Roman Empire on Twitter
Share Sol Invictus: The pagan Sun god that helped Christianity conquer the Roman Empire on LinkedIn
The crash course version of ancient history holds that the Roman Empire abandoned its old gods after Constantine the Great received a vision during an important military campaign. The night before a pivotal battle against his rival, Maxentius, Constantine was told in a dream to “mark the heavenly sign of God” on his soldiers’ shields to ensure victory. He obeyed and defeated Maxentius. Out of gratitude for the higher power that came to his aid, he turned Christianity from a persecuted sect into the Empire’s official religion.

There might be some truth to this narrative, but in reality, Rome’s transition from polytheism to monotheism was more complicated. Informed by new archeological excavations, modern-day historians credit other, lesser-known cults with paving the way for Christianity’s takeover — a development so drastic that there must have been some preexisting framework for Christianity to latch onto. At the center of this framework, historians argue, is Sol Invictus, a Sabine-Arab Sun god whose role in Roman society was eventually supplanted by Jesus Christ.

The origins of Sol Invictus
Roman history knows two Sols. Worship of the first, Sol Indiges, was limited to the Eternal City itself. A god of agriculture, their first temple — located on the Quirinal Hill — is said to have been built by the Sabine king Tatius, the legendary rival-turned-ally of Rome’s equally legendary founder, Romulus. The cult of Sol Indiges survived into the Republican and early imperial periods. Augustus constructed temples for them. Vespasian converted a giant statue of Nero into the god by adding a crown. Commodus, the son of Marcus Aurelius, added Sol’s name to his own.

A wall mural featuring Dionysos with Helios and Aphrodite.
Sun worship was everywhere in the Roman Empire. (Credit: ArchaiOptix / Wikimedia Commons)
As the borders of the Empire expanded, the Eternal City became a melting pot of different cultures. Italian traditions mingled with those of Africa and Asia Minor, and Sol Indiges combined with an eastern Sun deity to become Sol Invictus, the “Unconquered Sun.” During the third century AD, this second Sol gradually evolved from a god into the god of Rome. The emperor Elagabalus, who was raised in Syria, placed every god worshipped within Rome, including Jupiter, under the umbrella of the Sun god — one of many provocations that would anger the Roman elites and eventually led to his assassination at the hands of the Praetorian Guard.

Although the legacy of Elagabalus was erased by his immediate successors, the cult of Sol Invictus bounced back under Aurelian, who reunited the Empire after it split into three sub-empires. Like successful emperors before him, Aurelian fancied himself the instrument and, at times, embodiment of a higher power. In his case: Sol Invictus. While Aurelian’s connection to Sol is unclear — it has been said that his mother was a priestess — the consequences of his connection are apparent. As argued by Gaston Halsberghe and others, Aurelian’s elevation of the cult helped reforge a fractured empire.

Light and fire
The transition from Sol Invictus to Jesus Christ is best documented in archeological finds. In 1953, researchers began digging underneath St. Peter’s Basilica, built under Constantine, in hope of finding its namesake’s tomb. Although they didn’t find St. Peter, they did stumble across the bodies of various pagans and Christians. In particular, one Christian tomb was decorated with a mosaic that portrayed Christ as Sol Invictus encircled by a rayed nimbus and riding a chariot. Identification with the Sun god may also be preserved in Biblical passages describing Christ and God in relation to light and fire.

A close up of a mosaic on a wall showing Jesus Christ as Sol Invictus.
The mosaic depicting Christ as Sol Invictus from the necropolis under St. Peter’s Basilica. (Credit: Wikimedia Commons)
Even Christmas can be traced back to the cult of Sol. In contrast to the festive Romans, the death-oriented Christians didn’t celebrate birthdays, especially not for gods. “We men gather our vintages, and they think and believe that the gods gather and bring in their grapes,” wrote Arnobius, a Christian apologist from the third century. “We have birthdays, and they affirm that the powers of heaven have birthdays.” Most early Christians didn’t discuss the birth of Christ. Those who did made no reference to the date or offered conflicting dates.

Historians link the advent of Christianity to Sol Invictus partly because December 25 marked the so-called Feast of the Unconquered Sun before it became officially recognized as the birthday of Christ. The cult of Sol originally started holding the Feast on December 25 because it coincided with the winter solstice, the time of year when daylight starts to lengthen again. Theologians settled on the date not just because of the solstice. December 25 was also exactly nine months removed from what they deemed the anniversary of creation, giving the Messiah’s life a regularity befitting of his divine nature.

Rome reborn
Rome’s transition from polytheism to monotheism isn’t about Christianity replacing the cult of Sol Invictus so much as it is about non-Christian Romans accepting Christ as the replacement for the Sun god. Historians still struggle to understand how and why the Empire appropriated a religion it had brutally persecuted for so long. Similarities between the character of Christ and Sol Invictus — such as their mutual association with light and the heavens — constitute one piece of this unsolved puzzle, as does overlap between the practices and rituals of their respective followers.

A painting of a Constantine the Great praying.
Constantine the Great’s visions of the cross as depicted by the Baroque painter Theodoor Boeyermans. (Credit: magnoliabox / Wikimedia Commons)
Some historians place emphasis on the role played by Constantine. Following his vision-verified victory, life became increasingly difficult for subjects who did not follow him into conversion. For example, Constantine’s trust in and promotion of Christians within his bureaucracy made joining the religion a prerequisite for a career in government or the military. As the Empire’s most powerful citizens converted, so did those under their command. Before long, Christianity had spread from Asia Minor to the shores of Spain.

Indicative of Rome’s pluralism, Constantine continued worshipping Sol Invictus even after he converted to Christianity. It was not until 323 AD, more than a decade after he received word from God, that he publicly renounced the Unconquered Sun in favor of the crucified Son. The same year that the Sun disappeared from the emperor’s life, solar symbols disappeared from Roman coins. From this point on, Constantine began donating substantial amounts of capital to the Church and also began showing an active interest in religious affairs. Christianity had become as intertwined with his regime as the cult of Sol was with Aurelian’s.

Introduction
In the emerging age of digitalization of business, Alibaba stands tall among competitors in the world, building and sustaining a successful business model around the concept of a business ecosystem, driven by data for smart businesses. According to Zeng, (2018), there is an underscoring of the innovation adopted by the Alibaba group with its main focus on building an ecosystem. A critical assessment of this data driven model therefore begs the question, how have businesses fared in the ecosystem? It is in the light of attempting to answer this question and many others that this essay attempts to critically look into the data – driven model of smart business in the Chinese market as put forward by Zeng.

Summary of the Business Ecosystem Model
Zeng, (2018), in the article ‘Alibaba and lessons from China’s innovative digital giant’, highlights business ecosystem as the key component and model for Alibaba. According to him, the business ecosystem is a community, connecting businesses to consumers, for the purpose of interactions, with each other and with the business environment. This is in line with Su, Zheng and Chen, (2018), the discussions on the strategic management of businesses cannot be successfully held in recent times without the mentioning of the term ‘ecosystem’. According to them, the term has been defined severally and in various settings by researchers. However, the central message of the idea remains the same. For Li, (2009), the business ecosystem is a look alike of the biological ecosystem which is a representation of the demonstration of a couple of complex relationships existing among the resources co existing in a particular environment. And similar to this biological look alike, the business ecosystem also exists for the functional goal of being self-sufficient and maintaining a sustaining state (de Langen, Sornn-Friese and Hallworth, 2020; Harmaakorpi and Rinkinen, 2020).   The ecosystem serves as a means of fostering communication between this communities of organisms, with the sole imperative of making sure that as Li (2009), rightly pointed out, the platform would cater for its needs by providing all resources needed for the success of any smart business. For this business model, generally key players interact within the ecosystem by sharing data, which according to Koepke, (2015), is a major player of the ecosystem. 

Strengths and weaknesses of Data Driven Smart Business
Since business needs data, and in a large quantity, machine learning has been employed by businesses to gain a cutting edge competitive advantage over traditional business models (García-Muiña et al., 2020). According to Zeng, (2018), machine learning thrives on computing power and of course digital data. This according to him, is directly proportional to the number of iteration the algorithm goes through. Digital data is the basis for business decisions making, and Alibaba sure utilized this approach to better position the business and make it one of the renowned businesses in recent times, competing closely with Walmart, Amazon and e-bay (Hänninen, Mitronen and Kwan, 2019; Lu et al., 2022). Smart businesses have been driven generally by data, and the data volume is just not a disadvantage or limitation for the model, as the iterations are made to answer the questions generated accurately and with the speed of light. The microloan business of Ant financial services, as presented by Zeng, is a typical example of a business within the Alibaba ecosystem using the smart business model driven by digital data. Major decisions such as how much a customer is qualified to borrow, and of course at what interest rate, are now made and decisions taken immediately and the best part is that these decisions are taken with precision and not less accuracy. However, issues of customer privacy is a major concern and drawback of this model. As a consumer, Taobao, a domestic retailing arm of the Alibaba group collects live data naturally using the instant messaging app wangwang (Zeng, 2018). How safe is the customer?

Recommendations 
There are various challenges faced by smart businesses in emerging markets. These challenges are generally issues of privacy and other inadequacies stumbled upon as a result of the implementation of machine learning methods in decision making (Li, 2018). To manage these challenges, firms must adopt cutting edge optimized supply chain strategies, and must utilize and adopt a network in order to meet their objective of surviving the competition in the emerging market. This particular responsibility rests on the leaders, whose roles must be that of providing motivation to employees and everyone involved in the ecosystem including the customers (Mabaso et al., 2021). These recommendations are not rigid because even the business environment is fluid and so the leaders and their business must evolve alongside to ensure they stay afloat and competitive.

Conclusion 
The key lesson learned from Alibaba's model in the Chinese market is the power of leveraging data and technology to drive smart business decisions. By utilizing machine learning and large volumes of digital data, Alibaba has gained a competitive edge and improved its understanding of customer needs, leading to more efficient and effective operations.

As I groggily answered the phone, Randy's voice filled my ear, cutting through the early morning haze. “Joseph, don't worry about Richard anymore. I've sent him to London to oversee the business. You can rest assured he won't come between your work.”

“He's stubborn, Joseph. He doesn't care about anything beyond his own vanity. I'll keep working on him, but until then, he won't be a bother to you.”

I ended the call, frustrated by their excuses. I knew Randy was lying. There was no way he couldn't exert his influence over his son when he held all the power. It was becoming increasingly clear that I needed to teach this father-son duo a lesson they wouldn't soon forget.

Shaking off my annoyance, I got ready for the day ahead. Mark joined me for breakfast, and as we sat at the table, we delved into a lively conversation about the upcoming school picnic. “Dad I want to go on my school trip.”

“Mark, I really don't think it's safe for you to go on that alone like that,” I expressed my concern, hoping he would understand. “There have been some security issues lately. I don’t want to happen what happened that day. I can't risk your life.”

But Mark, ever the adventurous spirit, waved off my worries. “Come on, dad! All my friends are going, and it's going to be so much fun! I promise I'll be careful.”

I sighed, realizing that convincing Mark otherwise would be a difficult task. “We’ll discuss about this later in the evening, okay?”

Mark beamed with disappointment. “Dad please.”

“Later Mark. I'm getting late.”

After finishing our breakfast, I accompanied Mark to school, bidding him farewell as he eagerly joined his friends. As I made my way to the office, my mind focused on the tasks at hand.

Upon arriving at the office, I was met by Alex and Rose, who eagerly presented the finalized advertisement to the entire team. The room buzzed with excitement as the advertisement played, showcasing their hard work and creativity.

I couldn't help but feel a surge of pride as I watched the advertisement unfold on the screen. The team had put their heart and soul into it, and the results were remarkable. “Congratulations, Alex,” I commended him, a genuine smile on my face. “You've done an excellent job.”

Alex beamed with gratitude, thanking me and then departing with his team to celebrate their success. With their departure, Rose and I were left alone in the office.

Turning to Rose, I spoke with determination. “We need to show this advertisement to the board of directors. Once they approve it, we can move forward and start pitching it to broadcasting channels for telecast.”

Rose nodded, her eyes shining with determination. “I agree, Joseph. Let's make sure this advertisement reaches its full potential.”

With a shared sense of purpose, we wrapped up our discussions, confident in the next steps we needed to take. As I left the office, a spark of excitement coursed through me. It was moments like these, when I saw the fruits of our labor and the passion of those around me, that reminded me why I fought so hard to protect what was rightfully mine.

Heading out into the bustling city, I couldn't help but feel a renewed sense of determination. The battle with Richard and Randy was far from over, but I was ready to face them head-on. The future held both challenges and triumphs, and I was prepared to embrace them all.

As I entered the bustling headquarters of Fame Foods, a wave of commotion hit me. It had completely slipped my mind that the elections were approaching this Friday, and the atmosphere in the office was charged with anticipation. My assistant hurried towards me, a look of concern etched on his face.

“Sir, Mr. Kent is already meeting with the board of directors, trying to persuade them to vote for him. What do you want us to do in response?” he asked, his voice tinged with urgency.

I paused for a moment, weighing my options. “Let him do his work,” I finally replied, a sense of calm determination coloring my voice.

My assistant looked taken aback. “You won't do anything? We need to play along, sir. What if you end up losing?”

A wry smile crept onto my face. “It's fine. I already have my hands full with other projects. Being chairman can be quite a headache.”

Handing him a drive containing the video advertisement we had worked tirelessly on, I instructed him, “Show this to the directors and seek their approval. Once we have it, we can move forward with the next steps.”

He nodded, understanding the gravity of the task. I retreated to my office, allowing the weight of anticipation to settle upon my shoulders. Time seemed to stretch as I awaited news from the board, each passing moment filled with both apprehension and hope.

Finally, the phone rang, shattering the silence. It was my assistant, his voice filled with excitement. “Sir, the results are in, and they're positive! The directors were impressed with the chemistry of the couple and the showcasing of our products. They believe it will resonate with the audience.”

A surge of satisfaction coursed through my veins. The hard work and dedication had paid off. It was a triumph not just for me but for Rose as well, whose creative brilliance shone through in the advertisement. I couldn't wait to share the news with her.

Dialing her number, I couldn't contain the excitement in my voice. “Rose, congratulations! Your first project has been approved!”

Her joy was palpable through the phone as she exclaimed, “Really?”

“Yes! You can go ahead and start contacting the broadcasting channels. The sooner we get this on air, the better.”

“Alright,” she replied eagerly, her determination shining through.

“And don't forget about the dinner you promised,” I added, a touch of playfulness in my voice.

She laughed, the sound melodic and infectious. “Yes, of course! Consider it done!”

As we ended the call, I couldn't help but feel a surge of happiness. The hurdles and challenges we had faced were nothing compared to the exhilaration of achieving our goals together. It was moments like these that reminded me why I embarked on this journey in the first place.

Mark and I arrived at Rose's house for dinner, and as soon as we stepped inside, the atmosphere was transformed into one of warmth and romance. The dining table was adorned with a beautiful display of roses and flickering candles, creating an ambiance that invited us to linger and savor the evening.

I couldn't help but notice the addition of a high chair at the table, replacing one of the regular chairs. Curiosity got the better of me, and I inquired, “You bought this high chair?”

Rose smiled, her eyes gleaming with tenderness. “I noticed that Mark wasn't comfortable sitting in the regular chairs, so I thought it would be better for him to have his own since he is at my place so often.”

“Thanks, Rose,” Mark chimed in, giving her a tight hug. His gratitude was evident, and it warmed my heart to see the bond growing between them. Mark's next question made me curious about the menu for the evening.

“What did you make for me?” he asked eagerly.

Rose's face lit up with excitement. “Everything you like. I even asked your father for a little guidance. I hope it turns out to be just the way you want it.”

We all worked together to set the table, the act itself fostering a sense of togetherness and anticipation. With everything in place, we sat down to feast on the delectable spread that Rose had prepared.

As I surveyed the table filled with an array of dishes—burgers, tacos, spaghetti, salad—I couldn't help but comment on the abundance. “You made quite a lot,” I mentioned, genuinely impressed.

A soft chuckle escaped Rose's lips. “I have a passion for cooking, but I don't often cook for myself. Having someone to cook for gives me the motivation to create all these dishes.”

I couldn't help but smile at her words. Her selflessness and desire to nourish others resonated deeply within me. As Mark dove into his burger with enthusiasm, he added, his mouth half full, “Rose, can you please convince Daddy to let me go to the picnic? I really want to go with my friends.”

Rose looked at me, confusion evident in her eyes. “Why are you not going?” she inquired, genuinely curious.

I chimed in, my voice firm but gentle. “Because going anywhere unsupervised is not wise at the moment. It's a matter of your safety Mark.”

Mark pouted, disappointment etched on his face. “But it's been so long, and Dad never lets me go anywhere alone. I really want to go. All my friends are going.”

I tried to reason with him, “I promise, next year you will definitely go. But for now, it's important to prioritize your safety.”

However, Rose interjected with a surprising proposal. “Alright, Mark, you will go to the picnic,” she declared, causing Mark to pause his tantrum in astonishment. “But not with your school friends. You'll go with me.”

Both Mark and I exclaimed simultaneously, “With you?”

Rose nodded, a determined glint in her eyes. “Yes, we can go together. It will be a fun day out.”

Mark's face lit up with uncontainable excitement. “Really? You'll take me, Rose?” he asked, his eyes brimming with anticipation.

A soft smile curved her lips as she replied, “I'll take you, Mark. You deserve to have a great time.”

Mark turned to me, his expression triumphant. “See, Dad! Rose said I can go!”

I couldn't help but chuckle at the turn of events. “Alright, alright. It seems I've been outvoted. But promise me you'll stick together and stay safe, okay?”

Mark nodded enthusiastically, a mix of relief and joy radiating from him. “Thank you, Rose. You're the best!”

We continued our meal while joy and laughter in the room multiplied. In that moment, I realized that Rose's presence had brought a new dimension to our lives—a sense of adventure, love, and shared experiences. And as Mark and Rose shared excited whispers about their upcoming adventure, I couldn't help but be grateful for the unexpected bond that was forming within our unconventional bond.

As we sat chatting and basking in the warm afterglow of our delicious dinner, my phone buzzed with an incoming call. I excused myself from the conversation and answered, only to be greeted by my secretary's urgent voice on the other end.

“Joseph, you need to turn on the television right now,” she exclaimed.

But Rose had a plan, her confidence shining through. “I have a great idea that I believe will work. We can offer them a ten percent share of the new sales generated through their promotions. It will be an irresistible incentive for them to showcase our products.”

Her determination was contagious, and I found myself intrigued by the prospect. “Let's go over the details tomorrow,” I agreed, realizing that Rose's innovative thinking could be the key to expanding our reach and capturing a broader audience.

With our plans set aside for the moment, we returned to the table to indulge in the mouthwatering desserts that awaited us. As we savored each sweet bite, I couldn't help but feel a surge of excitement for the future. The success of our advertisement and the prospect of further expansion filled the room with an electric energy, and I knew that with Rose by my side, we could conquer any challenge that lay ahead.

通过本课程的学习，我对电气工程及其自动化专业有了更深入的认识。电气工程及其自动化专业主要包括电机、变压器、发电设备、输电设备、配电设备、控制设备等方面的研究和应用。在实际生产过程中，本专业需要对电气系统进行设计、制造、安装、运行和维护。而自动化技术的应用，则是为了提高电气系统的可靠性、安全性和经济性。为了实现这一目标，我深刻的明白本专业需要掌握一系列知识技能，包括电气工程基本原理、自动化技术、电气设备、工程实践和创新能力等。通过本课程的学习，我对这些方面有了更清晰的概念，更好地认识了电气工程及其自动化专业的内涵。

通过本课程的学习，我发现自己对电力系统及其装备和自动化技术两个方向较感兴趣。电力系统是电力工程的核心内容，通过了解和研究电力系统的运行原理和装备，可以为我在电气领域的发展奠定一个良好的基础。而自动化技术近年来发展迅速，在各行各业中都有广泛的应用，我认为掌握自动化技术，对我的职业发展也会有很大帮助。

        啪咚、啪咚，百花公园的石板路被我的脚砸得山响，路边小树上的一群麻雀被惊得飞逃了。呼，呼，我气喘如牛，汗出如浆，“我……不行了，我歇歇。“爸妈果然是有预谋地要坑我，他们所谓的一年之计竟然就是拉着我跑步锻炼，真是要了我的老命，呜……

        本来以为爸爸出差走了，我能放松了，没想妈妈却带着秒表监督我。我心理暗道：这妈也不是亲妈了，真是狼狈为奸！
        杨柳拂风，池塘蛙鸣，一个周五的傍晚，我在跑第二圈中，发现前面有几个和我穿着相同校服的学生在讨论游戏，我从他们身边跑过。只听一人说道：咦，看看，同样是附中学生，看看人家多上进啊！另一人道：是啊，这才是我辈楷模呀。
        我脸上有些发烫，我努力作出步伐轻盈的样子，拉开了和他们的距离，却不由地回味那一丝被人羡慕的幸福。

        阳光透过槐叶洒在我的身上，麻雀唱着歌儿从枝头飞起，我的心就化成了那只麻雀。

maxDays = max_circle
# 创建一个空列表ProductList，用于存储产品对象
ProductList = []

# 在给定的最大天数maxDays范围内反复遍历训练数据集中的每一天
step = len(train_data)
preAction = 0
preNum = 0
for i in range(maxDays):
# 机器学习，补货
j = i%step # 将变量i除以step的余数赋值给变量j,将i限定在0到step-1之间，循环遍历train_data
buy_num = int(train_data[j])
# int将字符串型数据转换为整数型数据

deleteOverDueProduct(ProductList)

# 当前状态

if buy_num > current_num:
short_n = buy_num - current_num
else:
short_n = 0

# 当天卖出的货物出库，即将前buy_num - short_n个产品从列表中删除
ProductList = CheckOutProduct(ProductList, buy_num - short_n)
# 重新获取当前状态，准备补货
current_num = getInStoreHouseNum(ProductList)

# 根据贝尔曼方程，更新 Q table 中当前状态-动作对应的 Q value
alpha = mySetting.getAlpha(i)
gamma = mySetting.getGamma()
rewards = mySetting.getRewards(overdue_n,short_n,buy_num - short_n,preNum)
pre_q_v = mySetting.Q_table[preNum, preAction]
mySetting.Q_table[preNum, preAction] += alpha * (rewards + gamma * max(mySetting.Q_table[current_num]) - pre_q_v)

# 随机或贪婪地选择当前动作
if (np.random.uniform() < mySetting.getEpsilon()) or ((mySetting.Q_table[current_num, :] == mySetting.init_min_val).all()):
tmp_a = get_valid_actions(mySetting, current_num)

current_action = mySetting.actions.index(tmp_a[s]) # 探索
else:
valid_actions = [a for a in mySetting.actions if (a * mySetting.unit + current_num) <= mySetting.max_storages]
current_action = mySetting.Q_table[current_num, :len(valid_actions)].argmax() # 利用

preNum = current_num
preAction = current_action

# 补充货物
add_num = mySetting.actions[current_action] * mySetting.unit
AddProductOrder(ProductList,mySetting.liftime,mySetting.onwaydays,add_num)

# 刷新货物生存时间
updateProductLife(ProductList)

fh = open(qfile,“w”)
aa = mySetting.Q_table.shape
# 遍历Q_table数组中的每个元素，将其转化为字符串形式
for i in range(aa[0]):
tmp1 = mySetting.Q_table[i].tolist()
# 按照逗号进行连接，并在其末尾添加一个换行符
tmp2 = [str(a) for a in tmp1]
cntStr = “,”.join(tmp2)+“\n”
fh.write(cntStr)
fh.close()

# 读取文件所有的行
def ReadTxtName(filename, dot=‘,’, encoding=“gbk”):
lines = []
if os.path.exists(filename): # 判断filename文件是否存在
pass
else:
return []

with open(filename, ‘r’, encoding=encoding) as file_to_read:
tmpall = file_to_read.readlines()
for line in tmpall:
tmpstr = line.strip(‘\n’).strip() # 去掉每行字符串开头和结尾的空白字符（包括空格、制表符、换行符等）
if tmpstr.startswith(‘#’): # 判断tmpstr字符串是否以#开头
continue # 如果是注释行，则继续跳过后面的代码，进行下一轮循环

if len(tmpstr) >0:
line = tmpstr.split(dot) # 将tmpstr字符串按照指定的分隔符dot进行分割
lines.append(line)
return lines

def GetColumnFromList(list, startrow=0, endrow=None, col=0):
data = []
if endrow is None or endrow > len(list):
endrow = len(list)

for i in range(startrow, endrow): # 遍历列表的行数
data.append(list[i][col]) # 将每行的第“col”列的数据添加到“data”列表

return data

def StrListToFloat(list):
data = []
for x in list:
if x != ‘’: # 当前元素不为空字符串
data.append(float(x)) # 转化为浮点数类型
else:
data.append(0)
return data

# 将二维字符串列表转化为浮点数列表
def StrList2ToFloat(list):
rslt = []
for row in list:
data = []
for x in row:
if x != ‘’:
if is_number(x):
data.append(float(x))
else:
data.append(x)
# 如果当前元素为空字符串，则将其填补为默认值 0，并添加到 “data” 列表中
else:
data.append(0)
rslt.append(data)
return rslt

def Create_Train_Data(datafile):
mysetting = Settings()
mu = mysetting.expect
sigma = mysetting.variance
num = mysetting.train_data_n
np.random.seed(1234)
Train_Data = np.random.normal(mu, sigma, num)
# 生成符合正态分布的随机数（μ为期望，σ为方差，数量为num）

f1 = open(datafile,“w”)
for i in range(len(Train_Data)):
cnt = int(Train_Data[i]+0.5)

if i<len(Train_Data)-1:
f1.write(str(cnt)+“,”)
else:
f1.write(str(cnt))
f1.close()

# 读取训练数据并返回其中的一行数据
def Read_Train_Data(datafile):
data = ReadTxtName(datafile)
return data[0]

data = ReadTxtName(datafile)
data1 = StrList2ToFloat(data)
rslt = np.array(data1)
return rslt

Keep conversations moving forward by bringing context from an email into a Slack channel or direct message with the Slack for Gmail Add-On available in the G Suite Marketplace. You can choose to add a message and include attachments along with the email as well.
When to send email into Slack:
• Email chain getting too noisy? Send it into Slack where you can discuss quickly and move forward.
• Have an idea you want to share with your team? Send it along to a relevant channel with a note about your insights.
• Need to coordinate a response to a customer question? Flag your teammates in Slack and use the email content to set context.
How the Add-On works:
• Start by installing the Slack for Gmail Add-On from the G Suite Marketplace
• Open any email and click on the Slack icon in the right-hand side of your inbox
• Choose the channel or person you’d like to forward the email to inside of Slack
• Add a message and include attachments if you’d like
• Voilà! The email is forwarded into Slack where anyone in the channel or direct message you shared it to can see the email content and open attachments.
Please note that the following limits apply to emails shared via this app:
• The combined headers and body of an email cannot be larger than 1MB.
• When combined with attachments, an email cannot be larger than 30 MB.
• There is a maximum of 20 attachments per email.

As I stepped out of the taxi, bidding farewell to the chaotic night, a new day unfolded before me, painting the world in hues of possibility and anticipation. It was Sunday, a day that whispered of quiet reflection and the embrace of mundane tasks that tethered me to reality. With a flicker of determination, I decided to make a quick stop at the grocery store before retreating to the sanctuary of my home.
Navigating the aisles, I found myself captivated by the kaleidoscope of colors that adorned the shelves, each product vying for my attention. Lost in a reverie, my thoughts drifting between the items on my mental shopping list and the memories of the previous night, I was momentarily caught off guard.
As fate would have it, I collided with a passing stranger, our bodies melding together in a brief, electric encounter. In that fleeting moment, a surge of familiarity coursed through me, like a thread of destiny woven between us.
My eyes followed the man's retreating figure, a spark of recognition igniting a cascade of memories. The scenes from last night's revelry danced before me, vibrant and alive. Drunken Rose, with her audacious charm and unapologetic desires, had come to life under the influence of spirits. The memory of her leaning in, tantalizingly close to Joseph's lips, hung in the air, a silent invitation suspended in time. The tension between us crackled, an invisible current that defied sobriety, daring us to explore what lay beyond the realm of friendship.
But amidst the haze of the night's intoxication, a surge of embarrassment washed over me. How could I face Joseph after my uninhibited attempts at seduction? The memories were both mortifying and exhilarating, a tapestry woven with vulnerability and boldness.
With a deep breath, I shook off the weight of self-consciousness and resumed my shopping, determined to face whatever awaited me. The tinge of romance lingered in the air, subtle but undeniable, like a whisper of a love story waiting to unfold.
As I moved through the aisles, my fingers lightly grazing the products on display, I couldn't help but be drawn back to the memories of last night. Each fragment played out in my mind with fluidity and grace, like the steps of a well-choreographed dance.
I could almost taste the heady mixture of anticipation and desire that swirled between us as Joseph led me to his car, his voice laced with a gentle yet firm resolve. The mere thought of his touch sent a shiver down my spine, the memory of his hand securing the seatbelt around me tinged with a tenderness that made my heart flutter.
“In the grand scheme of adventures, my dear, it's time to head home,” Joseph's voice resonated, his words carrying a hint of longing and determination.
“But I want to drink more,” I pouted, my words slurring slightly, my inhibitions fading like wisps of smoke.
Joseph's gaze held a mix of concern and unwavering resolve as he guided me into the car’s back seat, his touch gentle yet firm. “You'll get sick, Rose,” he reasoned, his voice a soothing balm against the chaos of the night while caressing my falling head all the way as someone else drove his car.
Fatigue washed over me, rendering me too tired to put up a fight. Reluctantly, I acquiesced, allowing him to take the wheel and guide us towards an unknown destination. As the car came to a stop in front of his house, confusion and protest welled within me.
“Why are we here? Take me to my place,” I insisted, a touch of frustration lacing my words.
Joseph's eyes met mine, his resolve unshaken. “No,” he replied firmly, a hint of playful determination lacing his voice. “You are sleeping here.”
A flicker of defiance ignited within me, and I unbuckled my seatbelt, lunging forward to grab his shoulder, a desperate attempt to regain control. “Take me to my home,” I implored, my grip tightening, my words laced with a mixture of intoxication and determination.
He maintained his composure, his eyes brimming with patience and a touch of amusement. “You know I can resist your charming threats, but I don’t want you at your hope alone when you are this stupidly drunk after just five shots.” he responded calmly, his words carrying a hint of playful warning.
My protests faltered, my grip loosening as the realization dawned on me that perhaps Joseph knew what was best for me in that moment. The weight of my intoxication settled in, and reluctantly, I allowed him to carry me inside his home, surrendering to his protective embrace.
As we navigated the familiar hallways, silence enveloped us, punctuated only by the soft sound of our breaths. In the room where I had awakened earlier that day, a sanctuary for the remnants of a night filled with blurred memories and unspoken desires, Joseph began to undress me with a tenderness that made my heart flutter.
“What are you trying to do?” I asked, my voice slurred but laced with a hint of curiosity, a tinge of vulnerability that mirrored the uncharted territory between us.
He staggered back slightly, momentarily caught off guard by my sudden resistance. “I'm changing you out of this chaotic mess,” he explained, a mixture of gentle exasperation and unwavering affection coloring his words.
Determined to assert my independence, I pushed him away, a surge of fiery spirit coursing through me. “I'll do it myself,” I insisted, a mixture of intoxication and determination shaping my actions.
The room grew quiet as I struggled to remove the dishevelled remnants of the night, my hands fumbling with buttons and zippers. Joseph watched me, his gaze a blend of admiration and amusement, a silent acknowledgment of my spirited nature even in the midst of inebriation.
As I stood there, surrounded by the mundane routine of grocery shopping, the weight of embarrassment settled upon me like a velvet cloak. How would our encounters be marred by awkwardness and regret? I messed it all up. I acted all calm and controlled in front of him, but now I've shown him all my drunken escapades, insulted him and myself. I don’t deserved to see him again. I quietly went back home, drowned myself in the comfort of my bed and refused to leave it the whole day. Until I can really have enough strength to stand up.
**
Monday arrived, casting a shadow of uncertainty upon me as I grappled with the question of how to face Joseph. Amidst my swirling thoughts, an idea began to take shape—a daring plan to feign forgetfulness, to don the veil of dementia and shield myself from the embarrassment of the previous night. With newfound determination, I pushed my nervousness aside and prepared for the day ahead, choosing a sophisticated brown and beige pant suit that exuded confidence. Today marked the beginning of a new chapter in my life, a chapter filled with nervous excitement and the promise of unexpected twists.
As I approached the building that held a special place in my heart, memories of my father flooded my mind. This was the place he would bring me to every weekend, regaling me with stories of his work and his entrepreneurial journey. I recalled his passion, his vision to create an agency that would help local businesses thrive. It all began with a small investment from my grandfather, and with my father's unique and refreshing ideas, the agency soon attracted big clients who sought his transformative touch. They used to say that my father had the power to breathe new life into any product through rebranding, and indeed, he worked wonders in his days. However, with success came the bitter taste of betrayal. Even his closest friend Randy, Richard's father, succumbed to the allure of money, severing their friendship and leaving my father with nothing in return for his generosity.
When my father passed away, the power of attorney fell into Richard's hands, as my father had not left behind a will and he was the second most important person in the business. Perhaps dad never expected his life to be cut short. Richard and his family took advantage of this situation, exploiting their newfound control over the agency. It was a painful realization for me, knowing that my father had intended for me to take over once I graduated from college—a dream that would forever remain unfulfilled.
I gazed up at the once majestic building, a monument to my father's dreams and aspirations. Time had not been kind to it, leaving behind a faded facade and an air of neglect. Richard had never cared for the business, choosing to extract profits without investing any effort into its growth. In seven years, all my father’s work is now reduced to something with zero value. It now stood as a mere shadow of its former glory. Doubts crept into my mind, whispering of the enormity of the task ahead, questioning whether I could ever restore it to its former grandeur. But in that moment, a flicker of determination ignited within me, promising that I would give it everything I had, against all odds.
With a deep breath, I pushed open the worn-out doors, stepping into the familiar yet decaying interior. Dust danced in the rays of sunlight that filtered through cracked windows, giving the room an ethereal quality. I could almost hear the echo of my father's voice, guiding me through the halls, sharing his wisdom and dreams. Each step I took was laden with purpose, a silent declaration that I would honor his legacy, breathe life into the forgotten corners, and revive the agency that had once been the source of his pride.
The path ahead was uncertain, strewn with obstacles and challenges. But as I stood there, surrounded by the remnants of a forgotten empire, I embraced the weight of responsibility. Determined and resilient, I vowed to breathe new life into this space, to create a future that would make my father proud. The journey was just beginning, and as I embarked on this chapter of my life, I couldn't help but feel a flicker of excitement, eager to see how the story would unfold. Feeling the strength pulsating beneath, I entered inside.
Joseph stood in the room that once belonged to my father, his presence commanding attention. “Good morning,” he greeted with a warm smile. “Ready for the big day?”
I nodded, my nerves still palpable beneath my composed exterior. “I didn't expect the place to look like this,” I confessed, my eyes scanning the room. “It feels like an entirely different space from my childhood memories.”
Joseph's gaze softened, understanding the weight of nostalgia that hung in the air. “The renovations will start tomorrow,” he explained. “But today, I called you here to discuss any ideas you might have for the restoration. Your input is valuable, and I want you to be a part of the process.”
A hint of skepticism tinged my response. “Shouldn't we trust the workers to handle it? I would rather have experts do it, rather than my “
Joseph chuckled, his eyes sparkling with a mix of amusement and reassurance. “Of course, we trust their expertise. But your perspective is unique, and your memories of this place hold sentimental value. It's a chance for you to leave your mark on the transformation.”
His words resonated with me, and I nodded in agreement. “Alright, let's head to your office then. I assume you have something to discuss.”
As if on cue, Joseph's car awaited us outside. He directed his driver to take my car back to my place, while he took the wheel. The gentle hum of the engine filled the silence as we embarked on our journey to his office.
With a lighthearted air, Joseph initiated a conversation. “Are you feeling fine?” he asked, his eyes studying my expression with a mix of concern and curiosity.
I couldn't help but feel a pang of guilt as the memories of the previous night resurfaced. How could I possibly be fine knowing what had transpired? “Yeah, why?” I replied, attempting to mask my inner turmoil.
“Just curious if you're still hungover,” he confessed, a playful glint in his eyes.
Suppressing a nervous laugh, I replied with feigned nonchalance, “No, I'm fine! I'm quite used to drinking. I don't get hungover.” Oh, the lies we weave.
His lips curled into a knowing smile. “I had your dress cleaned. You can pick it up next time.”
“Thank you, Joseph. I appreciate it,” I responded, my tone genuine. “By the way, why did you lie?”
His eyebrows furrowed in confusion. “I lied?”
“Yes,” I stated matter-of-factly. “You said you changed my clothes when you didn't.”
A mischievous twinkle danced in his eyes as he took a brief pause, savoring the moment. “Oh well, so you remember what you did.”
Caught off guard, I stumbled over my words. “Bits and pieces,” I admitted, my cheeks flushing with embarrassment.
A devilish smirk graced his lips. “Then you must also remember when you kissed me.”
My heart skipped a beat, my mind scrambling to process his revelation. “I didn't kiss you,” I protested, though doubt gnawed at the edges of my memory. “You stopped me, remember?”
His gaze locked with mine, his eyes filled with a playful blend of amusement and desire. “I remember, and it seems like you do too. Do you also remember kicking me?”
My voice cracked nervously as I vehemently denied the accusation. “No!” I exclaimed, the fear of my actions surfacing once again.
Unfazed, Joseph nodded with a knowing smile. “You do.”
His parking maneuver brought our car to a halt, and he turned to face me. “Let's get out. I need you to meet a few people,” he stated, his voice a mixture of authority and anticipation. “Your new employees. We'll be rebranding the company, and I want only useful people working there. I've already made a few appointments. I'll be managing the company for the time being until you become familiar with the work you need to do.”
I absorbed his words, a mixture of gratitude and curiosity swirling within me. As we stepped out of the car, he led the way toward the elevator, his presence both commanding and comforting. My mind buzzed with questions, anticipation building for the encounters that awaited me. “Who am I meeting?” I couldn't help but inquire, eager to face the challenges and opportunities that lay ahead.
“Your new team,” he replied with a hint of excitement. “The individuals who will help shape our future.” I nodded and the elevator door opened.

import random

class Drone:
    def __init__(self, x, y):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.mode = "Idle"

    def update_location(self, new_x, new_y):
        self.x = max(0, min(new_x, 100))
        self.y = max(0, min(new_y, 100))

    def update_mode(self, new_mode):
        self.mode = new_mode

def calculate_distance(drone1, drone2, metrics):
    total_distance = 0
    for metric in metrics:
        if metric == 'euclidean':
            distance = math.sqrt((drone1.x - drone2.x) ** 2 + (drone1.y - drone2.y) ** 2)
        elif metric == 'manhattan':
            distance = abs(drone1.x - drone2.x) + abs(drone1.y - drone2.y)
        elif metric == 'chebyshev':
            distance = max(abs(drone1.x - drone2.x), abs(drone1.y - drone2.y))
        total_distance += distance
    return total_distance

Перескажи данный текст своими словами: Ответ прост – конечно, разные. Из всего этого разнообразия я приведу простую классификацию, которую рассматривал в цитированной выше книге З.Бауман. Он говорил о двух типах отношений: «дарения» и «обмена». Автор иллюстрировал различие между ними следующими примерами, проистекающими из типичной житейской проблемы: нужно занять денег. Первый тип отношений возникает, если вы идете к брату, и он вам одалживает денег на необременительных, естественно, условиях. Второй тип отношений вы обнаружите, если пойдете брать ссуду в банке. Первый тип отношений сопровождается, по мнению автора, бескорыстной жертвой (даже воинский подвиг он относит к этому типу). Второй сопряжен с конкуренцией интересов двух сторон и их урегулированием общепринятыми правилами совершения сделок. Два указанных типа социальных взаимоотношений располагаются по разную сторону следующих альтернатив (первым в приведенных далее парах указывается качество, присущее отношению дарения, а вторым – качество, присущее отношению обмена): личное – безличное; партикулярное – универсальное; диффузное – специфическое; аффективное – аффективно нейтральное.

Ниже будет приведено мое понимание соответствия между двумя указанными видами отношений в виде некоторой исторической сказки, поскольку, как представляется, между ними существует определенная историческая преемственность. Кроме того, к ним будет добавлен третий тип отношений – отношение услуги (термин столь же неудачный, как и «отношение дарения», но его применимость можно будет оценить после разъяснения его смысла).

Итак, представим себе первобытное племя – этакую расширенную семью, небольшую общность наших предков, которые объединились для защиты друг друга. Единство и защищенность племени обеспечивается постоянными связями между его членами. В силу этого услуги, пища, предметы переходят от одного члена общины к другому не в порядке обмена, а в рамках отношений дарения, но вот в каком смысле. Конкретное дарение символизирует, во-первых, что тот, кто получает дар, является полноценным членом сообщества. Тот, кто дарит, – не только член группы, фактом дарения он подчеркивает свою принадлежность к ней, ее установлениям, ее морали, если угодно. Дарение одобряется, отказ от него порицается. Дарение сопровождается положительными эмоциями не только потому, что кто-то что-то получил, но и потому, что оно означает очередное подтверждение принадлежности сообществу. Но дело не только в этом. Дарение означает, что тот, кто подарил, может также рассчитывать на подарок, когда возникнет необходимость. Так, врачевательница, залечившая рану охотнику, через две недели получит кусок мяса убитого животного.

Дарение – самый древний вид отношений, но он сохраняется до сих пор. Причем легко увидеть простую закономерность: чем больше группа, тем «жиже» эти отношения. Вы можете прийти к соседям и попросить соль, поскольку она у вас неожиданно закончилась. Как правило, обе стороны с удовольствием участвуют в этом акте. Здесь группа – соседи. Вы отблагодарите позже, той же солью или спичками. Но телевизор не будет включен в перечень в этот обмен. Для этого должна существовать другая группа с более устойчивыми и развитыми связями: «хорошие соседи». Но такая группа будет, скорее всего, поменьше. Группа, охваченная подобными отношениями, может резко расширяться в условиях общей опасности. Тогда цена дара может возрастать, доходя до самопожертвования. Отношения дарения могут модифицируясь охватывать большие группы. Так возникает клиентизм или блат. В более или менее чистом виде отношения дарения сохраняются ныне в патриархальных группах, в частности – на селе.

Отношения обмена стали возникать по мере интенсификации контактов между племенами. Далее в их развитие внес вклад процесс социальной сегментации. Пожалуй, главное качество отношений обмена, отличающее их от дарения и не отмеченное Бауманом, – это их случайность и неустойчивость. Как правило, вы совершаете покупки в разных магазинах, у разных продавцов, не заводя знакомств. В таких условиях не могут развиваться эмоционально окрашенные межличностные отношения. Главное здесь – общепринятая процедура. Если же мы попадаем в условия небольшой общины, между продавцами и покупателями могут возникать отношения, превышающие процедурную сухость стандартного обмена.

Замечу, что различия между отношениями дарения и обмена хорошо соотносятся с двумя типами коррупции, которые можно условно назвать «западный» и «восточный». Первый тип может трактоваться как нелегальный рынок теневых услуг, который регулируется отношениями обмена. Для восточной коррупции характерно вплетение коррупционных отношений в ткань других, фактически легитимных (в веберовском смысле: принятых обществом как нормальных) социальных отношений, и здесь нередко размыта грань между коррупционными отношениями и отношениями дарения.

Третий тип отношений укоренялся по мере развития государства и осознания того факта, что государство – это институт оказания определенных услуг его гражданам. Эти отношения – отношения услуги – развиваются следующим образом. Сначала граждане «дарят» государству свои налоги. Эти налоги идут на то, чтобы оказывать гражданам определенные услуги. Для этого нанимаются другие граждане, которых у нас называют должностными лицами. Гражданин приходит к должностному лицу, когда у него возникает некоторая потребность, и обе стороны вступают в отношения услуги. При этом незримо присутствует третья сторона – государство, которое оплачивает (деньгами гражданина) услуги, оказываемые этому гражданину должностным лицом, включая его жалование. Ниже мы увидим, как искажение этих отношений преобразуется в коррупцию.
