We’ll use standardisation for our training features X by removing the mean and scaling to unit variance. Standardisation helps the deep learning model to learn by ensuring that parameters can exist in the same multi-dimensional space; it wouldn’t make much sense to have the weights have to change their size simply because all the variables have different scales. For our target y, we will scale and translate each feature individually to between 0 and 1. This transformation is often used as an alternative to zero mean, unit variance scaling:



from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler
mm = MinMaxScaler()
ss = StandardScaler()

X_trans = ss.fit_transform(X)
y_trans = mm.fit_transform(y.reshape(-1, 1))


---

We want to feed in 100 samples, up to the current day, and predict the next 50 time step values. To do this, we need a special function to ensure that the corresponding indices of X and y represent this structure. Examine this function carefully, but essentially it just boils down to getting 100 samples from X, then looking at the 50 next indices in y, and patching these together. Note that because of this we'll throw out the first 50 values of y. :



# split a multivariate sequence past, future samples (X and y)
def split_sequences(input_sequences, output_sequence, n_steps_in, n_steps_out):
    X, y = list(), list() # instantiate X and y
    for i in range(len(input_sequences)):
        # find the end of the input, output sequence
        end_ix = i + n_steps_in
        out_end_ix = end_ix + n_steps_out - 1
        # check if we are beyond the dataset
        if out_end_ix > len(input_sequences): break
        # gather input and output of the pattern
        seq_x, seq_y = input_sequences[i:end_ix], output_sequence[end_ix-1:out_end_ix, -1]
        X.append(seq_x), y.append(seq_y)
    return np.array(X), np.array(y)

X_ss, y_mm = split_sequences(X_trans, y_trans, 100, 50)

I want you to analyze and learn and remember the tone, style and structure of the below writing 
The world is sad, Oscar Wilde said, because a puppet was once melancholy. He was referring to Hamlet, a character he thought had taught the world a new kind of unhappiness—the unhappiness of eternal disappointment in life as it is, Weltschmerz. Whether Shakespeare invented it or not, it has proved to be one of the most addictive of literary emotions. Readers consume volumes of it, and then ask to meet the author. It has also proved to be one of the most enduring of literary emotions, since life manages to come up short pretty reliably. Each generation feels disappointed in its own way, though, and seems to require its own literature of disaffection. For many Americans who grew up in the nineteen-fifties, “The Catcher in the Rye” is the purest extract of that mood. Holden Caulfield is their sorrow king. Americans who grew up in later decades still read Salinger’s novel, but they have their own versions of his story, with different flavors of Weltschmerz—”Catcher in the Rye” rewrites, a literary genre all its own.
In art, as in life, the rich get richer. People generally read “The Catcher in the Rye” when they are around fourteen years old, usually because the book was given or assigned to them by people—parents or teachers—who read it when they were fourteen years old, because somebody gave or assigned it to them. The book keeps acquiring readers, in other words, not because kids keep discovering it but because grownups who read it when they were kids keep getting kids to read it. This seems crucial to making sense of its popularity. “The Catcher in the Rye” is a sympathetic portrait of a boy who refuses to be socialized which has become (among certain readers, anyway, for it is still occasionally banned in conservative school districts) a standard instrument of socialization. I was introduced to the book by my parents, people who, if they had ever imagined that I might, after finishing the thing, run away from school, smoke like a chimney, lie about my age in bars, solicit a prostitute, or use the word “goddam” in every third sentence, would (in the words of the story) have had about two hemorrhages apiece. Somehow, they knew this wouldn’t be the effect.
Supposedly, kids respond to “The Catcher in the Rye” because they recognize themselves in the character of Holden Caulfield. Salinger is imagined to have given voice to what every adolescent, or, at least, every sensitive, intelligent, middle-class adolescent, thinks but is too inhibited to say, which is that success is a sham, and that successful people are mostly phonies. Reading Holden’s story is supposed to be the literary equivalent of looking in a mirror for the first time. This seems to underestimate the originality of the book. Fourteen-year-olds, even sensitive, intelligent, middle-class fourteen-year-olds, generally do not think that success is a sham, and if they sometimes feel unhappy, or angry, or out of it, it’s not because they think most other people are phonies. The whole emotional burden of adolescence is that you don’t know why you feel unhappy, or angry, or out of it. The appeal of “The Catcher in the Rye,” what makes it addictive, is that it provides you with a reason. It gives a content to chemistry.
Holden talks like a teen-ager, and this makes it natural to assume that he thinks like a teen-ager as well. But like all the wise boys and girls in Salinger’s fiction—like Esmé and Teddy and the many brilliant Glasses—Holden thinks like an adult. No teen-ager (and very few grownups, for that matter) sees through other human beings as quickly, as clearly, or as unforgivingly as he does. Holden is a demon of verbal incision. He sums people up like a novelist:
He was always asking you to do him a big favor. You take a very handsome guy, or a guy that thinks he’s a real hot-shot, and they’re always asking you to do them a big favor. Just because they’re crazy about themselves, they think you’re crazy about them, too, and that you’re just dying to do them a favor. It’s sort of funny, in a way.
She was blocking up the whole goddam traffic in the aisle. You could tell she liked to block up a lot of traffic. This waiter was waiting for her to move out of the way, but she didn’t even notice him. It was funny. You could tell the waiter didn’t like her much, you could tell even the Navy guy didn’t like her much, even though he was dating her. And I didn’t like her much. Nobody did. You had to feel sort of sorry for her, in a way.
His name was George or something—I don’t even remember—and he went to Andover. Big, big deal. You should’ve seen him when old Sally asked him how he liked the play. He was the kind of a phony that have to give themselves room when they answer somebody’s question. He stepped back, and stepped right on the lady’s foot behind him. He probably broke every toe in her body. He said the play itself was no masterpiece, but that the Lunts, of course, were absolute angels. Angels. For Chrissake. Angels. That killed me.
”You had to feel sort of sorry for her, in a way.” The secret to Holden’s authority as a narrator is that he never lets anything stand by itself. He always tells you what to think. He has everyone pegged. That’s why he’s so funny. But The New Yorker’s editors were right: Holden isn’t an ordinary teen-ager—he’s a prodigy. He seems (and this is why his character can be so addictive) to have something that few people ever consistently attain: an attitude toward life.
The moral of the book can seem to be that Holden will outgrow his attitude, and this is probably the lesson that most of the ninth-grade teachers who assign “The Catcher in the Rye” hope to impart to their students—that alienation is just a phase. But people don’t outgrow Holden’s attitude, or not completely, and they don’t want to outgrow it, either, because it’s a fairly useful attitude to have. One goal of education is to teach people to want the rewards life has to offer, but another goal is to teach them a modest degree of contempt for those rewards, too. In American life, where—especially if you are a sensitive and intelligent member of the middle class—the rewards are constantly being advertised as yours for the taking, the feeling of disappointment is a lot more common than the feeling of success, and if we didn’t learn how not to care our failures would destroy us. Giving “The Catcher in the Rye” to your children is like giving them a layer of psychic insulation.

(Những hình ảnh về khoa học công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo)

Giọng nam: “Phát triển khoa học công nghệ sẽ giúp Việt Nam tiến bộ và tạo ra giá trị gia tăng cho kinh tế. Chúng ta cần phải áp dụng những công nghệ tiên tiến và đúng thời điểm để tận dụng tối đa tiềm năng kinh tế. Trí thông minh nhân tạo, robot, Blockchain hay Internet of Things là những xu hướng công nghệ mới được áp dụng và phát triển tại Việt Nam.”

(Âm nhạc và hình ảnh về sự phát triển kinh tế)

Giọng nữ: “Với các tầng lớp nhân dân luôn phấn đấu để cống hiến cho đất nước, Việt Nam đang phát triển nhanh chóng và có tốc độ tăng trưởng kinh tế ấn tượng. Thử thách lớn nhất của chúng ta là giữ vững tốc độ tăng trưởng này và tạo ra sự phát triển bền vững. Việt Nam đang từng bước đổi mới hệ thống kinh tế và xây dựng hạ tầng điện, giao thông, viễn thông, nước sạch để giảm tỉ lệ nghèo hơn nữa và đổi mới kinh tế tạo ra nhiều cơ hội hơn cho hàng triệu người Việt.”

(Âm nhạc và hình ảnh về sự đoàn kết của người dân)


Giọng nam: “Hãy kết nối các khối kinh tế trong khu vực và trên toàn thế giới để hưởng lợi từ các thỏa thuận thương mại tự do và phát triển hơn nữa. Hãy tiếp tục đẩy mạnh năng lực hợp tác và đào tạo để tạo ra sức mạnh cho các ngành kinh tế của chúng ta.”

(Những hình ảnh về cuộc sống đầy màu sắc và sinh động của người dân Việt Nam)

Giọng nữ: “Thật tuyệt vời khi chúng ta có một đất nước đầy màu sắc văn hóa và người dân thân thiện, giúp Việt Nam trở thành điểm đến du lịch hấp dẫn. Sự phát triển này sẽ mở ra nhiều cơ hội mới cho ngành du lịch, giúp tạo ra nhiều việc làm và thu nhập cho người dân.”

(Âm nhạc lạc quan và hình ảnh về hy vọng và tương lai)

Giọng nam: “Hy vọng của chúng ta là đưa Việt Nam phát triển thành một quốc gia với nền kinh tế mạnh mẽ, công bằng và bền vững trong tương lai. Với sự hỗ trợ và đóng góp của mỗi cá nhân trong cộng đồng, chúng ta có thể đạt được mục tiêu này. Hãy cùng nhau hướng tới tương lai rực rỡ và cơ hội mới.”

(Âm nhạc lạc quan và hình ảnh về cộng đồng đoàn kết trên khắp thế giới)

Giọng nữ: “Cảm ơn các bạn đã đến với phiên bản mới của chúng tôi về Việt Nam. Hãy cùng tiếp thêm sức mạnh cho cộng đồng Việt Nam trên khắp thế giới và tỏa sáng để đưa quốc gia của chúng ta phát triển hơn nữa. Vươn tới ngày mai, hãy cùng nhau vươn tới những thành công mới, tạo ra giá trị và thể hiện sức mạnh của chúng ta.”

Kịch bản kết thúc với cảnh những hình ảnh tràn đầy hy vọng về tương lai và những cộng đồng đoàn kết trên khắp thế giới. Âm nhạc lạc quan và ngọt ngào tiếp tục phát ra, khi khung hình được đóng lại.”

Rewriting the quantum-computer blueprint
An architecture for quantum computers based on parity is attracting money from government and industry.
Edwin Cartlidge
Twitter Facebook Email
A team of ParityQC researchers around a table discuss the architecture of quantum computing
ParityQC licenses the intellectual property for it's quantum-computing architecture to other companies.Credit: Elisabeth Fitsch

Parity Quantum Computing in Innsbruck, Austria, spun off from the University of Innsbruck, Austria, in 2020.

In 2013, Wolfgang Lechner had an idea that he thought was probably too good to be true: a mathematical trick that would change how quantum computers encode information. If it worked, he reasoned, it would be a big deal. Quantum computers can, in theory, perform certain calculations many times faster than conventional digital computers, but they are extremely sensitive to interference and are hard to scale up. Lechner’s brainwave was to provide these computers with an architecture based on the concept of ‘parity’. This could transform them from small laboratory devices into vast, commercial machines capable of solving problems that are currently intractable.


Read more about The Spinoff Prize

Lechner, a physicist at the University of Innsbruck in Austria, discussed the proposal with a colleague, but they managed to persuade themselves that it was a non-starter. Over the next two years he kept turning the idea over in his mind, and says it became an obsession. Eventually, at 3 a.m. in a hotel room, he had a flash of inspiration that could mean his parity-based approach should work after all.

He quickly filed a patent and, just six months later, received an offer for the intellectual property from a large technology company. (Lechner declined to reveal the company or the size of the offer.) This told him that the architecture had commercial potential, and that it might be better to try to reap the rewards directly. So he and his colleagues at the University of Innsbruck decided to reject the offer and set up a spin-off company. ParityQC launched in 2020, and has been named a finalist in The Spinoff Prize 2023.

Three years on from its set-up, the company now employs about 30 people. It has landed sizeable contracts from high-tech manufacturers and from governments — with one deal alone worth several tens of millions of euros. According to Lechner’s co-chief-executive Magdalena Hauser, this early success — combined with grants from the European Union and the governments of Austria and Germany — has meant that the company has avoided having to drum up support from venture capitalists. “We made revenue from the start,” says Hauser.

Busting limits
Quantum computers owe their calculating prowess to certain quantum phenomena of atomic-scale objects. These computers encode data in the form of qubits, which can exist as 0 and 1 at the same time — unlike conventional bits, which exist as only one or the other. Multiple qubits can be entangled to generate all possible values from a string of 0s and 1s simultaneously, enabling parallel processing that is not possible with classical computers.


Part of Nature Outlook: The Spinoff Prize 2023

But qubits are fragile. Their states can be disrupted by the slightest amount of heat or other interference. Their durability varies according to the kind of physical qubit used — ions, neutral atoms, superconducting circuits or quantum dots. They might remain intact for a few seconds if they are perfectly isolated or might disappear after milliseconds if they interact with other qubits during a calculation.

A second major issue for quantum computing is the spatial properties of qubits. The physical processes that link qubits to one another usually occur only over very short distances, such as the overlap of two electron clouds around atomic nuclei or the connection of two superconducting circuits. This means that each qubit typically interacts only with its nearest neighbours, rather than qubits farther away.

ParityQC’s architecture helps quantum computers to deal with both limitations. It does so by changing how the data are encoded in qubits. Rather than representing the values of individual logical qubits — as specified by the program being executed — physical qubits instead record the relationship between pairs of logical qubits in terms of parity. If the qubits in a pair have the same value, then the parity is 1; if the values are different, then the parity is 0 (See ‘Blueprint for quantum computing’).

Blueprint for quantum computing
Credit: Alisdair MacDonald

This change in encoding to a system based on parity transforms all operations involving several qubits, no matter how far apart they are, into the equivalent of local interactions. That eliminates the need for interactions over long distances. And operations can be carried out on all qubits in a computer simultaneously, maximizing the complexity of calculations that can be performed in the brief period during which qubits remain intact.

A commercial mindset
Since dreaming up the parity architecture1, Lechner and his colleagues at ParityQC and the University of Innsbruck have gone on to have dozens of papers published that elaborate the scheme. In one of the most recent2, they have proposed a specific set of operations, or gates, that rely on parity encoding and have confirmed3 that this set would speed up several of the most important quantum algorithms devised so far. These include an algorithm that would allow quantum computers to find the prime factors of large numbers, posing a threat to Internet encryption schemes that rely on the difficulty of such calculations.

To turn this knowledge into revenue, ParityQC licenses its intellectual property to hardware developers so that they can build chips incorporating the architecture. According to Hauser, the company has sold licences to Japanese electronics giant NEC to produce a superconducting quantum chip, and has entered several consortia that were set up in response to the German government investing €2 billion (US$2.2 billion) to fund the development of quantum technologies.

Notably, the company jointly received an €83-million contract awarded by the German Aerospace Center in Cologne to build ion-trap computers. Along with manufacturers eleQtron in Siegen, Germany, and NXP Semiconductors in Eindhoven, the Netherlands, it won the contract to build a 10-qubit demonstration computer and then develop modular and scalable devices. (This type of computer is also being developed by another The Spinoff Prize 2023 finalist, Alpine Quantum Technologies, although Alpine is not part of ParityQC’s collaboration.)

Sue Sundstrom, a start-up coach based in Clevedon, UK, and a judge for The Spinoff Prize 2023, is impressed by what she describes as ParityQC’s analysis of “how previously radically different technologies have been able to get into the market and make money”. She notes a parallel with Arm in Cambridge, UK, a firm which started selling blueprints of chips for reduced-instruction set computers in the 1980s. She also praises the hiring of people with commercial expertise. “For quantum companies that is quite rare,” she says.

Fellow judge Emily MacKay, who is a technology strategist at Siemens Energy and is based in Cambridge, UK, applauds ParityQC’s efforts to make its architecture scalable and applicable to various types of hardware. “Their research approach is future-proofing as far as possible,” she says. (Her comments on ParityQC do not necessarily reflect the views of Siemens Energy.)

But MacKay adds that the company faces an “elephant in the room” — having to decide whether to compete or collaborate with the world’s biggest provider of cloud computing, Amazon Web Services. Lechner says that ParityQC would be “an ideal supplier” to the larger firm, arguing that its parity architecture is well suited to Amazon — which plans to build quantum computers that mitigate errors, partly in hardware and partly through software. “We are not in contact [with Amazon] at the moment but would be happy to [be],” he says.

However, not all specialists are convinced that the parity architecture will achieve its desired results, at least when it comes to solving optimization problems (such as maximizing the return from a financial portfolio or minimizing the distance travelled by goods vehicles). Itay Hen, a numerical physicist at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, questions whether a quantum computer fitted with the architecture could solve such problems more quickly than would a classical computer — given what he says is the absence of any quantum algorithm that guarantees such an outcome. “Even if we had the perfect quantum computer, we still wouldn’t know whether it is better than a laptop,” he says.

Lechner acknowledges that there is no general proof showing that quantum computers have an advantage over their classical counterparts when it comes to optimization problems. But he is confident that at some point in the next few years — perhaps by around 2030 — the parity architecture will enable a quantum computer to pass this milestone for one or more problems, with classically impossible optimization made possible by new algorithms that emerge. “That is our dream,” Lechner says, “and the target we are working towards.”

كشف تقرير جديد صادر عن الأمم المتحدة وشركائها أن العالم ليس على المسار الصحيح لتحقيق الهدف السابع من أهداف التنمية المستدامة، المتعلق بضمان حصول الجميع على طاقة موثوقة ومستدامة وبتكلفة ميسورة.

ويحذر التقرير المعنون "تتبع الهدف السابع من أهداف التنمية المستدامة: تقرير تقدم الطاقة"، من أن الجهود الحالية ليست كافية لتحقيق الهدف المنشود بحلول عام 2030، على الرغم من بعض التقدم المحرز.

وصدر التقرير بالتعاون بين الوكالة الدولية للطاقة، والوكالة الدولية للطاقة المتجددة، وشعبة الإحصاءات في الأمم المتحدة، والبنك الدولي، ومنظمة الصحة العالمية.

وأكد التقرير إحراز بعض التقدم في عناصر محددة يتضمنها الهدف السابع، بما في ذلك على سبيل المثال زيادة معدل استخدام مصادر الطاقة المتجددة في قطاع الطاقة، إلا أن هناك المزيد الذي يتعين القيام به بحلول الموعد النهائي.

الهدف السابع من أهداف التنمية المستدامة يُعنى بضمان الحصول على طاقة حديثة وموثوقة ومستدامة وبأسعار معقولة. وقال معدو التقرير إن الهدف يتضمن الوصول الشامل إلى الكهرباء ووقود الطهي النظيفين، ومضاعفة المستويات التاريخية لتحسينات الكفاءة، وزيادة حصة مصادر الطاقة المتجددة في مزيج الطاقة العالمي بشكل كبير.

فوائد تحقيق الهدف السابع
بلوغ الهدف السابع سيكون له تأثير عميق وإيجابي على صحة الناس ورفاههم، مما يساعد على حمايتهم من المخاطر البيئية والاجتماعية مثل تلوث الهواء، وتوسيع نطاق الوصول إلى الرعاية والخدمات الصحية الأولية.

ومن المتوقع أن تحفز أزمة الطاقة العالمية، التي تفاقمت بسبب الحرب في أوكرانيا، نشر مصادر الطاقة المتجددة وتحسين كفاءة الطاقة، حيث تعزز بعض الحكومات الاستثمار في هذا المجال.

ومع ذلك، تُظهر تقديرات الوكالة الدولية للطاقة المتجددة أن التدفقات المالية العامة الدولية لدعم الطاقة النظيفة في البلدان منخفضة ومتوسطة الدخل قد تناقصت حتى قبل جائحة كورونا، وأن التمويل يقتصر على عدد صغير من البلدان.

وشدد مؤلفو التقرير على ضرورة إجراء إصلاح هيكلي للتمويل الدولي العام وتحديد فرص جديدة لفتح الاستثمارات من أجل تحقيق هدف التنمية المستدامة السابع.

كما وجد التقرير أن الديون المتزايدة وارتفاع أسعار الطاقة يفاقم من مشاكل الوصول الشامل إلى مصادر الطهي والكهرباء النظيفين.

أوجه التقصير
وتقدر التوقعات الحالية أن 1.9 مليار شخص سيكونون بدون مرافق طهي نظيفة، وأن 660 مليون شخص لن يحصلوا على الكهرباء في عام 2030، إذا ما استمر الوضع الراهن.

وأشار التقرير إلى أن هذه الفجوات ستؤثر سلبا على صحة السكان الأكثر ضعفا حول العالم، وستؤدي إلى تسريع تغير المناخ.

ووفقا لمنظمة الصحة العالمية، فإن 3.2 مليون شخص يلقون حتفهم كل عام بسبب الأمراض الناجمة عن استخدام أشكال الوقود والتقنيات الملوثة، والتي تزيد من التعرض لمستويات سامة من تلوث الهواء المنزلي.

حماية الأجيال المقبلة
وقال الدكتور تيدروس أدهانوم غيبريسوس، المدير العام لمنظمة الصحة العالمية، إن الاستثمار في الحلول النظيفة والمتجددة لدعم الوصول الشامل هو السبيل لإحداث تغيير حقيقي. وشدد على أنه يمكن لتقنيات الطهي النظيفة في المنازل والكهرباء الموثوقة في مرافق الرعاية الصحية أن تلعب دورا حاسما في حماية صحة السكان الأكثر ضعفا.

وقال: "يجب علينا حماية الأجيال المقبلة من خلال العمل الآن".

من جهته، أكد ستيفان شوينفست، مدير شعبة الإحصاءات في الأمم المتحدة، إنه على الرغم من التباطؤ الأخير، انخفض عدد الأشخاص الذين لا تصل إليهم الكهرباء إلى النصف تقريبا خلال العقد الماضي، من 1.1 مليار في عام 2010 إلى 675 مليونا عام 2021.

وقال شوينفست: "ومع ذلك، يجب بذل جهود واتخاذ تدابير إضافية على وجه السرعة لضمان عدم تخلف أفقر الناس الذين يصعب الوصول إليهم عن الركب. لتحقيق الوصول الشامل بحلول عام 2030، يجب على المجتمع الإنمائي توسيع نطاق استثمارات الطاقة النظيفة وتكثيف دعمه للسياسات".

وسيتم تقديم التقرير إلى كبار صانعي القرار خلال المنتدى السياسي رفيع المستوى حول التنمية المستدامة في 11 يوليو المقبل، قبيل انعقاد قمة أهداف التنمية المستدامة الثانية في سبتمبر بنيويورك.

وحث مؤلفو التقرير المجتمع الدولي وصانعي السياسات على حماية المكاسب في سياق تحقيق الهدف السابع من أهداف التنمية المستدامة، والمضي قدما في الإصلاحات الهيكلية، واستمرار التركيز الاستراتيجي على البلدان الضعيفة التي تحتاج إلى أكبر قدر من الدعم.

import random
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class Book:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        Initializes a Book object with a randomly generated title, author, and pages.
        """
        self.title = self.generate_word().capitalize()
        self.author = self.generate_word().capitalize() + ' ' + self.generate_word().capitalize()
        self.pages = []
        for i in range(100):
            self.pages.append(self.generate_page())

    def generate_word(self):
        """
        Generates a random word with alternating consonants and vowels.

        :return: Randomly generated word.
        :rtype: str
        """
        vowels = 'аеёиоуэюя'
        consonants = 'бвгджзйклмнпрстфхцчшщ'
        length = random.randint(2, 8)
        word = ""
        for i in range(length):
            if i % 2 == 0:
                word += random.choice(consonants)
            else:
                word += random.choice(vowels)
        return word

    def generate_page(self):
        """
        Generates a random page consisting of multiple random words.

        :return: Randomly generated page.
        :rtype: str
        """
        text = []
        for i in range(random.randint(5, 20)):
            text.append(self.generate_word())
        return ' '.join(text)

class Library:
    def __init__(self):
        """
        Initializes a Library object with a list of 10 randomly generated Book objects.
        """
        self.books = []
        for i in range(10):
            self.books.append(Book())

    def find_book(self, title):
        """
        Finds a Book object in the library with the specified title.

        :param title: Title of book to search for.
        :type title: str
        :return: Book object with specified title, or None if not found.
        :rtype: Book or None
        """
        for book in self.books:
            if book.title.lower() == title.lower():
                return book
        return None

    def find_page(self, title, page_number):
        """
        Finds a specific page in a Book object with the specified title.

        :param title: Title of book to search for.
        :type title: str
        :param page_number: Number of page to search for.
        :type page_number: int
        :return: Text of specified page, or "Invalid page number" if page number is out of range,
                 or "Book not found" if book with specified title is not found.
        :rtype: str
        """
        book = self.find_book(title)
        if book:
            if page_number >= 1 and page_number <= len(book.pages):
                return book.pages[page_number - 1]
            else:
                logger.error("Invalid page number for book: %s", title)
                return "Invalid page number"
        else:
            logger.error("Book not found: %s", title)
            return "Book not found"

# Example usage

# Print all books in library
for book in library.books:

Akshay Kumar tweeted, “Heartbreaking to see the visuals from the tragic train accident in Odisha. Praying for the speedy recovery of the injured. My thoughts and condolences to the families of the affected during this difficult time. Om Shanti”

In the worship of ghosts and ancestors, the Shang Dynasty merchants not only worshiped the ancestors of their own families, such as ancestors, kings, and mothers, but also worshiped those renowned ministers who had made remarkable contributions. The Shang Dynasty kings and their nobles held sacrificial ceremonies for these deceased ministers. Сначала мы рассмотрим историю возникновения науки «тафсир». Эта наука появилась сразу после того, как Коран был ниспослан, и первым его исследователем стал пророк Мухаммад. Сначала он объяснял значение предписаний из Небесной книги своей семье, а затем – всем остальным людям. Пророк Мухаммад не мог всегда руководить мусульманской общиной и решать ее проблемы, и поэтому он всегда поддерживал их самостоятельное исследование Корана и принятие решений, опираясь на айаты Корана. Например, в известном хадисе Му’аза ибн-Джабаля, пророк одобрил использование иджтихада при поиске ответов на трудные вопросы без явного текстового указания. Этот иджтихад в дальнейшем расширился до такой степени, что возникло новое направление в комментировании Корана, основанное на не полностью достоверном тексте, а на личных выводах ученого (тафсир би-р-ра’ий). Как отмечает Салахов А.М., в эпоху основателя ислама Мухаммада сам Коран не был истолкован полностью, так как преимущественно истолковывались лишь «неясные места», которых со временем становилось все больше «по мере отдаления от времени ниспослания Откровения» [1]
После ухода пророка Мухаммада, знатоки тафсира продолжали свою деятельность. Среди них абу-Бакр ас-Сиддик, Умар ибн-Хаттаб, Усман ибн-Аффан, Али ибн-Абу-Талиб, Абдуллах ибн-Аббас, Абдуллах ибн-Масуд, Убай ибн-Кааб и многие другие. Они передавая свои знания и умения ученикам, делая вклад в область комментирования Корана. Начало письменной фиксации тафсира, по сообщению исследователей, происходится на конец эпохи омейядов – начало эпохи аббасидов, которые встречаются в формате отдельных записей в сочинениях по хадисам (либо один из его разделов). В тафсирах, приводимые комментарии были подтверждены цепочкой передатчиков, нисходящей от пророка Мухаммада, его сподвижников, последователей и их последователей. Однако со временем, в работах более поздних толкователей Корана, цепочки передатчиков стали опускаться [1].
Стоит отметить, что существует несколько видов тафсиров, а именно токования основанные на преданиях – ат-тафсир би-ль-ма сур), а также, основанные на суждении -ат-тафсир би-р-ра й), «которые образуют два основных корпуса мусульманской экзегетики» [1].
В последствии сложилось три школы толкования Корана, к которым относили всех ученых данной сферы, среди которых можно выделить Мекканскую, Мединскую и Иракскую школу. Многие их представители являлись таби унами, учениками Пророка Мухаммада и его последователями.
Мекканская школа считается самой информированной, потому что ее основатель, ибн- Аббас, был автором большинства комментариев к Корану и обучал многих известных толкователей, таких как Муджахид, Ата и Икрима.
В Мединской школе учителями были многие сподвижники Пророка, включая Убай ибн-Ка б, среди учеников которого были Мухаммад ибн-Ка б аль-Карзи, абу-ль-Алийя ар-Рияхи, и Зайд ибн-Аслам. 
Иракская школа основана ибн-Мас удом и имела два основных центра - Басру и Куфу, где проходили обучение и передача знаний. Известными толкователями, которые обучались у ибн-Мас уда, были аль-Хасан аль-Басри, Масрук ибну-ль-Аджда’ и Ибрахим ан-Наха.
Иногда толкователи Корана не могут достичь единства в интерпретации конкретного айата, что может быть обусловлено различными причинами, включая следующие:
- Внешние: игнорирование цепочки передачи истории; использование сомнительных источников, таких как аль-Исраилият; сознательное искажение, возможно, основанное на предубеждении или других скрытых мотивах.
- Внутренние: чистая ошибка в понимании; интерпретация, основанная на невольном предубеждении; многозначность смыслов, заключенных в откровениях Аллаха.

translate following for IELTS writing task 2 with score expectation over than 8: 人们常常对是否应该赋予孩子额外的责任而争论不休，比如是否应该要求他们课余时间帮助家务劳动或者一些工作相关的任务，或者是否应该允许他们在学校环境之外随心所欲的度过闲暇时间。在这篇文章中，我将对两种观点进行讨论，并提出我自己对这个问题的看法。 一方面，支持赋予孩子们额外责任的人们认为，给孩子分配课外责任可以尽早培养对时间管理和职业道德重要性的意识。通过协助家务劳动或者帮助完成合适的工作任务，孩子们可以学习基本的职业技能，特别是团队合作、面对难题时的解决方案和心态调整以及努力工作的价值认同。此外，拥有责任感可以培养孩子的自豪感和成就感，从而增强他们的自尊心，这些品质往往在一个人的成功中不可或缺。而且，让孩子参与家庭的日常工作也能加强家庭内部的团结意识。 而另一方面，相反观点的支持者断言，应该让孩子在学业之外尽可能享受童年的自由。这是因为，年轻人正处于人生重要决断的早起，需要更多的时间去发掘自己的兴趣以及自己的才能所在，这对他们未来的个人发展和人生决策有着至关重要的作用。而且，参加体育、艺术等休闲活动抑或是与朋友共度时光，也有助于孩子的情绪健康和精神放松，这与在学业方面的成功同等重要。此外，通过有更多的时间沉浸在各种愉快的体验中，孩子们能更好的应对生活中的挑战以适应不断变换的环境。 于我而言，在两种观点中保持一种适当的平衡是孩子培养过程中更为理想的一种方式。诚然让孩子尽早的具备责任感和发展基本的生活技能至关重要，但是我们也应当注意到每个人个人兴趣和整体心理健康的重要性。给予与年龄相匹配的任务并留出时间进行休闲活动的灵活安排对年轻人大有裨益，因为这不仅使他们意识到努力工作的价值，同时也有助于他们自我探索和享受生活的乐趣。 总之，无论是分配额外的责任，还是让孩子享受校外的生活，都各有优点。因此，考虑个人需求和兴趣的平衡才是最有可能为儿童成长提供更全面机会的思考方向。

Write a page of dot point notes that would allow someone to rewrite this entire essay using these dot points (include all important information). MAKE SURE to retain ALL quotes used throughout the essay as individual dot points (everything that is surrounded by ""): 
Introduction:
"Rita and Shawshank Redemption" (“Rita”) is a novella authored by Stephen King and published in 1982; and serves as the basis for Frank Darabont's 1994 film adaptation, "The Shawshank Redemption" (Shawshank). The hypotext conveys the perspective of a prisoner named Red telling the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongfully convicted to serve three consecutive life sentences, as he endures prison hardships, overcomes obstacles, and masterminds his escape. Darabont recreates this film while maintaining “a certain level of faithfulness to respect the original work” by representing the original ideas, themes and concepts in “a fresh take of the source material”, providing “a new and refreshing interpretation” of these themes by distilling and supplementing certain language, stylistic devices, and text conventions in King's novella during the adaptation process to further shape their meaning and enhance the audience’s response, enabling a discussion of the comparisons between the hypotext and the hypertext.
Body Paragraph 1 (Main themes/ideas – innocence-guilt):
“Rita” and Shawshank construct the ideas of innocence and guilt, respectively, as one of the main themes in their texts. In the novella, Stephen King represents the concept of innocence by constructing a scene where Andy Dufresne is wrongfully convicted to three consecutive life sentences for murdering his wife and a professional golfer with whom she was discovered to be engaged in infidelity. The audience is first introduced to Red, the narrator of Andy’s story, who immediately establishes rapport with the audience by declaring, “I came to Shawshank when I was just twenty, and I am one of the few people in our happy little family who is willing to own up to what he did. I committed murder”. This shows the audience that Red is proclaiming to be rightfully placed in prison, revealing his intentions to be pure when he claims Andy is truly innocent, making the audience believe in him. Frank Darabont remains faithful to the original work but also expresses this opening in an alternative way by opening a question in the audience’s minds regarding Andy’s innocence. In the film, Darabont represents Andy as drunk and dishevelled, sitting in his car at night with a gun. This scene switches to Andy standing in court with a grim expression, being questioned about the murder of his wife. Darabont has clearly distilled certain aspects of the novella scene in the adaptation process, such as excising Red’s introduction of himself as the narrator of Andy’s story. This raises a question regarding Andy’s innocence, inviting a greater audience response as the theme of guilt is amplified through uncertainty. Darabont adds a supplementation to the novella by coupling Andy’s innocent responses in court with visuals suggesting he is guilty. This allows a fresh take on the source material and thus shapes the meaning of the story by focusing the audience’s attention on whether Andy is innocent or guilty. This supports Conner McCallion’s statement of film adaptations remaining faithful to the original work but changing enough aspects to allow a fresh take on the source material and make room for a new and refreshing interpretation.

Body Paragraph 2 (Main theme/idea – corruption/injustice):
“Rita” explores the idea of corruption as one of the main themes in the novella. Darabont’s adaptation, Shawshank, alters the original structure to allow a fresh take on the idea of injustice as one of the main themes in the film. In the novella, Stephen King depicts the idea of corruption when it is revealed to Andy that Tommy Williams is moved to a low-security prison facility by Warden Norton in exchange for maintaining his silence regarding the true murderer of Andy’s wife, Elmo Blatch. While talking to Andy, Norton discloses that Tommy Williams “is no longer an inmate of this facility.” Red, the narrator, clarifies to the audience that a deal was made between Norton and Williams, that he could have “a chance to live life like a normal man, at least on the weekends” if he kept silent on Blatch. This effectively shows the audience the corruption that pervades the authority figures within Shawshank and gives the audience a profound insight into Tommy’s lack of morality. Darabont remains faithful to the original work in removing Tommy Williams from the story but also expresses his character arc differently to focus on injustice. In the film, Red is told Tommy’s revelation right alongside Andy himself, which differs from the novella where Red finds out later. This change helps heighten the audience’s emotional impact of the revelation, enhancing their experience. Darabont also chooses to keep Tommy a pure-hearted character, and his arc in the story ends with him dying at Norton’s hand instead of being relocated. A guard takes Williams outside to Norton, who gives him a cigarette and asks him, “Is what you said to Andy true?” Williams confirms and, soon after, gets shot by Hadley from a guard tower. The scene culminates with Norton towering over the lifeless body of Williams, a purposeful decision by Darabont to preserve Williams’ morality and amplify the prisoners’ powerlessness inside Shawshank’s walls, enhancing the idea of injustice. Darabont has also distilled certain narrative elements of the novella during the adaptation process to enhance the story and the audience’s experience. More than two dozen prisoners passed their tests through the resources available in the library, but Darabont selectively places the focus on Andy’s tutoring of Williams. This focuses the audience’s attention on his character development, which invites a greater audience response as his eventual death by Norton further amplifies the theme of injustice. Williams’ murder scene is a complete supplementation added by Darabont, showcasing the lengths to which Norton is willing to reach to continue using Andy for his covert and shady business operations. This deviation from the source material allows a fresh take on the source material and enriches the meaning of the story by further antagonising Norton’s character, delivering the audience a more satisfying payoff when Norton meets his end. This also supports Conner McCallion’s statement of film adaptations, remaining faithful to the original work while changing enough aspects to allow for a fresh take on the source material, making room for a new and refreshing interpretation and, in turn, enhancing the overall viewing experience.

Body Paragraph 3 (Main theme/idea – redemption/hope):
Both “Rita” and Shawshank explore the themes of redemption and hope in their texts. Andy's escape in the novella represents King's construction of these ideas. After twenty long years of painstakingly chipping away at his cell wall with a rock hammer, Andy’s meticulously planned escape eventually comes to fruition as the tunnel he creates leads to his escape through a long sewerage pipe. This serves as a testament to his everlasting hope and redemption from the forces that led to his detainment, becoming the story’s climax and filling the audience with satisfaction and awe. The theme of redemption is evident during this scene in “Rita” through various quotes and text conventions throughout the text. At the beginning of Red’s recount of Andy’s escape, he says, “In 1975, Andy Dufresne escaped from Shawshank. He hasn't been recaptured, and I don't think he ever will be.” He introduces the idea of redemption through Andy’s escape and shows that despite the odds, it was possible to break free from the imprisonment Andy faced. When Red states, “I think there’s a man down in Zihuatanejo, Mexico named Peter Stevens. Probably running a very small new hotel in this year of our lord 1977”, he foreshadows that Andy has built a new life for himself, implying he has freed himself from the injustice he served in prison and symbolising redemption. Andy’s escape also has a profound impact on everyone else in the prison, as seen when Red says, “I do know that there were twenty-eight cons listening to Norton’s little dust-up with Rich Gonyar that evening as the last of the light faded from a dull late winter sky… And by God, it almost seemed to me that somewhere I could hear Andy Dufresne laughing.” This tension between Warden Norton and the rest of the prison staff highlights the power of Andy’s escape as it disrupts the established order and challenges the wardens’ authority. This inspires hope in the prisoners and provides a sense of redemption for their suffering. The use of detailed descriptions of Andy’s cell and the prison staff’s reactions to his escape also emphasises the significance of Andy’s escape and redemption. Andy is never recaptured, and the story ends hinting at Andy’s new life in Mexico, which inspires the audience and serves as a testament to Andy’s redemption. Frank Darabont remains faithful to King’s original work in his portrayal of redemption and the power of hope but also expresses the ending in an alternative way by showing the audience Andy’s escape. In the novella, Red simply narrates what his escape may have looked like, but the film brings the audience right alongside Andy’s escape, enhancing their experience and amplifying the theme of redemption. Darabont’s distillation of the three wardens into Warden Norton further increases the audience’s satisfaction when he meets his end in the film, giving the audience a sense of closure and freedom from Andy’s problems. The final scene depicts Andy and Red united in Zihuatanejo, symbolising the culmination of Andy’s pursuit of freedom right alongside his best friend, Red. Darabont purposely shows this scene to illustrate to the audience the vision that constantly gave Andy hope throughout the story, from the sand in between their toes, the bright sky and beach colours, the lack of anyone around, and an endless horizon stretching for miles with no walls. This completely contrasts with the colours and theme of Shawshank, making for a perfect symbolisation of Andy’s redemption. Darabont has changed the meaning through the adaptation process by using visuals and amplifying the effects of Andy’s escape, enhancing the key ideas of hope and redemption.

Conclusion:
In adapting "Rita and Shawshank Redemption" into the film "The Shawshank Redemption," Frank Darabont remains faithful to respect the original work while successfully manipulating language, stylistic devices, and text conventions to express important ideas and themes in alternative ways. This allows for a new and refreshing interpretation, and a paratext from Jason Fraley affirms the changes made and their impact on the story. Posted on October 3rd, 2011, Jason says, “A lot of people are in prisons of relationships, of jobs they hate, of lives unfulfilled, and have given up hope, and what this movie was saying to them was it might take a while, it might take some time, but there is a light at the end of the tunnel. And if you have the patience and the belief, you can make it there.” The reason why this film continues to resonate with audiences today is due to the fact that many people may have their own individual problems in life, similar to Shawshank, but Andy’s story inspires hope in the audience, allowing them to relate to and better engage with the material.

Give me a summary for the following essay: •	International Segmentation and Targeting strategy – POINT 6

	Stage 1: Market Segmentation

In the first stage, El-Wahy will identify different segments within the Tunisian market. Some potential segments include:

1. Expatriate Egyptians living in Tunisia who might be seeking a taste of home.
2. Local Tunisians who enjoy trying various international cuisines, especially Middle Eastern cuisines similar to their own.
3. Tourists from Egypt as well as other countries who are interested in trying authentic Egyptian food.
4. Business clientele and local companies looking for a unique dining experience for meetings or events.

Stage 2: Market Targeting

El-Wahy should adopt a differentiated marketing strategy, in which different marketing mixes are designed for each segment. The rationale for choosing this strategy is to cater to the unique needs of each segment and provide a more personalized experience for customers, ultimately leading to higher customer satisfaction and loyalty.

Segment 1: Expatriate Egyptians
El-Wahy should target this segment by offering authentic Egyptian dishes and traditional flavors. Marketing efforts should emphasize nostalgia and the connection to Egypt. Strategies could include targeted social media and outreach through Egyptian community associations in Tunisia.

Segment 2: Local Tunisians
El-Wahy should target this segment by showcasing the diverse menu and unique Egyptian flavors. The restaurant can emphasize the use of fresh and high-quality ingredients. Marketing efforts may include local TV ads, billboards, and food events.

Segment 3: Tourists
This segment can be targeted by promoting the unique dining experience and the opportunity to try traditional Egyptian cuisine. Collaborations with tour operators and hotels in Tunisia can help in attracting tourists to the restaurant.

Segment 4: Business clientele and local companies
El-Wahy should offer both on-site and off-site services for this segment, such as private dining rooms and catering. The restaurant can tailor its menu offerings to accommodate specific business preferences and budgets. Networking events and partnerships with local business organizations can help tap into this market.

Stage 3: Market Positioning
Having chosen the segments to target, El-Wahy must create a clear and unique brand image in the minds of customers from each segment. For expatriates and tourists, the positioning should emphasize the authenticity and connection to Egypt. For local Tunisians and business clientele, the focus should be on the unique dining experience, high-quality ingredients, and excellent customer service.

In conclusion, adopting a differentiated marketing strategy will allow El-Wahy to effectively cater to the different needs of each segment within the Tunisian market, leading to increased customer satisfaction and ultimately, business success.

Поднявшись на вершину гор, Тэллиен познакомился с гномом по имени Гроган, который рассказал ему об уникальной карте, указывающей путь к древнему храму. Именно там он сможет найти грифона.

Тэллиен и Гроган отправились к храму, в поисках грифона. По пути их ждало множество новых приключений и испытаний, но они не остановились.

После долгих путешествий, Тэллиен и Гроган наконец-то обнаружили храм. Он был старый и разрушенный. Однако, беда не закончилась, их преследовали бандиты, которые тоже желали завладеть грифоном.

Быстро забравшись на потайную полку храма, где находился грифон, Тэллиен решил, что гном останется у выхода, чтобы обезопасить их и не допустить, чтобы враги их настигли. Тэллиен остался один.

Осмотревшись внутри храма, он увидел грифона, который сразу же заподозрил в нем врага и начал нападать на него. Тэллиен замедлил птицу своим волшебством и начал говорить с ним, пытаясь успокоить зверя. Вскоре грифон успокоился и подошел к Тэллиену.

В течение многих дней они занимались дрессировкой грифона, заданием было приручить его и сделать его подчиненным Тэллиену. После многих дней Тэллиен наконец успешно приручил грифона и улетел на нем до своей эльфийской деревни.

Тэллиен не мог поверить, что эта мечта оказалась реальностью. Его любовь и уважение к зверю выше всего, и теперь грифон охраняет его и деревню, служа верой и правдой.

Задача преследования или уклонения сопровождала человека с самых древних времен. От охоты на животных в лесу, до спасения от них же. В наше время эта задача не потеряла своей актуальности, люди все так же преследуют и уклоняются, но уже чаще ради развлечения. Та же детская игра «Пятнашки», в своей сути является соревнованием в алгоритмах преследования и уклонения.
Задачи преследования и уклонения разделяют на две основных формулировки задачи, Дискретную и Непрерывную. 
Дискретная формулировка
В дискретной формулировке задач окружающая среда строится как граф. В такой формулировки преследователи и уклоняющиеся перемещаются по графу. На каждом из ходов преследования каждая из групп, преследователей и уклоняющихся, находится в узле графа и имеют варианты оставаться на том же узле или перемещаться по ребрам в другие узлы. В такой формулировке часто ставится задача поиска минимального количества преследователя для поимки всех уклоняющихся за минимальное количество времени, за минимально возможное количество ходов и так далее. 
Непрерывная формулировка
При такой формулировки задач окружающая среда строится геометрически, принимая форму евклидовой плоскости или другого многообразия. В данной формулировке преследователи и уклоняющиеся перемешаются по плоскости окружающей среды. При этой формулировке часто ставится задача оптимального достижения цели, для преследователя достижение уклоняющегося, а для уклоняющегося успешное уклонение от преследователя.

Как говорилось ранее, задачи преследования и уклонения не потеряли актуальности со временем, а наоборот стали более актуальны. Это связано с развитием технологий. Так, к примеру, алгоритмы преследования активно используются для создания искусственного интеллекта неигровым персонажам видеоигр. Так же алгоритмы преследования и уклонения используются для управления различными дронами. И даже используются в Геоинформационных системах, что говорит о широком распространении алгоритмов. 
В современном мире важную роль играет компьютерное моделирование в виртуальной визуальной среде, для тестирование различных продуктов. Этим и актуальностью задач преследования и уклонения, определятся необходимость создания среды моделирования для данных алгоритмов.
Объект исследования: Алгоритмы преследования и уклонения
Цель: Создание на платформе Unity реалистичной модели антагонистического процесса преследования.
Задачи:
1.	Анализ предметной области (Анализ алгоритмов преследования и уклонения для выделения параметров модели)
2.	Создание модели на языке C#
3.	Реализация визуального представления модели на платформе Unity

The study aimed to determine the epidemiology of traumatic spine injuries in Kashan, Iran. It was a cross-sectional study that included 986 patients with traumatic spine injuries admitted to Shahid Beheshti hospital of Kashan University of Medical Sciences from 2014 to 2017. The majority of the patients were male (77%) and aged 15-30 years. Traffic accidents were the most common mechanism of injury (35.2%) followed by falls (26.95%). The lumbar section was the most common site of injury. The rate of spinal cord injury was 2.63% and the mortality rate was 2.3%. The study highlights the importance of understanding the epidemiology of traumatic spine injuries in order to create appropriate preventative measures.
16: This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 206 patients with cervical spine and cord injuries admitted to a trauma center in Shiraz, Iran. The majority of patients were male and the mean age was 37.2 years. The most common fracture location was C6 vertebra, with the upper cervical spine (C0-C1-C2) being affected in 64 cases and the lower in 205. Concomitant injuries included brain, lung, and abdominal injuries, as well as fractures of the face, skull, and other parts of the spine. Treatment options varied, with non-operative management being most common, followed by anterior and posterior decompression, fixation, and fusion. The mortality rate was 7.3%, with factors such as longer hospital stay, brain and lung injury, and cord injury associated with a higher risk of death. Patients with associate injuries (AOI) had a higher risk of death compared to those without AOI.
17: The study analyzed data from 127 patients with traumatic spinal cord injuries (TSCI) due to motor vehicle accidents (MVA) at Poursina Hospital, Iran between March 2015 and March 2018. The mean age of patients was 38.27 years, and 78% of the patients were male. Most accidents involved car/pickup truck collisions in urban areas with 48.8% of patients being car passengers and 32.3% being motorcyclists. SCIs were predominantly cervical and lumbar, with safety devices rarely used. The majority of patients had a Glasgow Comma Scale (GCS) of ≥13, and only a few had cardiovascular or respiratory diseases. Complications were rare, but pain was moderate. Good recovery was noted in 91.2% of patients upon discharge, with two patients being discharged with their consent.
18: The study aimed to describe the characteristics and outcomes of cervical spinal column and spinal cord injuries in patients admitted to Rajaee Trauma Hospital over a 30-month period. A retrospective cross-sectional study was conducted, and data was collected from the medical charts of 206 patients who had cervical spinal column and spinal cord injuries. The majority of patients were male (75.2%) with a mean age of 37.2±15.9 years. The most common site of fracture was C6 vertebra (29.1%), and the most commonly performed operation was anterior decompression, fixation, and fusion (21.4%). Fifteen patients (7.3%) died during hospitalization, and 11 patients (5.3%) were released before completing recovery. Longer hospital stay, brain and lung injury, and cord injury were significantly associated with an increased risk of death. Additionally, C7 fracture was found to differ significantly between patients with and without associated injuries.

The Nature of the Task
At HL, students are required to write a 1,200 –1,500 word formal essay which develops a particular line of inquiry of their own choice in connection with a non-literary text, a collection of non-literary texts by one same author or a literary text or work studied during the course.

External Assessment
The HL essay offers students an opportunity to develop as independent, critical and creative readers, thinkers and writers by exploring a literary or language topic over an extended period of time, refining their ideas by means of a process of planning, drafting and re-drafting. The essay requires students to construct a focused, analytical argument examining the work from a broad literary or linguistic perspective. It also requires them to adhere to the formal framework of an academic essay, using citations and references.
Any text, texts or work previously studied in class may be selected, with the exception of the texts used for the internal assessment and the works the student plans to use in paper 2.
Determining the Topic
The chosen topic should enable a broad literary or linguistic focus for the essay. In achieving this, the course’s seven central concepts may be a helpful starting point for students in generating or determining a topic for the essay. While students do not have to trace their essay back to one of the seven concepts and the assessment criteria do not require it, working with one of the seven concepts will allow students to begin thinking about their topic as they refine their ideas and arguments. The seven concepts are briefly discussed here in relation to the assignment:
Identity
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of identity of a
particular character or group of characters in the text, or on the way in which the text
relates to the identity of the writer.
Culture
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of the culture of a

particular place, institution or group of people, or on the way inwhich the text itself
relates to a particular culture.
Creativity
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of individual or
collective creativity, or lack of creativity, within the text, or on the way in which the text
represents the creativity of the writer.
Communication
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of acts of
communication, or failures in communication, in the text, or on the way in which the
text itself represents an act of communication.
Transformation
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of transformation or
transformative acts in the text, or on the way in which the text itself is a transformative
act either of other texts through intertextual reference to them or of reality by means of a transformative effect on the reader’s identity, relationships, goals, values, and beliefs.
Perspective
The student might be interested in an aspect of the representation of a particular
perspective or perspectives within the text, or on the way in which the text represents the
writer’s perspective.
Representation
The student might be interested in an aspect of the way in which the text represents
different themes, attitudes and concepts, or in the extent to which language and literature
can actually represent reality.
Here is how a suitable QUESTION OF INQUIRY might arise using concepts as starting points. The following are some examples of how this could be done:
Identity—how does Ralph Ellison, in his novel Invisible Man, succeed in making his narrator a convincing spokesperson for the concerns of African-Americans in the 20th century?
Culture—how does Robert Capa represent post-Second World War France to qualify/exemplify the brutalities of the French population on former Nazi collaborators in La Femme Tondue? (Language A: language and literature only)
Creativity—how do Mario Testino’s portraits manage to convey the personalities of those portrayed in original ways? (Language A: language and literature only)
Communication--which view of love does Matt Groening convey in Love is Hell? (Language A: language and literature only)
Transformation--in what ways does The Alan Parsons Project’s Tales of Mystery and Imagination offer a transformative re-reading of Edgar Allan Poe’s tales?
Perspective--how does Mary Shelley’s protagonist in Frankenstein use the motif of dangerous knowledge to show the perspective of fear and anxiety of excesses in scientific enterprise in early 19th century Europe?
Representation--through what means does Juan Rulfo successfully convey the representation of realistic and non-realistic characters and situations in Pedro Páramo?​
However, using the seven concepts is neither prescriptive nor exhaustive. Other literary focuses, theoretical approaches or areas of exploration could lead to lines of inquiry such as:
How does F. Scott Fitzgerald foreshadow how Gatsby’s unnatural attachment to the past causes his downfall in The Great Gatsby?
In what ways would Marxist theory about the stratification of wealth and power explain the violence that runs through the action of the novel A Hundred Years of Solitude by Gabriel García Márquez?
To what extent was the characterization of the protagonist in Patrick Süskind´s Perfume influenced by Franz Kafka´s The Metamorphosis?

The static nature of James Wilson in House
House is one of the most iconic TV series among the drama genre; it managed to garner
much critical acclaim and a very devoted, cult-like fan base. The TV series took the viewers
through eight seasons, each marked by powerful drama between characters, several
antagonists, political commentary of the most varied nature and, of course, dark humor. House
has a dynamic storyline; the lead character is constantly forced to repeal the wrath of various
adversaries, and each episode features a unique and unexpected medical intrigue. Among this
ever-changing environment and storyline, one character manages to remain unchanged
throughout the series: Dr. James Wilson. Wilson retains his impersonal, compassionate,
selfless and loyal nature throughout the eight seasons of the series. Though far from being a
flat character, Wilson is static in terms of his goals, feelings and unquestioned loyalty to
House’s well-being. This essay seeks to explore the manner in which Wilson retains his
identity throughout the entire series.
The core aspect we need to delve into is that of “identity”; in the strict sense of the
word, Wilson’s identity is relayed to the audience in a very resume-like manner. We pointedly
find out Wilson’s religious affiliation (“A lot of Jews have non-Jewish relatives, and most of us don’t
keep kosher”, he reveals1, without his religion ever being used as part of the plot in any way)
and his academic background (revealed to us thanks to him wearing a “Graduated from
McGill University” sweater2). Even his name is made known to the audience only incidentally,
halfway through the first episode. This austere manner of presenting the audience with
Wilson’s biographical background provides stability and a certain degree of artistic
immovability. His academic background, religious affiliation or family ties never come up
during the series; this is worth looking at in light of other characters’ biographies. Chase, a
colleague of Wilson’s, is constantly modulated based on his millionaire father’s erratic
behavior. House, the 50 year-old lead character, is very much still caught up in feuds he had
back in college. Wilson’s identity, however, never comes back to influence his behavior or to
change the audience’s impression of him. Providing the audience with stable and minimal
information about Wilson’s basic identity helps preserve Wilson’s ever-static nature.
Identity, however, ought to be looked at from a broader perspective. Wilson is not just
a good oncologist from a middle-class Jewish background; he is also a husband, a friend, a
former adult films actor, an important director of the hospital, a lover, a widower, a wanted
fugitive and a cynical man. While Wilson certainly is all of those things, his character simply
fails to live up to the standard of being anything other than House’s nemesis. At some point
in the first season, the audience is told that Wilson is an active member of his hospital’s board
of directors. Wilson is only ever shown in his capacity as a director once. “You can’t make my
vote void by making me stand in the hallway”3, Wilson says, in the context of a contentious
administrative matter. That is the extent to which his influence on the board is ever invoked
throughout the series, despite other characters with similar directorial appointments being at
the forefront of administrative intrigue systematically throughout the series. Wilson’s core
professional identity remains static, despite the occasional plot developments that place
Wilson in lateral contexts; the audience cannot help but visualize him strictly as a doctor.
Wilson’s previous encounters with law enforcement turn out to have led him to being
a wanted fugitive for almost two decades. “James Evan Wilson, there’s an arrest warrant out in
your name”, a police officer tells, before primarily House proceeds to present the reasons as to
why Wilson was arrested once upon a time. Wilson rarely plays a central role whenever his
own life is a subject of discussion. For instance, in the scene where Wilson’s arrest is being
presented to the audience, the camera hardly focuses on Wilson; other minor characters and
rich décor receive more airtime in that particular scene, despite the entire scene being about
Wilson. The character is physically isolated from matters pertaining to him; perhaps ironically,
the scenes focusing on Wilson’s own life are the scenes where Wilson receives the least amount
of camera work. This helps preserve Wilson’s immaculate image of the well-dressed and well-
meaning doctor.
It is fair to say that Wilson receives a good amount of light mockery from (almost
exclusively) House. This mockery, however, only helps to consolidate Wilson’s image as a
professional, compassionate individual. House’s jokes about Wilson certainly aim to upset
(and perhaps demean) him, but the unintended effect of these jokes is to simply further
Wilson’s core identity. “Wilson’s so good, people thank him for telling them that they’re dying”4,
House tells, in the context of describing Wilson to a stranger. This conveys just how
compassionate Wilson can get; most jokes about Wilson aim to mock his goodness. On another
occasion, Wilson’s co-worker mocks him for being “too much of a good boy”5. Wilson disagrees
and agrees to steal a dollar to prove he’s capable of being devious. However, when it comes to
actually doing it, Wilson backs out and immediately returns the dollar to the cashier he stole
it from, all while a panicked and uncomfortable Wilson is showed on camera. Even mockery
serves the purpose of constantly reminding the audience just how upstanding and righteous
Wilson is.
The scenarios themselves appear to be designed exactly for the purpose of minimizing
Wilson’s ability to take control of his own storyline. One of Wilson’s girlfriends, Amber,
tragically dies in an automobile accident. House attempts to reconstruct the circumstances of
the accident, while Wilson tries to criticize the feasibility of reconstructing the accident
involving his own girlfriend. “Wilson is done talking now”6, one of House’s co-workers says, and
then proceeding to carry on with total disregard of Wilson’s earlier observations. On another
occasion, Wilson is devastated to find out that his wife had been cheating on him. “Turns out
you were right. She was having an affair”7, Wilson tells House, in the context of Wilson
announcing his separation from his wife (a fact House previously speculated on). Even scenes
that focus on aspects of Wilson’s personal life are monopolized by either other characters who
take the lead or House’s earlier aphorisms, which somehow always end up targeting Wilson.
By placing distance between Wilson himself and his personal life, the creators of the show
have managed to retain Wilson’s relative independence from matters concerning his own life.
Wilson has a professional life of his own; his medical cases and patients are regularly
presented to the audience and are part of the script. However, his medical cases are never
presented autonomously; his patients somehow always become intertwined with House or
other controversies related to the main character. The audience simply has no time to pay close
attention to Wilson’s modus operandi. On one occasion, Wilson’s oncology patient (in
remission) and personal friend, Tucker, comes in with severe respiratory issues. Wilson makes
the diagnosis without looking at Tucker, but at Tucker’s girlfriend. He notices that she has
herpes; Wilson concludes that Tucker must have caught herpes from her, causing him
respiratory issues. “I just had a House moment”8 , Wilson says in awe. He personally sets aside
his professional wisdom by reminding the audience of House’s genius, but his facial
expression certainly shows internal satisfaction. “Draw some blood. He has cancer”, House
intervenes, followed by Wilson deciding to conduct further medical tests. House turns out to
have been ultimately right about the diagnostic. The whole episode carries on focusing on
House’s intuitions being confirmed step by step by House’s medical team, despite Tucker
being Wilson’s patient and friend. The one occasion where Wilson would have had the chance
to shine is yet again overshadowed by House. By systematically placing Wilson in a position
of professional inferiority in relation to other nominally equal colleagues, the audience is
always reminded of Wilson’s subservient and pacifying nature.
A good part of this essay focused not on Wilson’s lines, but on what other characters
said or did in connection to Wilson. This certainly rings true to Wilson’s fundamental nature:
his warm-hearted spirit rests not on making himself feel good, but by making others feel good
in his own detriment. Wilson never snaps at others cutting him off, belittling him or
demeaning him. He only tried this once, at House’s supposed funeral. He lashes out. “House
was an ass. He mocked his dwindling friends. He betrayed everyone who cared about him”, Wilson
says in his “eulogy” for House, before being interrupted by an SMS containing one of House’s
catchphrases, “shut up you idiot”. Wilson’s facial expression fades from one of anger to his
regular Wilson self; needless to say, the eulogy stops. Not even in the very last episode of the
TV series did Wilson have the chance to speak out his mind freely, unabashed about the impact
of his words.
Wilson’s character is never held to low standards; it is merely kept to the same
standards the audience expected from him since the very first episode. The audience is never
presented with an unjust or unprofessional Wilson, but an immaculate Wilson that stands in
sharp contrast with the lead character’s outer behavior.

Cassidy was about to leave when Chad grabbed her hand and pressed her on the bed as he hovered over her, his amber eyes staring at her deeply. 
“Are you trying to be petty and charming at the same time?” he teased. 
His voice caressed her heart like a delicate feather. 
Cassidy’s cheeks turned red as she blushed trying to fight the embarrassment, she rolled her eyes and snorted
 “Isn’t it obvious?”

With another kiss on her hair, he got out of bed, turned back and carefully tucked the quilt around Cassidy, his eyes glassy with affection. 
“Good night, Cass,” he beamed a smile at her and with that, disappeared out of the room. 
The room became quiet as soon as he left and for the first time since that evening, Cassidy felt lonely. Part of her wanted to walk through the door and beg Chad to come back to the room because she was so used to him sleeping beside her but her more realistic side got the better of her. 
“You’ll be fine, Cassidy Hart,” she murmured to herself thumping on her chest. “Chad West is a kind mand and will literally do any one he meets on the street good so do not be swayed by his kindness because if you do and think that there’s a small possibility that he likes you as a woman and not because you’re a warm body and potential baby making machine, you’ll end up hurting yourself…” she took a deep breath wishing her heart would stop pounding in her chest. 
“So, guard your heart, Cassidy,” she poked her chest her face drawn into a determined resolve “Don’t you dare like him back nor love him. Don’t you dare!”. 
After the pep talk to herself, she laid on the bed and drifted into a peaceful sleep. 
The next day, Cassidy got up bright and energized. 
She had a lot to do and little time. For one, she needed to start looking for individuals, companies or brand willing to invest into the new movie ‘When Heart meets’ and since it was urgent, she needed the funds as soon as possible so production will kick off right away. 
She went through her morning routine trying to draw up a schedule in her head by the time she went downstairs, she had planned for the entire day and from everything, she had only thirty minutes for breakfast. 
She met Chad coming out of the kitchen with steaming bowls of food that he placed on the dining table. The delicious aroma from the food filled her nostrils in no time making her mouth to water as her stomach growled in hunger. 
“Good morning,” she greeted stiffly walking into the dining room. 
Chad was hunched at the table dishing food. He looked like something straight out of the magazine with the way his sweatshirt was rolled up to his elbows. 
“Oh!” he turned to her, his eyes registering surprise ”Hi,” he greeted “You’re up early,”. 
“Yeah,” Cassidy murmured half-heartedly avoiding his gaze as she started walking towards the kitchen. 
“Where are you going?” Chad asked 
“Pouring myself a cup of coffee and also grab a quick breakfast,” Cassidy responded from behind her shoulders. 
“Oh, don’t worry about that,” Chad said immediately “I cooked up a storm, so let’s eat together, okay?” he urged her. 
“Sorry, can’t,” Cassidy continued to the kitchen ignoring the hunger pangs in her stomach as she tried to forget how delicious the food on the dinning had looked when she peeked. 
“Why is that?” Chad followed closely after her “C’mon babe... don’t be like this. I cooked for us and should eat,”. 
“I have a lot to do this morning, Chad,” she ignored him as she busied herself at the coffee machine. I simply don’t have time for a meal at this rate. Maybe some other time…”. 
Chad sighed as he came close to her. He turned off the coffee machine and gently collected the coffee cup in her hand which he set on the table. Then he held her shoulders and turned her gently so she was now facing him. 
“What do you want?” Cassidy squeaked trying to break from his firm hold. 
“I am sorry, Cass,” Chad started “I realized that my behaviour last night was inexcusable. I treated you like a trash and I forced myself on you against you will. I’m truly sorry and I hope you can find a place in your heart to forgive me especially since I’m going to promise that it’ll not happen again,”. 
The apology was unexpected and left Cassidy stunned as she tried to collect herself and speak. 
“Well,” she shrugged daintily “Your actions in the future will determine if I can forgive you or not but for now… I haven’t,” she said. 
“Fair enough,” Chad nodded with a gentle smile on his face “Can you do me a favour and just eat with me, this morning? Please…”. 
Chad seldom says Please but when he does, he means it with every sincerity something that Cassidy didn’t need to let anyone tell her. 
She allowed him lead him out of the kitchen towards the dining table. When they got there, Cassidy’s eyes scanned the table, taking in all the mouth-watering dishes on it. 
“Y-you made this yourself?” she asked fighting the urge to grab the freshly baked croissants staring invitingly on the table. 
“Well…” Chad shrugged scratching his head. 
“Why?” she asked, eyeing him. 
He didn’t respond immediately, he pulled out her sit as he settled her against the table and then leaned beside her his eyes filled with amusement and affection. 
“I didn’t want to be kicked out of the house by my wife,” he teased dropping a light kiss on Cassidy’s cheeks. 
At that instant, Gerald, the butler entered the dining room and he heard Chad’s remark. He couldn’t resist laughing causing Cassidy to blush deeper in embarrassment as she playfully nudged him by his rib.
“You can’t change my mind after one meal,” she scoffed. 
“Then I’ll cook a few more meals. Anything you want, I’ll be willing to make it for you. Do you me to make lunch for you and have it delivered to you?” he suggested, a mischievous glint in his eyes. 
Cassidy’s eyes widened with fright as she turned to him. 
“Don’t you dare,” she warned. “If anyone in Wellspring should see you delivering food to me, it’ll not only create a huge scandal but I’ll be hot topic for every media house throughout the year. Is that what you want?” she huffed. 
Her response caused Chad displeasure as he scooted close to her again. 
“You make it sound like I am your secret lover,” he said. 
“Well,” the smile drained from Cassidy’s face “Aren’t you?”. 
“What?” Chad arched his brow at her already getting irritated “If I am your secret lover, then it means you’re…”.
“Stop talking nonsense,” she kicked him hard before he could complete his sentence. 
“That hurts,” he complained nursing his smarting leg. 
“Let’s just eat, Chad, else the food will get cold,” Cassidy flared, getting irritated by his behaviour. 
But Chad didn’t notice she was angry. He was happy to see that she was talking to him at least and she looked happy an improvement from last night when she was cold and distant. 
As he watched her eat, he felt that he would never be able to understand her no matter how much he tried. 
“By the way,” Chad said in between spoonful of food “Now that you’ve taken over H&G, there must be a thousand problems butt don’t worry if there’s anywhere you want me to help, just tell me. I’ll come to your rescue,”. 
Cassidy paused eating as she looked up at him, a smile on her face. 
“Don’t worry, I have everything under control. Be rest assured,” she beamed him another smile. 
Although there were too many problems but Cassidy was determined to solve all of them by herself. She didn’t want to rely on him anymore. She couldn’t risk all of his help accumulating into many debts to the extent that she’ll become powerless and humiliated when it’s time for their divorce. 
“Really?” Chad eyed her disbelievingly “Are you sure you’re capable of running the affairs of H&G?” he asked again. “From what I was told, the company would need all the expertise to have things turn around,”. 
“And I said I am on it, don’t worry,” Cassidy insisted as she flashed him a confident smile. “Have you forgotten who I am?”. 
Chad was amused by the proud way she carried herself and was comforted by that. Still her responded solemnly…
“Why would I forget? You’re Chad Wests’ woman – my wife. So, it’s only natural that you possess such great power to turn anything you want around,”. 
His reply made Cassidy’s heart skip a beat and in response she gave him a stern look. His words had caught her off guard so she didn’t know how to react without letting him know that his words affected her. 
“You know,” she sighed “I can’t put up with the nonsense you won’t stop spilling all day. Since I am done eating, I’m going to head to the company now,” she stood to her feet. 
“Oh!” Chad stood up as well “Then I’ll drive you. Let me change into something more presentable,” he said gazing at her tenderly. 
“There’ll be no need for that,” Cassidy stopped him giving him a stiff smile “I will drive myself,”. 
With that, she turned and walked away leaving a confused Chad in her wake. 
Chad furrowed his brow, his amber eyes deep in thought as she walked away. He couldn’t understand how one minute she was so close and it seemed like she had forgiven him and the next she was cold and distant again. 
“Was it because of last night?” Chad mused to himself. “I asked her for forgiveness and it seemed like she was ready to put everything in the past or is she harboring resentment towards me?”
For the first time in his life, he didn’t have all the answers.
