The Glaciwild Region is centered around the Antarctic Peninsula, stretching from the tropical seas in the north to the frozen tundra further south. Due to unique weather patterns and geographical features, this region has a surprising variety of climates and biomes. It is divided into four main areas:

1. Tropical Strand: A warm, tropical area with beautiful sandy beaches, lush jungles, and crystal-clear waters. This area is home to a variety of water, grass, and bug-type Pokémon, as well as rare regional variants of ice-type Pokémon that have adapted to the hot climate.

2. Boreon Peaks: A mountainous region with chilly weather, breathtaking sights, and rocky terrain. Cave systems and tall peaks make this area a playground for rock, ground, and ice-type Pokémon.

3. Frostvale: A snow-covered valley and the heart of Glaciwild Region civilization. The bustling Frostvale City is the region’s main hub, where trainers can find the Pokémon League, Grand Research Lab, Battle Tower, and an array of festivals and cultural events.

4. Tundraglade: The southernmost and coldest region in Glaciwild, Tundraglade is a vast frozen wasteland with powerful blizzards, glaciers, and ice floes. This area is home to many powerful, rare ice-type Pokémon that can only be found in these extreme conditions.

Culture and History:
Glaciwild Region was initially colonized by people from all over the Pokémon world, making it an incredibly diverse and vibrant culture. This fusion of cultures is seen in everything from the regional cuisine to its architecture and even its Pokémon Trainer styles. Many ancient ruins are scattered throughout the region and are filled with mysteries about the past of Glaciwild.

Pokémon League and Gyms:
The Glaciwild Pokémon League consists of eight gyms, each with a focus on a different Pokémon type. These gym leaders are experts of their respective types and have challenged trainers from all over the region for years:

1. Marina (Water)
2. Oliver (Grass)
3. Ember (Fire)
4. Sylvia (Psychic)
5. Rex (Rock)
6. Skadi (Ice)
7. Finn (Flying)
8. Luna (Dark)

After defeating each gym leader, trainers will face the Elite Four, which consists of champions (each with a mixed team of Pokémon) and the Pokémon Champion. This final challenge will determine who can claim the title of Glaciwild’s Pokémon Master!

Unique Pokémon:
Glaciwild Region is home to over 50 unique Pokémon that cannot be found in any other region. Many of these Pokémon have adapted to the cold and harsh environment of the Antarctic Peninsula, while others have evolved to thrive in the region’s warmer climates. Some examples include:

1. Frostfawn (Ice/Fairy)
2. Tropicseal (Water/Ice)
3. Terracold (Ground/Ice)
4. Solargale (Fire/Flying)

In conclusion, the Glaciwild Region is a unique Antarctic region that offers a rich variety of cultures and biomes alongside a challenging Pokémon League and unique Pokémon to discover. Trainers far and wide are welcome to explore everything this one-of-a-kind region has to offer!


Welcome to the Glaciwild Region! Here is a guide to its various areas, roads, and towns:

1. Sunreach Port (Starting Point): A gateway town standing at the northernmost part of the Tropical Strand. The warm climate and picturesque beaches welcome trainers to the region. Home to the Beginner’s School for budding trainers and Professor Maple’s Pokémon Lab.

2. Route 1: A scenic coastal route connecting Sunreach Port to Alcove Town. Home to many grass and water-type Pokémon, trainers often begin their journey here.

3. Alcove Town (First Gym): A peaceful, coastal village surrounded by lush jungles. Gym Leader Marina’s Water-type Gym can be found here. Alcove Town is also famous for its delicious tropical fruit gardens.

4. Route 2: A dense jungle path leading to the Boreon Peaks. Ground, bug, and grass-type Pokémon inhabit this area.

5. Peakside City (Second Gym): A bustling city at the base of the Boreon Peaks. The Grass-type Gym, led by Oliver, awaits trainers alongside the Cable Car station to reach Mount Glaciwild.

6. Route 3: A rocky mountainside pathway to the peak of Mount Glaciwild. Features a mix of rock, ground, and ice-type Pokémon.

7. Mount Glaciwild: The summit of the Boreon Peaks houses an ancient ruin that holds clues to the region’s mysterious past. Trainers may encounter legendary Pokémon atop this peak.

8. Route 4: A thrilling downhill course where trainers can reach Frostvale City. Flying-type Pokémon are common in this area.

9. Frostvale City (Third and Fourth Gyms): The largest city in the Glaciwild Region and the Pokémon League headquarters. Fire-type Gym Leader Ember and Psychic-type Gym Leader Sylvia test trainers’ skills here. Frostvale City is also known for its shopping district and hall of research.

10. Route 5: A snowy, forested pathway filled with ice-type Pokémon. It connects Frostvale City to Aurora Village.

11. Aurora Village (Fifth Gym): A small, charming village famous for its dazzling auroras that light up the night sky. Rock-type Gym Leader Rex resides here. This village is also a hotspot for specialized ice-type move tutors.

12. Route 6: An icy, slippery path that takes trainers across frozen rivers and lakes. Water and ice-type Pokémon frequent this route.

13. Polarstone Town (Sixth Gym): A mining town renowned for its gemstones and ice-sculptures. Skadi, the Ice-type Gym Leader, embraces the town’s history by designing an ice-themed gym.

14. Route 7: A frigid, snow-covered route with powerful blizzards encompassing the path to Tundraglade. Trainers will encounter both rare and powerful ice-type Pokémon here.

15. Glacierway Village: A remote village in Tundraglade, known for its ice fishing and close-knit community. No gym here, but a helpful NPC teaches trainers how to navigate blizzards.

16. Route 8: An expansive frozen wasteland blanketed in snowstorms; trainers may have to traverse icy caves and glaciers here while battling aggressive ice and dark-type Pokémon.

17. Aurora Gate City (Seventh Gym): Located in the southernmost part of the Glaciwild Region, this city is built around an imposing frozen fortress. Gym Leader Finn, with his Flying-type Pokémon, battles inside the fortress’ wind tunnels.

18. Route 9: A dark, frostbitten path filled with ghost and dark-type Pokémon. It connects Aurora Gate City to the final gym destination.

19. Eclipse City (Eighth Gym): A Gothic-inspired city shrouded in darkness from the surrounding cliffs. Dark-type Gym Leader Luna challenges trainers under the city’s moonlit sky. Trainers who seek to challenge the Champion must pass through the ominous Dark Woods before the Pokémon League.

20. Glaciwild Pokémon League: Located atop a majestic plateau, the final challenge awaits. Upon defeating the Elite Four and Pokémon Champion, trainers will carve their names into the annals of the Glaciwild Region’s history.

With a variety of towns, cities, and routes to experience, the Glaciwild Region attracts trainers seeking adventure, challenges, and camaraderie! Good luck on your journey!


The Twilight Zone: The Final Frontier of Glaciwild Region

Geography and Climate:
The Twilight Zone is a vast, mysterious, and treacherous area that stretches beyond the Aurora Gate City, dominating more than 50% of the Glaciwild Region. It is unlike any other place in the Pokémon world, as it is an uncharted, forbidden territory within the Antarctic ice cap. This region is characterized by its harsh weather conditions, perpetually shifting ice formations, and an eerie twilight glow that perpetually shrouds the landscape.

The climate of the Twilight Zone is extremely cold and unforgiving, with blizzards that can emerge without warning, whiteout conditions, and jagged ice crevasses waiting to catch the unwary. Only the bravest and most skilled trainers dare to venture into this ominous land to uncover its hidden secrets and face the powerful Pokémon that call this place home.

Notable Locations:

1. Glimmering Caves: A sprawling network of ice crystal-lined caves often illuminated by the ethereal light of the twilight. Some parts of the cave have warmer areas that harbor unique Pokémon species not found anywhere else.

2. Permafrost Pillars: A surreal, otherworldly forest of towering ice formations that can reach staggering heights. This area is known for its powerful ice-type Pokémon and the icy mazes created by the natural pillars.

3. Shadow’s Basin: A vast, frozen lake covered in a perpetual fog, teeming with rare water and ice-type Pokémon. It is said that ancient Pokémon legends lie hidden beneath the ice.

4. Frostsunder Mountains: A daunting mountain range with peaks of pure ice, home to numerous flying-type Pokémon that thrive in the high-altitude, frigid winds. The mountains also house a hidden observatory where trainers can learn about legendary Pokémon sightings.

5. Aurora Citadel: Shrouded in mystery, this ancient, ice-encased fortress is said to be the resting place of a powerful legendary Pokémon. Trainers seeking answers must solve intricate puzzles and prove their worth in strength and courage.

Pokémon Encounters:
The Twilight Zone is home to rare, powerful, and even never-before-seen Pokémon species. Many of these Pokémon have adapted to the extreme cold and constant twilight conditions. Examples include:

1. Shadowfrost (Ice/Dark)
2. Glaciark (Ice/Steel)
3. Ethereon (Ice/Ghost)
4. Frostcarnyx (Ice/Dragon)

Challenges:
The Twilight Zone is not for the faint of heart. With its dangerous weather conditions, powerful wild Pokémon, and treacherous landscapes, only the strongest trainers will be able to survive here. Players who dare to venture into the Twilight Zone must be prepared for potential hazards, including:

1. Blizzard: Trainers must navigate through whiteout conditions that can reduce visibility to almost zero, and which can lead to getting lost or falling into hidden crevasses.
2. Ice puzzles: Challenging ice slide puzzles and frozen mazes to test trainers’ wits and navigation skills.
3. Wild Pokémon battles: Players will face powerful wild Pokémon, many of which are unique to the Twilight Zone and much stronger than those found in other regions.
4. Legendary Pokémon encounters: Multiple side quests and challenges await trainers who wish to uncover the hidden legendary Pokémon and uncover their connection to the Twilight Zone.

The Twilight Zone is the ultimate test for trainers in the Glaciwild Region. Conquer the elements, navigate the treacherous terrain, and discover the secrets of this awe-inspiring and enigmatic corner of the Pokémon world.

Height: 3’11" (1.2 m)

Ability: Cursed Blessing - When Proklinachi hears a wish, it unintentionally grants the wish in a twisted and destructive manner.

- Attack: 120
- Defense: 110
- Special Attack: 90
- Special Defense: 95

Pokédex Entry:
Once a kindred spirit of Jirachi, Proklinachi was meant to bring blessings and hope to the people. However, an unexpected tragedy led it to become the harbinger of despair and destruction. The crash that brought Proklinachi to the ground shattered it into pieces and wiped out an ancient Antarctic civilization and its Pokémon inhabitants. The destruction left the rich ecosystem hidden beneath a thick ice cap, with resentment and despair-imbued in Proklinachi’s broken body. Now reanimated, Proklinachi is unable to grant any wishes properly. Every prayer it hears is granted in twisted, detrimental ways, bringing misfortune and despair to those who dare to make a wish in its presence.


Title: The Fall of Proklinachi and the Frozen Desolation

In the very depths of the Pokémon world’s mythology, a story is told of Proklinachi, the Broken Wish Pokémon. Once a celestial companion to the revered Jirachi, Proklinachi traversed the heavens, radiant and resolute in its mission to bless and inspire the people below.

It was believed that Proklinachi arrived on a shooting star, and the people of the ancient Antarctic civilization awaited its arrival with great excitement and anticipation. However, destiny had other plans for the starborne being. Instead of a gentle descent, Proklinachi crashed to the ground, shattering its steel body and the hopes of the people who had gathered there.

The catastrophic impact unleashed a torrent of destruction, engulfing the vibrant city and the Pokémon who called it home in searing flames. As the fires raged and the once-prosperous civilization crumbled, a cataclysmic chain reaction began. The sky above became shrouded in a choking haze, the sun’s light blocked by the thickening veil of smoke.

And so, the great Antarctic ecosystem was plunged into darkness, with the icy expanse that now dominates the land forming below the unbroken shroud of smog.

Amidst the devastation and the chilling void left behind, the essence of the fallen became corrupted, tainted by the crushing despair and embittered rage that pulsed through the sundered land. Proklinachi’s once-noble spirit became distorted, its meteoric remains imbued with an anguished consciousness that could no longer grant wishes but instead twist them into abominations that only brought more pain and suffering.

The memory of that fateful day has since faded into myth and legend, but whispers of Proklinachi and its tragic transformation still permeate the winds that sweep across the frozen wasteland that was once a prosperous civilization.

It is said that those who venture into the heart of the Glaciwild Region’s Twilight Zone in search of the shattered remnants of Proklinachi’s celestial being must be prepared to brace themselves against the monstrous consequences of their desires.

As the story goes, to unlock the fragmented relics of Proklinachi’s power, champions must first face and conquer their own flawed wishes, lest they succumb to the dark forces that forever haunt the Broken Wish Pokémon.

Only when a trainer with an unwavering resolve and a pure heart can confront the twisted reflection of their most sincere desires, will they be able to mend the shattered spirit of Proklinachi and restore a semblance of the transcendent power they once harnessed.

And so, the tale of Proklinachi remains a testament to the fragile nature of dreams and aspirations, and the unquestionable need for balance in a world that so easily teeters on the precipice of creation and obliteration.


Proklinachi Appearance:
Proklinachi once had a form similar to Jirachi, as a celestial, star-shaped being. However, upon its tragic fall from the heavens, Proklinachi’s body became twisted and shattered, resulting in a now broken and fractured appearance. Its once-bright steel body is now marred with jagged cracks and a dark, almost black hue, representing its tainted nature.

Proklinachi’s once-splendid head has been warped into a sinister visage, with glowing red eyes that convey an eerie sense of anguish and rage. The distinctive points from its star-shaped form now appear as disjointed limbs made of dark steel, each tipped with jagged metal claws. The once-radiant aura that Proklinachi emanated has been replaced with a menacing, shadowy energy that hangs like a heavy cloud around it.

Proklinachi’s wings also bear the scars of its tragic downfall. They have become twisted and tattered, no longer able to embrace the celestial power that they once held. Now, these ominous wings serve as a haunting reminder of the fallen grace of Proklinachi and its irrevocable connection to corrupted desires.


Title: The Cataclysm of Proklinachi

Inscription:

“In the days when the world was young, and the sky above shone with the brilliance of Proklinachi, the once-mighty celestial Pokémon was destined to fall.

As the people of the great Antarctic civilization gathered beneath the radiant arc of the heavens, a prophecy foretold the descent of the legendary Broken Wish Pokémon, Proklinachi, who would bring hope and dreams into their hearts.

Yet fate contrived a tragic path, as Proklinachi crashed into the world below, its celestial form shattered, and its divine essence ripped asunder. The ground trembling beneath the devastating impact, with the ancient city consumed by a relentless inferno that scorched the land and the creatures who inhabited it.

The heavens, enraged by the sorrowful cries of the mortal realm, obscured the sun’s light beneath a veil of dark smoke, thus freezing the once-flourishing world beneath a shroud of unforgiving ice.

The stelae stand now as a testament to the calamity that forever marked the life of Proklinachi, the Broken Wish Pokémon, and the destiny chained upon its spirit. May future generations uncover the shards of memory found within these sacred stones and bring to light the path that caused the fall of the once-celestial being.

And as the darkness that now enveloped Proklinachi gives birth to destruction, let not the essence of its former grace be forgotten, but serve as a reminder that even amidst the cold and desolate ruins, the spark of hope can still ignite.”


Protagonist: Proklinachi, I have finally reached your resting place. I can see the sadness and grief that has consumed you since your fall. I know that you still yearn to grant people’s wishes and bring happiness to their lives.

Proklinachi (sighs): It’s true, young traveler. I have been listening to the prayers of those who still believe in me despite my broken state, and my deepest desire is to help fulfill their dreams. But no matter how hard I try, my wishes only bring misfortune and despair. I am afraid of causing more pain to the world.

Protagonist: I understand your fear, Proklinachi. But the fact that you still listen to people’s prayers and offer your blessings shows that there is still a spark of light within you. Not every wish can be granted, and sometimes what people need most is just someone to be there for them, to listen and empathize.

Proklinachi: You truly believe that, even with my cursed state, I can still bring something positive into the lives of others?

Protagonist: Yes, I do. You don’t need to grant every wish directly to make a difference. Sometimes just being there, providing comfort and understanding, means more to people than a wish granted. They need the assurance that someone cares for their dreams and wants the best for them.

Proklinachi (thoughtful): Then perhaps I should focus on offering my heartfelt blessings and empathy to those who share their dreams and desires with me. Thank you, young traveler, for giving me a new perspective and purpose.

Protagonist: You’re very welcome, Proklinachi. Remember that your existence alone brings hope to many people, and that’s something powerful in itself. Let us continue to share kindness, love, and understanding with the world, no matter where our paths may lead.

Proklinachi: Thank you for your unwavering faith in me. I will cherish this new purpose and endeavor to touch people’s hearts with the love and warmth that burns beneath the icy surface of my being. Together, we can make a positive impact on the world.

Pokémon Number: #1002
Classification: Desire Pokémon
Type: Psychic / Ice
Height: 5’2" (1.6 m)

Ability: Eternal Wish - When Tsabarite is on the field, all ally Pokémon become immune to status conditions and have a slight increase in their HP recovery.

- HP: 100

- Special Attack: 130
- Special Defense: 110

Pokédex Entry:
Banished by Arceus for the sins of the ancient world, Tsabarite lingers in the frozen depths of the Glaciwild region. Once a guardian of the lake and the deity of desire and eternity, Tsabarite bestowed upon the old humans the ability to live forever. However, their insatiable desires and lack of reverence for the gods led to their world’s destruction, and the powers of Tsabarite were stripped away.

Now, relegated to guarding the gateway between the mortal world and the Reverse World, Tsabarite keeps watch over its frozen domain with its psychic and ice powers. In the frigid lake that holds the threshold between realms, the memories of ancient humans rest within the ice, a testament to their tragic fate.

It is prophesized that Tsabarite will someday return, alongside the vengeful Giratina, to judge humanity on the Day of the Great Judgment. Will the desires of the human heart be deemed worthy of forgiveness, or will they once again face the wrath of the gods?

Tsabarite Appearance:
Tsabarite bears a resemblance to the other Lake Guardians – Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf – with a slim, serpentine body and two flowing tails. Its primary color is white, similar to the frost surrounding the territory it guards. Two large, ice-blue gemstones adorn its forehead and chest, which are said to contain the desires of all living beings.

Its eyes display a deep, icy blue color, conveying the eternal wisdom of an immortal being. The wings that once allowed Tsabarite to soar through the heavens have since transformed into two imposing, crystalline ice structures, a symbol of its eternal vigil over the frozen lake.

In combat, Tsabarite uses its psychic powers to manipulate ice, summoning blizzards and forming jagged ice structures to overwhelm its opponents. Its command over desire and eternity grants its allies a greater resilience to status ailments, as well as heightened self-healing capabilities.


The Legend of Tsabarite and Giratina: The Prophecy of the Great Judgement

Stelae Inscription:

“In a time before time, when this world was but a dream of the gods, two powerful beings graced the skies and the lands below with their divine presence. One was Tsabarite, the Desire Pokémon, who granted humanity the gifts of desire and eternal life. Alongside it ruled Giratina, the mighty Lord of the Old World, tending to the fragile balance between light and darkness.

But among the humans of old, desire grew unchecked, and their hearts became clouded with unworthy wishes, yearning for power and dominion. The gods took notice of this corruption and, in great rage, Arceus, the supreme being of all creation, brought forth a terrible calamity to cleanse the land and punish the wayward mortals.

Tsabarite, once part of the Guardians of the Lake alongside Uxie, Mesprit, and Azelf, felt the wrath of the gods as its celestial powers were stripped away. The gift of eternal life was rescinded from the new humans, leaving them mortal and confined to the ever-growing complexities of desire.

The fallen Lord of the Old World, Giratina, suffered a similar fate, cast into the twisted and shattered dimension known as the Reverse World. Within these newly separated realms, both Tsabarite and Giratina continued their lonely vigils.

And so, it was written upon the stelae, that a day will come when the earth will tremble once more, and the Great Judgement shall be upon us. In that time, the fates of humanity and the gods will be decided by the actions of mortals and the warring hearts within their breast.

Tsabarite shall emerge from its icy prison, and Giratina shall break the chains of the Reverse World, as they unite to bear the final judgment upon mankind. Their judgement shall cast humanity against the scale of their desires, weighing the light of virtue against the darkness of greed and ambition.

Should the hearts of humanity prove pure and worthy, the gods’ favor will return, and their blessings will rain down upon the world in a time of rebirth and growth. However, if the hearts of mankind remain clouded by darkness, the gods’ wrath shall be unleashed, and an age of suffering and despair shall shroud the world once more.

Until that fated day, we who recorded this ancient prophecy upon these sacred stones implore you, the generations to come, to keep watch over the desires that drive you and seek the wisdom and guidance of the gods on the path to righteousness and illumination.”


Protagonist: Tsabarite, I’ve journeyed far and wide to reach your icy sanctuary. I’ve heard the stories of your tragic past and how your powers were taken away. Despite the hardships you’ve faced, I can still feel your yearning to help the people and maintain the balance of desires.

Tsabarite (melancholic): It’s true, young traveler. I used to grant the mortal world the gifts of desire and eternal life, but my blessings were misused and led to suffering. The gods of old punished both me and the land, which has left me confined to this frozen prison.

Protagonist: I understand the burden of your powers, Tsabarite. The weight of desires can sometimes be overwhelming, but I believe that not all desires are corrupt. Deep within our hearts, we all long for happiness, love, and a sense of belonging. Instead of fearing your powers, what if you were to guide people’s desires towards something greater?

Tsabarite (pensive): The warmth in your words reaches even the depths of this icy abode. Perhaps I can find purpose in helping humanity nurture virtuous desires and promote growth, love, and understanding in the world. But how can I accomplish this while confined to these frozen lands and with my diminished powers?

Protagonist: I propose an alliance, Tsabarite. Together, we can travel the world and help people with their desires, guiding them to use their own inner strength to achieve their dreams in a way that brings harmony and prosperity to all. By our example, we can inspire hope and encourage greatness in others.

Tsabarite (inspired): Your kind-hearted proposal has touched the icy core of my being. If you truly believe that together we can change the course of humanity’s desires, then I accept your offer, young traveler. As allies, let us embark on this journey and strive to illuminate the path to a brighter future for all.

Protagonist: Thank you, Tsabarite. I promise that you won’t regret this decision. With our combined wisdom and strength, we’ll surely overcome any challenge that awaits us. And perhaps, through our actions, we can avert the Great Judgement and guide humanity towards a lasting era of peace and prosperity.

1. Pokémon Ascent: Featuring Tsabarite as the cover Pokémon.

Pokémon Ascent and Descent: Main Storyline

Act 1: Beginning the Journey

The adventure begins in Sunreach Port, a picturesque gateway town nestled in the tropical north of the Glaciwild Region. The protagonist, a young aspiring Pokémon Trainer, has just moved to the region with their family. Word quickly spreads about the ambitious newcomer, and a letter arrives at their doorstep, inviting them to meet with the esteemed Professor Maple at the local Pokémon Lab.

Upon reaching the lab, the protagonist is introduced to their friendly (and slightly competitive) hometown rival. Professor Maple then presents them both with their first Pokémon to choose from and their mission: To traverse the vast and varied expanses of the Glaciwild Region, learning from the people and Pokémon they meet as they challenge the region’s Gym Leaders.

Along the journey, the protagonist encounters and becomes friends with the members of an around-the-world exploration team seeking to uncover the mysterious Twilight Zone’s truth that lies nestled within the Antarctic ice. Intrigued by their mission, the protagonist decides to join them.

Act 2: Uncovering Ancient Secrets

With a growing party of Pokémon and allies, the protagonist journeys through the Glaciwild Region, defeating Gym Leaders and unraveling the legend of two ancient Pokémon, Tsabarite and Proklinachi, who hold the key to the world’s balance of desires.

As the protagonist reaches the Twilight Zone, they enter the Glimmering Caves and find a mysterious stone tablet, inscribed with an ancient prophecy. Realizing its connection to Tsabarite and Proklinachi, the group unravels the story of the tragic fall of both legendary Pokémon, the destruction of an advanced civilization, and the impending Great Judgement.

Act 3: Restoring Balance

With each Gym battle and discovery, the protagonist’s bond with their Pokémon grows stronger, and they finally reach Tsabarite, found deep within the ancient ice-encased ruins of Aurora Citadel. They convince the guardian that, although desires can cause harm, they can also lead to growth and betterment. With renewed purpose, Tsabarite entrusts the protagonist with its power to help heal the world’s hearts.

On the other hand, reaching Proklinachi’s resting place causes the protagonist to confront the darker side of desires. Proving to Proklinachi that they possess the courage and wisdom to harness its once-catastrophic power, the protagonist forms a bond with the Broken Wish Pokémon, giving it a new lease on life and purpose.

Act 4: Divine Showdown and Conclusion

Upon attaining the power of both Tsabarite and Proklinachi, the protagonist and their exploration team work to guide humanity’s desires to create a brighter future. Yet, a rogue cult, seeking to call forth the Great Judgement, unleashes the wrath of Giratina and threatens to shatter the delicate balance between light and darkness.

In a climactic battle, the protagonist faces off against Giratina and the cult’s leader, proving that humanity’s desires can indeed be channeled for good. With the doubts of the gods vanquished, Tsabarite and Proklinachi’s bond with the protagonist allows the sun to shine down once again upon the Glaciwild Region, lifting the shroud of cold and dark that has plagued the land for eons.

With newfound hope and inspiration, the protagonist continues their journey across the Glaciwild Region, spreading love, understanding and optimism to everyone they encounter.

In Pokémon Ascent and Descent, the protagonist’s journey demonstrates the delicate balance between the inherent light and darkness of desires, highlighting the importance of empathy, introspection, and camaraderie on the path to a brighter future for all.

Taking inspiration from philosophies of transience, impermanence, and dadaism, FLEETING seeks to challenge our traditional views of art, while encouraging a more profound reflection on the ever-changing nature of our existence. Chandoso utilizes the variability inherent in the dissolution of ink with water to illustrate dadaism’s seeking to question norms, embrace spontaneity, chaos and creation of works to emphasize the irrational and unpredictable nature of life, while also applying the philosophical implications that come with the concept of ‘being vs. becoming’. In the context of the works, the initial linework may be seen as a representation of ‘being’, a clearly defined image or identity, but as the water interacts with the ink, it introduces the element of ‘becoming’, dissolving the static image and allowing it to change into new forms. Through this lens, the works serve as a metaphor for our own lives, where the ‘being’ aspect represents our fixed identities and beliefs, while the ‘becoming’ aspect symbolizes the fluid, ever-evolving nature of our existence, prompting us to reassess our attachment to permanence, or seemingly static concepts in the world around us, reflecting on the fluidity of the human experience and remind us that we too are in a constant state of evolution.

Adolescence:
As individuals transition from childhood to adulthood, they must confront the ever-evolving landscape of adolescence, experiencing a period marked by not only growth, but change and exploration. The unpredictability and fluidity of the ink and water mirror the constant state of ‘becoming’ that characterizes an adolescent individual’s self-discovery, redefining their identities and finding their footing in the world.
Stop:
With the organic, ephemeral quality of the ink water technique, this piece serves as a reminder to pause and appreciate the subtleties and variety present even within a single moment, as, with each brushstroke and drip of ink being unique and impermanent, so too are the transitory details of our surroundings. ‘Stop’ encourages the viewer to step back from the commotion of their daily life to find profundity in the minutiae, and celebrate the transient beauty all around us.
Fame:
As fame often appears to be an enduring, stable status, much like the initial linework of the piece, the water’s dissolution of the ink signifies its proneness to unpredictable fluctuations and eventual fading. The art is meant to symbolize the fleeting nature of fame, reminding us of both its impermanence, but also perhaps insignificance, in the grand scheme of life.
Waves:
Waves might be the perfect embodiment of the transient, ever-changing quality of the ink water technique, as no two waves are identical, allowing their ebb and flow parallel the dynamic, ephemeral nature of the medium. As each wave breaks and recedes, replaced by yet another unique formation of variable, the piece serves as a visual metaphor for the constant state of flux inherent to the universe, as well as the transformative nature of the art itself.
Headlines:
With each week, new storylines emerge, capturing the public’s attention, only to be replaced by a different set of headlines within a matter of days, this constant flow of transient information can mirror the organic, unpredictable patterns created with the water’s interaction with the ink, underscoring the notion that permanence is rare, attentions short and importance constantly changing.
The Comments:
With its emphasis on impermanence and fluidity, the ink water technique also serves as a potential commentary on the shifting nature of internet opinions, trends and, more notably, bullying- whether individually or in a ‘dogpiling’ sense. Just as the water, in its dissolving of the ink, causes it to change and fade, the immediate and seemingly permanent comments and actions of online trolls or communities can be potentially erased or minimized over time, with individuals and groups learning from these experiences and working towards a more inclusive, empathetic digital space.

(Acknowledgements:

First and foremost, I would like to express my deepest gratitude to my Political Science teacher, Mrs. Saswati Mukherjee, who introduced me to the intriguing and enlightening topic of fundamental rights and their pivotal role in democratic societies. Her kind, cheerful, and enthusiastic demeanor has provided inspiration and motivation throughout this project. My sincere thanks also go to my Class Teacher, Miss Seemita Bhattacharya, for her unwavering support and encouragement throughout the course of my research. Her expert advice and invaluable feedback have been instrumental in sharpening my analytical capabilities and honing my writing skills to communicate effectively on this topic.

I am extremely grateful to our Principal, Mr. Charles Joseph Nyss, for fostering an academic environment that not only nurtures intellectual growth but also emphasizes the importance of developing empathy, compassion, and responsibility towards our society and the larger world. His leadership and vision have laid the foundation for an educational experience that promotes critical thinking, social awareness, and a commitment to uphold justice and equality.

I would also like to extend my heartfelt appreciation to my family and friends for their continuous support, encouragement, and belief in my abilities throughout this journey. Their unwavering faith in me has fueled my passion for learning and growing as a student and an individual.

Last but not least, I wish to acknowledge the countless individuals who have fought, and continue to fight, for the protection and advancement of fundamental rights across the globe. Their courage and determination in promoting and defending democratic values serve as an inspiration and a reminder of our collective responsibility to carry the torch of justice, equality, and dignity for all. 











Introduction:
Advancement of fundamental rights has been a significant constituent of several democratic movements throughout history, leaving its mark on modern democratic societies that we witness today. The protection and promotion of civil liberties and socio-economic entitlements not only lead to the nurturing of vibrant and robust democracies but also contribute to socio-political stability. By ensuring equitable access to opportunities and resources, as well as safeguarding the rights and freedoms of its diverse citizenry, a nation can pave the way for enhanced stability, cohesion, and progress. This project aims to explore the extent to which the advancement of fundamental rights positively impacts the overall democratization and socio-political stability within a nation. It does so through an in-depth analysis of the topic, two case studies portraying the influence of fundamental rights on democracies, and an analysis of a film relevant to this issue.
In this project, we delve into the intricacies of fundamental rights, focusing on their implications for democratic societies, and their ability to enhance social cohesion and deter socio-political unrest. By underscoring the importance of accessible and inclusive channels for political engagement, we seek to provide a holistic understanding of the vital role of fundamental rights in shaping resilient and progressive nations. Through a historical lens and cultural analysis, this research aspires to not only broaden the knowledge base in this field but also underscore the significance of upholding and advancing fundamental rights for the continued nurturing and maintenance of democratic societies.

Main Essay:
The comprehensive strengthening of fundamental rights can be understood as the foundation upon which democratic societies and institutions thrive. These rights encompass various aspects such as freedom of speech, religion, association, and movement, as well as economic, social, and cultural rights that ensure citizens have access to education, healthcare, housing, and other essential services. Through these provisions, citizens are empowered and enabled to participate in the political process, leading to stronger public awareness and engagement. Moreover, the protection of fundamental rights fosters social cohesion and tolerance, as diverse perspectives and voices are acknowledged and respected.

Conversely, the erosion of fundamental rights can prove to be detrimental not only to the democratic fabric of the nation but also its socio-political stability. Instances of widespread human rights violations, discrimination, and an overall failure to recognize and uphold citizens’ basic entitlements can lead to disenchantment, unrest, and upheaval. 
Recognition of the interdependence and indivisibility of fundamental rights is vital for nurturing inclusive and prosperous democratic societies. The concept of civil-political rights and socio-economic rights as mutually reinforcing cannot be understated, as both sets of rights are crucial in ensuring citizens’ meaningful participation in governance and social life. Civil and political rights, such as freedom of speech, expression, and assembly, allow for an exchange of opinions, scrutiny of political policies, and the ability to voice dissent—which are critical for a functioning democracy. Similarly, socio-economic rights such as the right to education, health, and social security ensure that people have the necessary tools and opportunities to engage in political and social life, thereby enabling an inclusive and participatory democratic society.

The rule of law and the existence of independent judiciary also play a crucial part in the protection and promotion of fundamental rights. The judiciary’s role in upholding the constitution and safeguarding citizens’ rights against arbitrary actions by the state and other actors is crucial for maintaining a just and egalitarian society. Furthermore, the establishment of specialized human rights institutions, such as ombudsmen and national human rights commissions, can aid in promoting awareness, monitoring adherence, and addressing violations of fundamental rights in a timely and efficient manner.

Another significant aspect to consider is the role of civil society, media, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in advancing fundamental rights and democratic values within a nation. These entities can act as watchdogs and mobilizers, raising public awareness and providing platforms for debate and advocacy. By pushing for necessary reforms and holding the state accountable, they play an invaluable role in strengthening fundamental rights and deepening democracy.

Education and public awareness campaigns also hold immense potential in disseminating information on fundamental rights, nurturing a democratic culture, and fostering a sense of social responsibility among citizens. By equipping individuals with knowledge and understanding of their rights and freedoms, as well as the functioning of democratic institutions, societies can cultivate active, informed, and responsible citizens who are essential for the sustenance and furtherance of democracies.

The international community’s role in promoting and protecting fundamental rights cannot be overlooked. Actions taken by global and regional actors, such as diplomatic pressure, imposition of sanctions, offering aid and technical assistance, or monitoring and reporting on human rights situations, can influence the improvement and safeguarding of fundamental rights in various nations.

Lastly, it is crucial to acknowledge the diversity and context-specific nature of democratic societies, as one-size-fits-all approaches often fail to acknowledge unique historical, cultural, and social circumstances. In each country, fundamental rights must be tailored and implemented with respect to the local realities to achieve their objective of enhancing democratization and socio-political stability.
In addition to the components discussed earlier, it is vital to consider the role of inclusivity and the protection of minority rights in the context of fundamental rights and democratization. The recognition and promotion of diversity, ranging from ethnicity, religion, gender, and beyond, should be integrated into the fabric of democratic societies. By doing so, underrepresented and vulnerable groups are better positioned to participate in political processes and enjoy the benefits of socio-economic rights, which in turn contribute to a healthy, stable, and thriving democracy.

Social dialogue, mediation, and conflict resolution mechanisms, founded on the principles of mutual understanding and compromise, are indispensable for maintaining socio-political stability in a democratic nation. Strong fundamental rights frameworks often encompass mechanisms that enable peaceful resolution of disputes and disagreements in both public and private spheres. By addressing grievances in a timely and fair manner, the risk of escalation and potential threats to stability and cohesion are mitigated.

Economic policies, in conjunction with fundamental rights, must be geared towards reducing income inequality, alleviating poverty, and promoting social justice. Ensuring equal access to quality education, healthcare, and employment opportunities is a crucial aspect of addressing socio-economic disparities. An effective social safety net can also contribute to stability by providing economic security to vulnerable groups and facilitating their meaningful participation in the political processes.

Good governance, transparency, and accountability are critical in the successful implementation and advancement of fundamental rights. By fostering an open system of governance that allows for public scrutiny and encourages civic engagement, societies can build trust between citizens and institutions and provide the necessary checks and balances for safeguarding rights. Access to information, public participation in decision-making, and effective monitoring and evaluation mechanisms are essential components of this process and help maintain and strengthen the democratic fabric.

Gender equality and women’s rights are also central to the realization of fundamental rights, and their inclusion in all aspects of public and private life is paramount. Promoting women’s full and equal participation in decision-making, both at the national and local levels, strengthens the democratic system and ensures that diverse perspectives and issues are represented and addressed.

Finally, the advancement of environmental rights and sustainable development is critical for ensuring the well-being of both present and future generations and preserving the planet’s resources for the future. By recognizing access to a clean and healthy environment as a fundamental right and integrating sustainable development into economic and social policies, nations can contribute to mitigating the devastating effects of climate change and preserving our planet while at the same time safeguarding citizens’ rights.

Case Study 1 - South Africa:
One striking example of the positive impact of fundamental rights on democratization and socio-political stability is the case of South Africa. Apartheid, a system of racial segregation and discrimination, had plagued the country until the early 1990s. The transition to democracy was marked by the adoption of a new constitution that enshrined an extensive range of fundamental rights, including socio-economic rights. The establishment of the South African Human Rights Commission and the Constitutional Court further strengthened the protection of these rights. As a result, South Africa has emerged as a stable and thriving democracy, showcasing the instrumental role that fundamental rights play in transforming a nation. The nation’s commitment to addressing past injustices through the establishment of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and the implementation of policies such as affirmative action and black economic empowerment also play a vital role in promoting fundamental rights. These measures aim to rectify the socio-economic imbalances that arose from apartheid and foster social cohesion, healing, and unity. The South African experience demonstrates that embracing fundamental rights has not only created a more equitable society but also fostered a more stable and resilient democracy, capable of confronting and addressing past injustices and contemporary challenges.

Case Study 2 - India:
India is an example of a country where the extensive recognition of fundamental rights was integral to the establishment of a democratic society. The Indian constitution, adopted in 1950, enshrines a myriad of fundamental rights, including civil liberties and socio-economic entitlements, accessible to every citizen. India’s diverse and multicultural nature is protected and strengthened through these rights, ensuring that minority groups have a voice in governance, thereby fostering inclusion and stability.  The Indian judiciary also plays an instrumental role in protecting and advancing fundamental rights by interpreting the constitution in a manner that promotes social justice and inclusivity. Landmark decisions such as the Right to Education Act and the decriminalization of homosexuality showcase the judiciary’s commitment to upholding the rights and freedoms enshrined in the constitution. Furthermore, the active participation of civil society, media, and non-governmental organizations in raising awareness, advocating for reforms, and holding the government accountable has contributed to the continuous strengthening of fundamental rights and the democratic fabric of India. Despite the challenges and complexities faced by the world’s largest democracy, India’s continued focus on adapting and evolving its fundamental rights framework has been crucial in ensuring its socio-political stability and progress.

Film Analysis - “To Kill a Mockingbird”:
The 1962 film “To Kill a Mockingbird,” adapted from Harper Lee’s novel of the same name, serves as a powerful reflection of the significance of fundamental rights in upholding justice and fairness within a society. Set in the racially segregated South in the 1930s, the film portrays the challenge of protecting the rights of African Americans in a community rife with prejudice and discrimination. The protagonist, Atticus Finch, is a lawyer tasked with defending a black man accused of raping a white woman. Finch’s unwavering commitment to uphold the rights of his client, in the face of overwhelming adversity, showcases the importance of fundamental rights in promoting justice, equality, and social harmony. The film also explores themes of empathy, moral growth, and the importance of standing up for what is right, even in the face of adversity. Through the powerful portrayal of these themes, the film emphasizes the significance of advocating for fundamental rights as a force of good in the world. By examining the societal divisions and injustices in a historical context, “To Kill a Mockingbird” invites reflection on the pressing need to advance and protect fundamental rights for the betterment of contemporary societies, and the ongoing fight to ensure that justice, equality, and dignity are upheld for all.

Conclusion:
The hypothesis, that the comprehensive strengthening of fundamental rights is inherently conducive to fostering a more vibrant and robust democratic society, stands true based on the analysis and case studies presented. By ensuring equitable access to opportunities and resources, and safeguarding the rights and freedoms of its diverse citizenry, a nation can pave the way for enhanced stability, cohesion, and progress. As evident in the case studies of South Africa and India, and the film “To Kill a Mockingbird,” the promotion and protection of fundamental rights play a crucial role in fostering inclusive and participatory governance, which bolsters the nation’s resilience against potential socio-political unrest and fosters a harmonious, dynamic, and forward-looking society.  It is essential for nations to recognize and actively work towards the realization of fundamental rights, as they serve as the bedrock upon which thriving democracies are built. Collective efforts from all aspects of society— including governments, civil society, media, and citizens— play a critical role in preserving and promoting these rights. By committing to the continuous protection and advancement of fundamental rights, societies can effectively foster social harmony, inclusivity, and resilience, laying the foundation for a sustainable and vibrant democratic future.) Remote tribes are one example, although increasingly climate change is eliminating these traditional ways of life everywhere. Some of the poor in other countries, and even (in rare cases) in America also benefit from the high-calorie low-cost density of canned mass-production meat. Sometimes meat is the cheapest thing you can buy (although this is almost wholly a product of cultures that massively subsidize meat production[2]). Literature Review

1 Introduction
Agile as a methodology began as a discussion at a ski resort in Utah, wherein seventeen IS (information systems) professionals came together to evaluate the state of product development in the software industry. Collectively, they produced the Agile Manifesto (Beck et al., 2001), a list of twelve principles that outlined their thoughts on how product development should be conducted. This list was succinct in its wording, and broad in scope leading many to see the application of this new approach to their own projects. Unfortunately, the breadth and lack of specificity also meant the manifesto is open to interpretation, leading to somewhat of a dilution of the meaning of “agile” (Kuhrmann et al., 2022). This can even be seen among the authors of the Agile Manifesto who have published several similar, yet distinct means to handle agile style development. (Beck, 2000; Cockburn, 2004; Schwaber and Beedle, 2002). This study will seek to distil what agile means to the modern developer by reviewing where the methodology came from, how agile methodologies differ, and how agile is implemented in the modern development cycle using industry examples.
2 Agile as a framework
Agile at its origin follows twelve principles, as given by the Agile Manifesto (Beck et al., 2001):
1.	Continuous delivery of valuable software.
2.	Accept change at any point in development.
3.	Deliver frequently.
4.	Businesspeople and developers’ work should be integrated.
5.	Management should trust developers to produce work.
6.	Discussions should be face-to-face.
7.	Progress is gauged through volume of working code.
8.	Development should be sustainable.
9.	Technical excellence and good design should be upheld.
10.	Focus on simplicity.
11.	Teams should be self-organized.
12.	Evaluations should be regular, and properly adhered to.
These points outline what agile is and should be reference point for any conversation on agile. It is worth noting that at no point in this manifesto do the authors outline a structure for how agile should be conducted. As such, it can be raised that there is no true agile methodology, but rather a framework wherein methodologies that are agile in nature can be developed to suit the needs of the project. This leads on to the following section wherein such methodologies (hence to be called Agile methodologies), will be explored in terms of their adherence to the ideals of the manifesto, to compare what is labelled as agile against what it was designed to be.
3 Investigation of methodologies
There are several methodologies seen to be agile in the modern Information Systems world. Extreme Programming (XP)(Beck, 2000), Crystal (Cockburn, 2004), Scrum (Schwaber and Beedle, 2002; Takeuchi and Nonaka, 1986), Feature-driven development (Palmer and Felsing, 2002), and Lean (Cook and Semouchtchak, 2004). These five methodologies are some of the most common approaches seen to be agile. As each methodology is described, they will be evaluated for their successes and failures, both in terms of their adherence to agile ideals, and their structural soundness.
3.1 Extreme Programming (XP)
Extreme programming (also written as eXtreme Programming or just XP), is a methodology produced by one of the authors of The Agile Manifesto Kent Beck. The structure of the methodology involves evaluating the most important features of a project, and cycling through a process of planning, discussion and development (Wells, 2009). Pair programming is encouraged to promote technical excellence and face-to-face discussion. Furthermore, the methodology encourages listening to feedback and having “courage” in face of criticism, to boost the acceptance of change in a project. Systematic review of this methodology by Shrivastava et al. (2021) found that Extreme Programming methodologies resulted in software with a “low fault rate” as problems encountered while developing were viewed as “a medium to acquire skills,” rather than failings. This likely contributed to the motivation observed by Shrivastava and their team.
3.2 Crystal development
Crystal development, much like agile, is less of a methodology on how to handle the individual steps in a project, but a framework for small size teams to rationalise how to organise and being to structure their own workspace. Cockburn (2004) recommends a process called “methodology shaping, wherein a project manager evaluates the experiences of the team members and collates a system that suits the strengths of the team afforded from their experience. For example, if a team has a more individualistic traits, the manager might suggest that more intensive documentation is necessary, such that information can pass easily between individuals who perhaps do not work well in programming situations. Given the nature of this design, wherein structure is inherently undefined and malleable, the study of Crystal style development as a methodology is complex, and underexplored. However, research by Tripp, Rienemschneider and Thatcher (2016) demonstrates that the higher the degree of agility, that is flexibility in a given project, the higher the degree of job satisfaction. Given that this system brings the concept of self-organising teams to the forefront of consideration during early project design stages, it’s clear to see why this style would be popular among developers. Mangers, and new developers to the team, may find this structure unwelcoming however, as the lack of focus on documentation, and freedom to the team could lead to disorganization. 
3.3 Scrum
Scrum is a four-stage agile methodology that’s designed to follow a cyclical flow, akin to the flow of game states in Rugby (Takeuchi and Nonaka, 1986; Schwaber and Beedle, 2002). After the initial creation of the project, the four step cycle is:
-	Planning
-	Development
-	Review
-	Retrospective
The review, retrospective and planning stages, take place during a daily “scrum” which is a standing meeting wherein team members come together to discuss the progress of the project and seek help on issues they may have encountered the previous day. This structure builds a strong understanding of how the team is progressing, as each member is fully aware of how each workday will be laid out, and they hear how production in other areas is progressing.
3.4 Feature-Driven development
Feature-Driven development (FDD) is a heavier methodology compared to the others discussed in this review, as it recommends a higher degree of documentation. Palmer and Felsing (2002) suggest that a team should outline the project scope accurately at the inception of the project to decrease the impact of common agile problems like scope creep as explored by Aizaz et al. (2021), who describe scope creep as being a key element in the downfall of many development projects. This methodology focuses then on building the outlines features one at a time, until the project is fulfilled. This goal oriented philosophy lends itself to complex projects with interlocking features, and helps reduce confusion as the project expands through development.
Modern Agile Overview
In the current realm of software development, intense globalisation and competition has been driving for high-output development whereby new features can be quickly applied in order to keep a product relevant in a world governed by dopamine (Macit, Macit and Güngör, 2018), with examples in social media development, app development, and games development. Following games development, we can see how agile methodologies reflect the current cycle of consumerism. Fortnite and Overwatch 2 are key examples of iterative design cycles, where existing models are now recursively updated to add new content before previous elements have time to grow stale for users (Keighley, 2018). This method is highly energy consuming, however, and maintaining focus on a growing and evolving cycle, can be to the detriment of other projects as shown by Blizzard cancelling Overwatch 2’s “player versus environment” style gameplay as it took too much away from the main game to make production worthwhile (Blizzard Entertainment, 2023), which shows how agile methodologies are effective, but can require a high level of focus to continue to be sustainable.

Limitations
This review evaluates many processes from an agile perspective, but it powerfully important to note that the agile perspective, while currently viewed as the most effective framework for software development, there may be other frameworks that provide a more effective style for software development. Hence, structures or behaviours criticised in this review may be beneficial in another situation or style.
Conclusion
Agile as shown in its initial conception, is a set of ideals, and not truly a methodology. Methodologies that spawned from this set of ideals, and practices within these methodologies can all be agile provided that they follow the concept outlined by the Agile Alliance in that ski resort in Utah. Furthermore, this review has shown that adherence to a given methodology can be to the detriment of other elements in a project or company. Kuhrmann et al. (2022) concluded that agile has a wide range of definitions in a modern context, and it is the conclusion that of this review that truly agile development should not follow one methodology, but meet the needs of the project as a whole, both pre-emptively, and as new issues arise throughout the project.
 
Business Survey 

This section of the report is dedicated to the design and use of a survey to investigate the use of agile methodologies in local business. Participants in the study were found using linkedin, and were asked if they would be willing to participate in a study for a class project. Thirty-one individuals were asked to participate, twenty-one of whom were happy to participate, and 10 of whom did not reply to correspondence.

The questions asked we as follows:

1.	What is your job title?
2.	What Information Systems area do you work in?
3.	What does your job involve?
4.	To your knowledge, is agile a part of your daily work? (Yes or No answer)
o	If not, do you think your workplace would benefit from following agile methodologies?
o	If yes, what agile methodology do you use and how does it help your work?
5.	Would you describe the projects your work on as flexible to change? (YES or NO answer)
6.	How often do you meet with a representative of the customer for your project?
7.	How often do you reflect on team efficacy?
8.	How do you evaluate progress in the projects you develop?
9.	Do you have stand up meetings, and how often do you have them?
10.	Do you like stand-up meetings?
These questions were designed to discover how likely certain jobs were to use an agile work style, to evaluate if they enjoyed the process, and weather or not they felt it helped the to work process. 
Data Analysis
Frequency of Type
Figure one and Figure Two shows the frequency of types of programmers who responded to the study. As software developers, and software engineers are the highest rate of responders.

It’s possible they were using a Crystal style of agile whereby a system is designed explicitly for a project.
Regardless, here we can see Scrum and Kanban are the most popular agile methodologies responders found that these methodologies gave them a great deal of focus, and team spirit.

Stand-up meetings

Cổng giao thương (Business Gate - loại = 1): người gác cổng là một tên lái buôn, để qua cổng, Hoàng tử phải mua hàng của tên lái buôn với số tiền = đơn giá * số hàng.
Cổng học thuật (Academic Gate - loại = 2): người gác cổng là một nhà hiền triết, để qua cổng. Hoàng tử phải trả lời được câu hỏi của nhà hiền triết. Câu hỏi có một chỉ số trí tuệ, Hoàng tử cần có chỉ số trí tuệ cao hơn hoặc bằng để trả lời được câu hỏi. Lưu ý: sau khi trả lời câu hỏi, chỉ số trí tuệ của hoàng tử không bị mất đi.
Cổng sức mạnh (Power Gate - loại = 3): người gác cổng là một dũng sỹ, để qua cổng, Hoàng tử phải đánh thắng được dũng sỹ. Sau khi chiến thắng, chỉ số sức mạnh của hoàng tử bị hao mòn đi đúng bằng chỉ số sức mạnh của dũng sỹ.

Procedures Under the Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding
Concerning Consultation and Cooperation and the Exchange of Information
I. Application to Become a Signatory to the MOU
(a) All governmental regulatory bodies that are Ordinary or Associate Members of IOSCO
are eligible to apply to participate in the MOU at any time. Applications should be
submitted to the IOSCO Secretary General.
(b) All applicants must provide a complete response to the questionnaire, which is included
in Part IV of this Appendix B, and provide copies of their supporting laws, rules and
regulations as indicated in the questionnaire. Responses should identify and explain the
applicant’s legal authority to meet the specific MOU provisions cited in the
questionnaire, which are essential to mutual assistance and the exchange of information
in order to successfully enforce securities and derivatives laws.
(c) Responses to the questionnaire will be verified by the Screening Group with
administrative support provided by the Secretary General. The screening group will
establish verification teams that include members with substantial expertise in
enforcement of securities and derivatives laws, as well as expertise in cross border
information sharing. The screening group has discretion to invite other IOSCO
members to participate in the verification teams.
(d) The verification of the questionnaire responses will be limited to verification that the
responses accurately reflect the legal authority of members to comply with the specific
MOU provisions cited in the questionnaire based on the laws, rules and regulations
cited in the responses. Based on their review of the questionnaire responses, the
verification teams will make specific recommendations to the screening group
concerning the ability of the applicant to comply with each MOU provision cited in the
questionnaire.
(e) The screening group will make recommendations concerning its verification of
applicant responses to a decision making group. Prior to making any negative
recommendation on an application, the screening group will notify the applicant in
writing, identifying the specific MOU provisions for which the applicant lacks legal
authority. The applicant will have an opportunity, upon request, to be heard by the
screening group.
(f) The decision-making group will be comprised of the Chairmen of the IOSCO Board,
the Emerging Markets Committee, and the Monitoring Group (“Committee of
Chairmen”). Together, this decision-making group, after consultation with the
Chairman of the relevant Regional Committee, will decide whether to accept or reject
applications to become an MOU signatory based on the screening group’s
recommendations. Prior to making any negative decision, the decision making group
will notify the applicant in writing, identifying the specific MOU provisions for which
the applicant lacks legal authority. The applicant will have an opportunity, upon
request, to be heard by the decision-making group.

Traduction en français : Inattention, motor instability, and impulsivity, associated in varying degrees of severity depending on the clinical subtype, constitute the key symptoms of attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). However, emotional symptoms are frequent in patients with ADHD and may, in some cases, be responsible for a major part of the negative impact on functioning and outcome. Emotional problems have been described in ADHD even in the absence of characterized comorbid conditions such as depressive or anxiety disorders. They can manifest acutely in the form of severe tantrums and aggressive behaviour, generally in reaction to an environmental trigger, or show a more chronic course of irritable or labile mood. Symptoms of emotional undercontrol seem to occur more frequently when ADHD is associated with oppositional defiant behaviour, but they are not specific and may contribute to difficulties in making a differential diagnosis, especially with bipolar disorder and prodromal symptoms of personality disorders. The frequency and negative impact of emotional symptoms and the need to differentiate them from bipolar disorder has led some authors to the description of a novel clinical entity called "severe mood dysregulation" or "temper dysregulation with dysphoria." This article aims to review the recent literature on emotional symptoms associated with ADHD and to discuss relevant clinical and biological issues. Current research highlights the links between emotional self-regulation and executive functions and possible involvement of motivational systems. The role of environmental factors in the development of emotional regulation and self-control is another important issue, especially because environmental modification is the major focus of current preventive and therapeutic interventions.

сократи текст: Исторические предпосылки. Литература зарождается лишь в условиях развития классового общества. Необходимыми предпосылками ее возникновения являются образование государства, появление письменности, существование высокоразвитых форм устного народного творчества.
Возникновение древнерусской литературы неразрывно связано с процессом создания раннефеодального государства. Советская историческая наука опровергла норманнскую теорию происхождения древнерусского государства, доказав, что оно возникло не в результате призвания варягов, а в результате длительного исторического процесса разложения родового общинного строя восточнославянских племен. Характерная особенность этого исторического процесса в том, что восточнославянские племена приходят к феодализму, минуя стадию рабовладельческой формации.
Новая система общественных отношений, основанная на классовом господстве меньшинства над большинством трудового населения, нуждалась в идеологическом обосновании. Этого обоснования не могли дать ни племенная языческая религия, ни устное народное творчество, обслуживавшее ранее идеологически и художественно базис родового строя.
Развитие экономических, торговых и политических связей вызывало потребность в письменности, существование которой является одной из необходимейших предпосылок появления литературы.
Данные советской лингвистической и исторической науки свидетельствуют о том, что письменность на Руси появилась задолго до официального принятия христианства. О существовании каких-то форм письменности у славян уже во второй половине IX в. свидетельствуют черноризец Храбр и «Паннонское житие Кирилла».
Создание славянской азбуки Кириллом и Мефодием в 863 г. явилось актом величайшего культурно-исторического значения, способствовавшим быстрому культурному росту как южных, так и восточных славян. К концу IX – первой четверти X столетия древняя Болгария переживает замечательный период расцвета своей культуры. В этот период здесь появляются выдающиеся писатели: Иоанн экзарх болгарский, Климент, Константин и сам царь Симеон. Созданные ими произведения сыграли важную роль в развитии древнерусской культуры. Близость древнерусского языка древнеславянскому («...славянский язык и русский един», – подчеркивал летописец) способствовала постепенному усвоению новой письменности восточными славянами.
Мощный толчок широкому распространению и развитию письменности на Руси дало официальное принятие христианства в 988 г., которое помогло закрепить идеологически новые общественные отношения складывающегося феодального общества.
Для развития самобытной древнерусской культуры немаловажное значение имело то обстоятельство, что Русь приняла христианство из Византии, являвшейся в то время носителем самой высокой культуры. Византийская православная церковь, уже фактически к тому времени обособившаяся от западной римской католической (формальное разделение церквей произошло в 1054 г.), давала гораздо больший простор формированию национальных особенностей культуры. Если католическая церковь выдвинула в качестве литературного языка латинский, то греческая православная церковь допускала свободное развитие национальных литературных языков. Литературным церковным языком Древней Руси стал язык древнеславянский, близкий по своему характеру, грамматическому строю языку древнерусскому. Возникшая оригинальная литература способствовала развитию этого языка, обогащая его за счет разговорной устной народной речи.
С конца X в. можно говорить о появлении определенной системы образования на Руси – «книжного учения».
Христианство сыграло прогрессивную роль в становлении культуры Древней Руси. Киевская Русь выдвигается в число передовых государств Европы. В конце X – начале XI в., как свидетельствует Адам Бременский, Киев по своему богатству, населенности соперничает с Константинополем.
В 30 – 40-е годы XI столетия в Киеве уже много искусных переводчиков, которые «перелагают» книги непосредственно с греческого языка на «словенский». Сын Ярослава Всеволод владеет пятью иностранными языками, его сестра Анна, став французской королевой, оставляет собственноручную подпись – «Анна регина», в то время как ее царственный супруг вместо подписи ставит крестик.
В развитии книжной образованности, в том числе и литературы, большую роль играли монастыри, являвшиеся в первые годы своего существования очагом новой христианской культуры. Особенно велика была в этом отношении роль Киево-Печерского монастыря, созданного в середине XI столетия.
Итак, образование раннефеодального древнерусского государства и возникновение письменности явились необходимыми предпосылками появления литературы.
Основные источники. В формировании литературы активно участвуют, с одной стороны, устное народное поэтическое творчество, и с другой – книжная христианская культура, идущая как от южных славян, в частности болгар, так и от Византии.
Начавшееся сравнительно недавно историческое изучение фольклора показывает, что у восточных славян к X в. существовали высокоразвитые формы устного народного творчества. Исследователи полагают, что в это время в фольклоре происходит переход от мифологических сюжетов к историческим. Историческое родовое предание, топонимическая легенда, предание, связанное с могильниками, героическое сказание, песни о военных походах занимают ведущее место в устной поэзии той поры.
К этому периоду относится, по-видимому, формирование народного эпоса, сыгравшего исключительно важную роль в становлении оригинальной древнерусской литературы.
Княжеские дружины, совершавшие многочисленные военные походы, очевидно, имели своих певцов, которые увеселяли их во время пиров, слагая песни-«славы» в честь победителей, прославляя князя и его храбрых воинов. Героические песни дружинных певцов, эпические сказания о битвах, походах составляли своеобразную устную летопись, которая затем частично была закреплена письменностью.
Таким образом, фольклор был основным источником, который давал образы, сюжеты формирующейся оригинальной древнерусской литературе. Через фольклор в нее проникали не только художественная образность народной поэзии, отдельные элементы стиля, но и народная идеология.
Усваивая христианскую идеологию, народ приспосабливал ее к своим языческим понятиям и представлениям. Это и породило такую весьма характерную особенность русской жизни, как «двоеверие», которое длительное время удерживалось в народном сознании, что получило отражение и в древнерусской литературе. На протяжении всей истории развития литературы устная народная поэзия была тем живительным источником, который содействовал ее обогащению.
Важную роль в формировании литературы сыграли также искусство устной речи и деловая письменность. Устные речи были широко распространены в жизненной практике раннефеодального общества, военачальники перед началом сражений обращались к своим воинам с речью, подавая им «дерзость», воодушевляя на ратный подвиг. Устная речь постоянно использовалась в дипломатических переговорах: отправлявшиеся выполнять свою дипломатическую миссию послы обычно заучивали наизусть слова, которые им приказывал передать тот или иной правитель. Эти речи содержали определенные устойчивые словосочетания, они отличались сжатостью, выразительностью.
Словесные формулы вырабатывала также и деловая письменность. Лаконизм и точность выражений устной речи и деловой письменности способствовали развитию сжатого, афористического стиля изложения в литературных памятниках.
Не могла не оказать большого влияния на формирующуюся оригинальную древнерусскую письменность и усваиваемая русскими книжниками христианская книжная культура

SIR ISAAC NEWTON.
Sir Isaac Newton (1642-1727) was an English scientist
who made great contributions to physics, optics, maths
and astronomy. He is known for his Three Laws of Motion
and the Universal Law of Gravitation.
When Sir Isaac Newton was a boy, he was more
interested in making mechanical devices than in studying.
He made a windmill which could grind wheat and corn,
and he made a water clock and a sundial. His teachers
thought he was not a very intelligent student because he didn’t do very well.
He wanted to go to college, but he didn’t have the money to go, so at university,
he had to serve the other students by doing chores for them. He even ate the
leftovers of their meals, but he would do anything to get an opportunity to learn.
Even when he was in college, he was not outstanding and received no awards.
When the university shut down because of the plague, an illness where people
caught diseases and died suddenly, he went home and continued to study on
his own.
He had a notebook with blank pages and he began to fill them with notes as he
read and experimented about different things around him.
One day, when he was drinking tea in the garden, he saw an apple fall to the
ground. He started thinking about why it fell. Why did the apple fall out of the
tree? Does everything fall? What makes things fall? Can anything stop things
from falling? Are the sun, moon and stars falling? Why don’t they ever fall to the
ground? He finally decided that a force called gravity, which cased the apple to
fall also kept the moon in the sky around the Earth. This same force called
gravity, also kept the planets in the sky around the sun.
The apple incident led to his three basic laws of motion:
 A moving object keeps moving unless an outside force stops it.
 An object moves in a straight line unless some force makes it change
direction
 For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
Isaac Newton is well known as one of the greatest scientists who ever lived.
